status_note: Launched in 2025 and active as a salt-marsh restoration, research and voluntary-finance programme under development.

document_title: Massachusetts Blue Carbon Calculator
notes: The calculator provides a simple methodology for estimating the greenhouse-gas budget of aquatic ecosystem restoration projects, with particular emphasis on coastal wetlands and restored salt marshes. Users enter expected land-cover changes and the tool estimates carbon dioxide and methane outcomes using published emission factors, including factors derived from the IPCC Wetlands Supplement. It is a planning estimator and does not provide site-specific verification, certify removals, issue credits or replace project-level monitoring.
source: Massachusetts Division of Ecological Restoration
status_note: Made publicly available in 2015 and retained as an official restoration-planning tool.

document_title: H.R. 9912 — Coastal Restoration Act of 2024
notes: The bill proposed an Interagency Working Group on Coastal Blue Carbon, a national map and inventory, NOAA pilot programmes to protect and restore coastal blue-carbon ecosystems, a Coastal Carbon Data Clearinghouse, a Coastal Blue Carbon Inventory Program and a national assessment of sequestration potential. It was introduced but not enacted before the 118th Congress ended, so none of the proposed programmes, funding mechanisms or statutory requirements took effect.
source: United States Congress
status_note: Introduced on 4 October 2024 and not enacted before the end of the 118th Congress.

document_title: H.R. 2750 — Blue Carbon for Our Planet Act
notes: The bill proposed establishing an Interagency Working Group on Coastal Blue Carbon to coordinate federal research and management, develop a national map and inventory, identify conservation and restoration priorities and address data continuity and policy barriers. It received committee consideration but was not enacted before the 117th Congress ended; it therefore created no binding working group, programme, restoration mandate or funding entitlement.
source: United States Congress
status_note: Introduced on 22 April 2021, received a committee hearing and was not enacted before the end of the 117th Congress.

document_title: H.R. 3764 — Ocean-Based Climate Solutions Act of 2022
notes: The reported bill proposed a federal Blue Carbon Program, national mapping of coastal and marine blue-carbon ecosystems, conservation and restoration grants, research coordination and related ocean-based climate measures. Although it was reported from committee and placed on the Union Calendar in December 2022, it was not enacted before the 117th Congress ended. It therefore established no binding blue-carbon programme, grant entitlement, inventory requirement or restoration authorization.
source: United States Congress
status_note: Introduced in 2021, reported to the House as the Ocean-Based Climate Solutions Act of 2022 and not enacted before the end of the 117th Congress.

document_title: Ireland’s Marine Strategy Framework Directive Marine Strategy Part 1: Assessment, Good Environmental Status and Environmental Targets
notes: Ireland's 2025 Marine Strategy Part 1 updates the national assessment of marine environmental status, Good Environmental Status definitions and environmental targets under the EU Marine Strategy Framework Directive. It incorporates climate-change and ocean-acidification impacts for the first time and identifies protection of sensitive ecosystems and enhancement of services such as blue carbon storage as areas for additional measures. The document builds an evidence and planning base; it does not quantify additional carbon removals, approve restoration projects or establish a carbon-crediting mechanism.
source: Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment, Ireland
status_note: Published on 9 July 2025 as the current Marine Strategy Part 1 assessment and target update.

document_title: Norway’s Integrated Ocean Management Plans — Meld. St. 21 (2023–2024)
notes: The white paper integrates blue forests and carbon storage into Norway's ocean-management framework, covering kelp and other macroalgae, eelgrass, salt marshes, soft-bottom habitats and marine sediments. It reports an estimated annual uptake and storage contribution for key ecosystems in mainland territorial waters and states that biodiversity and natural ecosystem functions must be safeguarded if marine ecosystems are used as carbon sinks. It also states that no decisions had been made to initiate biological carbon-storage activities such as kelp cultivation and that the evidence base remained insufficient for deployment assessment.
source: Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment
status_note: Presented to the Storting in 2024 as the updated integrated ocean-management white paper.

document_title: Act Amending the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Act and the Pollution Control Act (Expanded Geographical Scope) — Act No. 54 of 19 June 2026
notes: The 2026 amendments expand the geographical reach of Norway's Pollution Control Act and provide a clear legal basis for regulating dumping, placement of material and marine geoengineering outside Norwegian territorial waters and the exclusive economic zone in accordance with international obligations. The amendments also support implementation of rules for transporting greenhouse gases for geological storage. The law creates regulatory authority rather than approving any marine-geoengineering or storage project; individual activities remain subject to applicable permits, regulations and environmental safeguards.
source: Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment / Lovdata
status_note: Sanctioned and entered into force on 19 June 2026 as Act No. 54.

document_title: House Bill 3409 / Oregon Laws 2023, Chapter 442 — Natural and Working Lands Carbon Sequestration Framework
notes: Oregon's 2023 climate legislation establishes a Natural and Working Lands Fund and requires a statewide net biological carbon-sequestration and storage baseline, activity metrics, community-impact metrics, non-binding goals and an inventory. The statutory definitions include wetlands, coastal and estuarine areas, submerged and submersible lands within Oregon's territorial sea and associated marine habitats, and the advisory structure includes blue-carbon expertise. The law does not create an offset protocol or guarantee carbon-credit issuance from coastal projects.
source: Oregon Legislative Assembly
status_note: Signed into law on 27 July 2023 as Oregon Laws 2023, Chapter 442.

document_title: Oregon Natural and Working Lands Grant Offerings — Blue Carbon Tidal-Wetland Eligibility
notes: The 2025 Oregon Natural and Working Lands grant offering made tidal-wetland conservation and restoration eligible as a blue-carbon natural climate solution. Restoration and technical-assistance grants could support planning and implementation, with statutory priority for Tribes and environmental-justice communities. The 2025 solicitation closed on 1 April 2025 and the official page states that no future offering is currently planned; the programme did not establish an offset methodology, quantify achieved removals or issue carbon credits.
source: Oregon Watershed Enhancement Board
status_note: The 2025 solicitation opened in February, closed on 1 April 2025 and is listed with no future offering planned.

document_title: Engrossed Second Substitute House Bill 2251 — Climate Commitment Act Accounts
notes: Washington's 2026 session law revises Climate Commitment Act accounts and expressly allows clean-water and natural-climate-solution investments that increase carbon storage in oceans and aquatic or coastal ecosystems and retain or increase sequestration and storage benefits on tidally influenced and other aquatic lands. The law creates eligible public-investment purposes and safeguards but does not select individual blue-carbon projects, establish an offset protocol or certify carbon units.
source: Washington State Legislature
status_note: Passed by the Legislature in March 2026 and enacted as a 2026 Washington session law.

document_title: Washington Blue Carbon Exploratory Working Group — Offset Protocol Feasibility Process
notes: The Washington Department of Ecology is using an exploratory working group to assess whether a blue-carbon offset protocol should be developed for the state's cap-and-invest programme. The process is a feasibility and stakeholder-engagement exercise linked to possible future protocol development. As of the official 2026 programme information, Washington had not adopted a blue-carbon protocol and the working group did not authorize projects or create tradable blue-carbon offset credits.
source: Washington State Department of Ecology
status_note: Active in 2026 as an exploratory working-group process; no blue-carbon offset protocol had been adopted.

document_title: Snohomish Watershed Resilience Action Plan — Action 13 Blue Carbon Sequestration
notes: The Snohomish Watershed Resilience Action Plan directs a landscape-scale carbon-sequestration inventory and calls for implementation of blue-carbon projects involving underwater vegetation, kelp, eelgrass and tidal forests. Action 13 contributes to a broader target of implementing 10,000 acres of carbon-sequestration projects by 2026, but the official material does not state that all 10,000 acres are blue-carbon projects or report verified net removals. The plan is a restoration and planning roadmap rather than a carbon-credit standard or project permit.
source: Washington State Department of Natural Resources
status_note: Launched in 2022 as a ten-year watershed-resilience roadmap with short- and long-term blue-carbon actions.

document_title: Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 10, Section 35D1/2 — Biodiversity Fund
notes: Massachusetts law establishes a permanent Biodiversity Fund administered by the Commissioner of Fish and Game. Eligible expenditures expressly include blue-carbon strategies, habitat management, conservation and restoration, data collection, technical assistance and grants to nonprofit organizations, researchers and community-based organizations. The statute creates a financing authority but does not define a blue-carbon methodology, require a particular appropriation for blue carbon or establish carbon-credit issuance.
source: Massachusetts General Court
status_note: Created through the Fiscal Year 2025 budget enacted in 2024 and codified in Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 10.

document_title: The Place of the Oceans in Norway’s Foreign and Development Policy — Meld. St. 22 (2016–2017)
notes: Norway's ocean foreign- and development-policy white paper commits the government to strengthen participation in international knowledge processes on blue forests, expand knowledge and capacity support for tropical blue-forest action in partner countries, promote inclusion of mangroves in work on reducing emissions from deforestation and degradation, and prioritize research on kelp in the global carbon cycle. The white paper establishes international policy and research priorities but does not approve a specific restoration project, quantify removals or create a carbon-credit standard.
source: Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
status_note: Presented to the Storting in 2017 without a fixed programme end date.

document_title: A Research Strategy for Ocean-based Carbon Dioxide Removal and Sequestration
notes: This National Academies consensus study, publicly released on 8 December 2021, evaluates six broad ocean-based carbon dioxide removal approaches: nutrient fertilization; artificial upwelling and downwelling; seaweed cultivation; marine and coastal ecosystem recovery; ocean alkalinity enhancement; and electrochemical processes. It recommends a USD 125 million cross-cutting research programme over ten years for shared scientific, economic, social, governance and public-engagement questions, while also giving separate pathway-specific research-cost estimates of about USD 290 million for nutrient fertilization, USD 25 million for artificial upwelling/downwelling, USD 130 million for seaweed cultivation, USD 220 million for ecosystem recovery, USD 125–200 million for ocean alkalinity enhancement and USD 350 million for electrochemical processes. These figures are research recommendations rather than a single appropriated federal budget. The report calls for responsible research, permitting and governance work, monitoring and carbon accounting, but it does not authorize deployment, establish carbon credits or conclude that any pathway is ready for climate-scale use. National Academies bibliographic pages commonly list the volume as a 2022 publication, while the formal news release and report highlights are dated December 2021.
source: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
status_note: Consensus study publicly released 8 December 2021; National Academies bibliographic metadata also lists the volume as 2022

document_title: Ocean Fertilization: A Scientific Summary for Policy Makers
notes: This IOC-UNESCO scientific summary for policy makers synthesizes the state of knowledge on deliberate ocean fertilization, especially the addition of iron or other limiting nutrients to stimulate phytoplankton production and potentially increase export of biologically fixed carbon to deeper waters. It reviews proposed climate benefits, experimental evidence, uncertainties over sequestration efficiency and permanence, verification challenges, ecological side effects, and governance questions. The report was prepared to inform international policy discussions occurring under the London Convention/London Protocol and biodiversity processes rather than to advocate deployment. It makes clear that enhanced biological production at the surface does not automatically translate into durable, additional and verifiable atmospheric CO2 removal. The publication is a scientific assessment, not a permit, carbon-credit methodology, project approval or authorization for commercial ocean fertilization, and it does not resolve the environmental and accounting uncertainties that motivated the precautionary international policy response.
source: Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of UNESCO
status_note: Published in 2010 as IOC/BRO/2010/2 and remains an official scientific reference on ocean-fertilization assessment.

document_title: Selected Potential Considerations with Respect to Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal: In Brief
notes: This Congressional Research Service report reviews biological and chemical marine CDR pathways, potential benefits and adverse effects, federal research activity and the statutes and permits that may apply to field projects. It is designed to inform congressional oversight and policy choices. The report does not approve any project, determine that a pathway is effective at scale or establish a federal authorization or carbon-credit programme.
source: Congressional Research Service, Library of Congress
status_note: Updated on 10 March 2025 and available as an active Congressional Research Service reference.

document_title: Coastal Blue Carbon as a Carbon Dioxide Removal Approach: Selected Issues for Congress
notes: This Congressional Research Service report examines mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrass as coastal blue-carbon reservoirs, including stock and sequestration estimation, mapping, durability, restoration and the federal science and policy landscape. It identifies measurement and governance questions for Congress but does not create a restoration programme, approve projects or establish a federal offset methodology.
source: Congressional Research Service, Library of Congress
status_note: Updated on 29 April 2025 and available as an active Congressional Research Service reference.

document_title: Carbon Dioxide Removal: Purpose, Approaches, and Recommendations — Draft Report for Public Comment
notes: The Department of Energy released this congressionally directed interagency draft for public comment to assess current and emerging CDR approaches, research and deployment needs, and potential federal policies. Its scope includes ocean-based and coastal approaches alongside non-marine CDR. The document remained a draft consultation instrument on the cited page; it did not authorize marine deployment, allocate project funding or establish a final federal MRV or crediting framework.
source: United States Department of Energy
status_note: Released for public comment on 16 January 2025; the comment period closed on 1 April 2025 and the cited DOE page continues to identify the document as a draft.

document_title: Integrated Ocean Carbon Research: A Summary of Ocean Carbon Knowledge and a Vision for Coordinated Ocean Carbon Research and Observations for the Next Decade
notes: The IOC-UNESCO report synthesizes knowledge on ocean carbon uptake and storage and proposes a coordinated medium- and long-term programme of observations, modelling and research. It addresses how human activities and carbon-dioxide-removal schemes may alter the ocean carbon cycle and is intended to improve the evidence available for climate mitigation and adaptation decisions. It is a research vision rather than a deployment authorization, accounting methodology or carbon-credit standard.
source: Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of UNESCO
status_note: Published in 2021 as an international research vision supporting the UN Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development.

document_title: Integrated Ocean Carbon Research: A Vision Primed for Implementation
notes: This IOC-UNESCO assessment updates the international ocean-carbon research agenda and identifies priorities for a coordinated global observing system, improved models, capacity development and cross-disciplinary research. It evaluates uncertainties in the natural ocean sink and in future interventions such as seaweed cultivation, ocean fertilization and alkalinity enhancement, including environmental risks and monitoring needs. The report guides research investment and policy evidence; it does not endorse commercial deployment or create a permitting or crediting system.
source: Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of UNESCO
status_note: Launched in February 2026 as the current IOC-UNESCO international ocean-carbon research assessment and implementation vision.

document_title: High Level Review of a Wide Range of Proposed Marine Geoengineering Techniques
notes: GESAMP Reports and Studies No. 98 provides a high-level scientific and governance review of a wide range of proposed marine geoengineering techniques. It examines potential effectiveness, feasibility, scalability, monitoring and verification, environmental and socioeconomic effects, uncertainties, reversibility, and governance implications across multiple ocean-intervention concepts. Röschel and Neumann use the report as a principal technical source for characterizing ocean-based negative-emissions technologies and their possible impacts on ocean condition and ecosystem services. The review emphasizes the very uneven maturity of the evidence base and the need for coordinated, independent and precautionary assessment before large-scale activity. It supports a structured framework for proposal submission and expert review rather than promoting deployment. The report is an official scientific assessment and not a permit, funding award, carbon-credit methodology or authorization for commercial marine CDR. Its conclusions should therefore be read as evidence-building and risk-governance input rather than a statement that any particular marine geoengineering technique is ready, safe or capable of delivering durable net removals at climate-relevant scale.
source: Joint Group of Experts on the Scientific Aspects of Marine Environmental Protection (GESAMP)
status_note: Published in 2019 as GESAMP Reports and Studies No. 98; continues to serve as a major international scientific and governance reference for marine geoengineering assessment.

document_title: A Scientific Summary for Policy-Makers — The State of the Science for Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal
notes: This GESAMP policy summary presents the current scientific understanding of actively investigated marine CDR techniques and highlights uncertainties concerning removal efficacy, durability, monitoring, ecological effects and societal implications. It is intended to support regulators and policy-makers considering research and project proposals. The summary does not approve a specific activity, establish binding assessment criteria or certify carbon removals.
source: Joint Group of Experts on the Scientific Aspects of Marine Environmental Protection (GESAMP)
status_note: Released in 2025 as a current science-to-policy summary under GESAMP Working Group 41.

document_title: Report of COMEST on the Ethics of Climate Engineering
notes: The UNESCO World Commission on the Ethics of Scientific Knowledge and Technology assesses ethical, social, cultural and governance issues raised by climate engineering, including ocean fertilization and artificial ocean circulation approaches. It recommends precaution, responsible research, public-sector oversight, inclusive participation, equity, human-rights safeguards and international dialogue. The report is advisory and does not authorize research or deployment, prescribe a technical MRV method or establish a carbon market mechanism.
source: UNESCO World Commission on the Ethics of Scientific Knowledge and Technology (COMEST)
status_note: Adopted by COMEST in November 2023 and published as a non-binding UNESCO ethics and governance report.

document_title: UNESCO Marine World Heritage: Custodians of the Globe’s Blue Carbon Assets
notes: UNESCO's Marine World Heritage blue-carbon assessment evaluates the global importance of mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrass meadows located within marine World Heritage sites. It compiles evidence on the extent and carbon stocks of these ecosystems, their role in maintaining long-term carbon stores, and the climate and biodiversity value of avoiding degradation and supporting conservation or restoration. The Röschel and Neumann review cites the assessment when discussing the World Heritage Convention's indirect relevance to ocean-based negative emissions: marine World Heritage areas can contain globally significant blue-carbon assets whose ecological and cultural values may be affected by climate interventions or by the condition of coastal ecosystems. The report also discusses opportunities for conservation finance and alignment with climate goals. It is an evidence and policy-support publication, not a treaty amendment, project permit, carbon-credit standard or guarantee of additional removals. Protection of an existing carbon stock should not automatically be treated as quantified new CDR.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre
status_note: Official UNESCO World Heritage scientific assessment of blue-carbon assets in marine World Heritage sites; retained as an active policy-support and evidence reference.

subnational_area: Global blue carbon projects and enabling institutions
document_title: Blue Carbon Finance Toolbox
notes: The toolbox provides an international guide to public, private, market-based and blended finance mechanisms for conserving, restoring and sustainably managing mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrass ecosystems. It reviews financing barriers, enabling policy conditions, project aggregation, community protections and approaches including grants, carbon credits, blue bonds and payments for ecosystem services. It is voluntary guidance and does not create a fund, approve a project, certify removals or establish a mandatory carbon-credit standard.
source: Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of UNESCO
status_note: First edition published in June 2025 as IOC Technical Series No. 208 and launched at the third UN Ocean Conference.

subnational_area: Countries preparing national greenhouse-gas inventories and REDD+ reporting
document_title: GFOI Methods and Guidance Documentation — Blue Carbon Module
notes: The module guides countries through methodological steps for reporting emissions and removals from coastal wetlands in national greenhouse-gas inventories. It addresses mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrasses, links remote-sensing and ground observations with inventory preparation, and provides examples relevant to REDD+ results-based payments and blue carbon initiatives. The module supports consistent MRV and accounting but does not replace IPCC guidance, create a carbon registry or certify project-level credits.
source: Global Forest Observations Initiative / Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
status_note: Released in January 2025 as an active module in the GFOI Family of Resources.

document_title: Ghana: A Blue Carbon Readiness Assessment
notes: The assessment applies the World Bank Blue Carbon Readiness Framework to Ghana and reviews the scientific data, greenhouse-gas inventory coverage, institutional arrangements, policy environment and financing conditions relevant to mangroves, salt marshes and seagrasses. It identifies readiness gaps and recommended actions for mobilizing public and private investment while safeguarding local benefits. The report is diagnostic and does not itself establish a national blue carbon strategy, approve projects or authorize carbon-credit issuance.
source: World Bank / Government of Ghana / PROBLUE
status_note: Country readiness assessment completed and published in 2024.

document_title: Mozambique — Strengthening NDC Ambitions through Blue Carbon Frontiers
notes: The report assesses how Mozambique can strengthen Nationally Determined Contribution ambition through mangroves, seagrass meadows and salt marshes. It examines carbon stocks, mitigation and adaptation opportunities, policy and institutional conditions, monitoring needs and investment pathways, and provides recommendations for integrating blue carbon into climate planning. It is a completed advisory study and does not amend Mozambique’s NDC, establish a crediting programme or authorize restoration activities.
source: World Bank / Government of Mozambique / PROBLUE
status_note: Final advisory report published on 26 September 2024 under the Blue Carbon Readiness Framework pilot.

document_title: Blue Carbon Rapid Assessment for Pakistan in Support of the Revision of Its Nationally Determined Contribution under the Paris Agreement
notes: The rapid assessment reviews Pakistan’s blue carbon exposure, estimates coastal carbon stocks and trends, and evaluates the potential contribution of coastal ecosystems to climate mitigation, adaptation and the revision of the national NDC. It provides a first-pass evidence base and identifies opportunities for improved data, policy integration and investment. The assessment does not itself revise the NDC, quantify verified project removals, approve restoration work or establish a carbon-credit mechanism.
source: World Bank / Government of Pakistan
status_note: Revised rapid assessment published in 2021 to inform Pakistan’s NDC revision process.

document_title: The Economics of Large-Scale Mangrove Conservation and Restoration in Indonesia
notes: The technical report evaluates the economic benefits and policy trade-offs of large-scale mangrove conservation and restoration in Indonesia. It compares conservation and restoration scenarios, values ecosystem services including climate regulation and coastal protection, and recommends long-term monitoring, integrated finance, stronger data and enforcement, and exploration of blue carbon payments with community benefit sharing. The report provides policy analysis and does not itself impose a mangrove moratorium, allocate restoration funding or issue blue carbon credits.
source: World Bank / Government of Indonesia
status_note: Technical report published on 27 June 2022 in support of Indonesia’s mangrove policy and the Mangroves for Coastal Resilience Project.

subnational_area: Small island developing States and other coastal countries
document_title: Blue Economies and Nature-Based Solutions
notes: This resource guide provides practical advice for integrating blue economy measures, coastal nature-based solutions and the protection and restoration of blue carbon ecosystems into Nationally Determined Contributions and related climate policy documents. It summarizes entry points, policy instruments and examples for policymakers and technical experts, with particular attention to Latin American and Caribbean small island developing States. The guide is voluntary and does not alter an NDC, create a financing facility or certify carbon removals.
source: United Nations Development Programme
status_note: Published on 23 October 2023 as an active policy resource for NDC preparation and implementation.

subnational_area: Parties submitting the 2025 round of Nationally Determined Contributions
document_title: 2025 Nationally Determined Contributions Synthesis Report
notes: The UNFCCC synthesis report evaluates the new round of Nationally Determined Contributions and documents the expansion of ocean-based climate action. It identifies conservation and restoration of blue carbon ecosystems, marine protected areas and blue carbon sequestration among reported adaptation and mitigation measures, and summarizes associated finance needs and conditional commitments. The report synthesizes Party submissions and does not create new obligations, approve projects, set a blue carbon accounting methodology or verify removals.
source: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change Secretariat
status_note: Published in 2025 as the official UNFCCC synthesis of the new NDC submission round.

document_title: Mozambique: A Blue Carbon Readiness Assessment
notes: This final country assessment applies the World Bank Blue Carbon Readiness Framework to Mozambique and evaluates data availability, greenhouse-gas inventory treatment, governance, legal and institutional conditions, and finance options for mangroves, seagrasses and salt marshes. It converts the earlier readiness mission into a formal published diagnostic with recommended next steps for policy development and investment preparation. The assessment does not itself enact a strategy, authorize projects, create a registry or issue carbon credits.
source: World Bank / Government of Mozambique / PROBLUE
status_note: Final country readiness assessment published in 2024; recorded separately from the earlier 2023 assessment mission page as a distinct formal publication.

document_title: National Blue Carbon Policy Assessment Framework
notes: The framework provides governments with a structured five-step assessment tool for determining whether and how mangrove, salt-marsh and seagrass carbon policies and incentive mechanisms can be aligned with existing coastal regulation and management. It supports policy-readiness analysis and integrated coastal planning, but it does not impose binding national rules, approve projects or establish a carbon-credit registry.
source: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
status_note: Published in 2016 as a voluntary international policy-assessment framework and retained as an active reference tool.

document_title: Mediterranean Blue Carbon Strategy: First Edition
notes: The strategy establishes a regional 2025–2030 roadmap for protecting, restoring and sustainably managing Mediterranean blue-carbon ecosystems, with particular attention to Posidonia oceanica and other seagrass meadows. It coordinates scientific, economic and community action, but it is a non-binding regional framework and does not itself create permitting rules, mandatory restoration targets or a carbon-credit standard.
source: International Union for Conservation of Nature — Centre for Mediterranean Cooperation
status_note: First edition published in 2025 with a regional action horizon through 2030.

document_title: Manual for the Creation of Blue Carbon Projects in Europe and the Mediterranean
notes: The Manual for the Creation of Blue Carbon Projects in Europe and the Mediterranean provides practical project-development guidance for coastal blue-carbon conservation and restoration. Produced with support from the EU LIFE programme and partner organizations, it translates scientific and policy concepts into a sequence of project-design tasks, including initial site screening, eligibility and feasibility assessment, stakeholder engagement, baseline and project-scenario development, carbon-stock and flux assessment, monitoring and reporting, environmental and social considerations, financing and possible certification pathways. The manual is especially relevant to mangroves, seagrasses, salt marshes and comparable vegetated coastal habitats in European and Mediterranean settings. Its role is methodological and capacity-building: it can improve project consistency and investment readiness, but it is not an EU regulation, does not certify a project by itself and does not override national permitting or land/sea-use rules. References to carbon finance or certification are options for project developers rather than automatic credit issuance. Quantified climate benefits still require project-specific baselines, additionality, monitoring, verification, permanence and leakage treatment under whichever standard or public programme is used.
source: International Union for Conservation of Nature — Centre for Mediterranean Cooperation
status_note: Voluntary project-development manual published in 2021; remains a guidance resource rather than a binding EU standard or credit issuer.

document_title: International Policy Framework for Blue Carbon Ecosystems
notes: The framework maps intersections and opportunities for conserving and restoring mangroves, seagrasses and tidal marshes across international climate, biodiversity and sustainable-development policy processes. Its purpose is to improve alignment and implementation across global institutions; it does not create binding treaty obligations, national permits, mandatory accounting rules or a carbon-credit mechanism.
source: International Union for Conservation of Nature and Conservation International
status_note: Jointly published in 2023 as a voluntary framework for alignment across international policy processes.

document_title: Blue Carbon Policy Framework: Based on the First Workshop of the International Blue Carbon Policy Working Group
notes: The first Blue Carbon Policy Framework was developed from the International Blue Carbon Policy Working Group process to organize policy options for protecting and restoring coastal blue-carbon ecosystems and integrating their climate value into international and national decision-making. It lays out policy objectives, activities, possible timelines and stakeholder roles across climate mitigation, coastal management, science, finance and incentive mechanisms. A central purpose is to make mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrasses visible in climate policy and to create conditions under which conservation and restoration can attract public or private finance, including voluntary carbon-market approaches where appropriate. The framework is intentionally strategic and non-binding. It does not itself create a carbon market, define a universally accepted offset methodology, establish mandatory MRV requirements or confer legal authority for restoration activity. The textbook's reference to a 'Blue Carbon Policy Framework' and voluntary carbon finance is therefore best understood as policy guidance rather than a United Nations regulation. This 2011 edition is retained separately from the 2012 revision because the database treats distinct formal versions as separate records.
source: International Union for Conservation of Nature and Conservation International
status_note: First edition published in 2011; subsequently revised by Blue Carbon Policy Framework 2.0 in 2012.

document_title: Blue Carbon Policy Framework 2.0: Based on the Discussion of the International Blue Carbon Policy Working Group
notes: Blue Carbon Policy Framework 2.0 is the revised international policy guidance produced through the International Blue Carbon Policy Working Group process. It refines a coordinated programme for incorporating coastal blue-carbon ecosystems into climate mitigation, conservation, restoration, sustainable management and incentive structures. The framework identifies policy objectives, suggested activities, stakeholders and sequencing, including opportunities to strengthen carbon accounting, mobilize finance and use voluntary market mechanisms to reward credible protection or restoration. Its significance for ocean carbon policy is that it links ecosystem management with climate-policy and financing architecture while recognizing the need for sound science, safeguards and consistent measurement. It remains a voluntary framework rather than an international treaty or a United Nations carbon-credit standard. It does not establish mandatory project baselines, issue credits, authorize restoration or create compliance-market eligibility. Any project using carbon finance must rely on a separate approved methodology and legal framework. The 2.0 record is maintained separately from the 2011 first edition because it is a distinct revised version with a more developed policy programme.
source: International Union for Conservation of Nature and Conservation International
status_note: Revised international blue-carbon policy framework published in 2012; voluntary guidance with no independent credit-issuance or permitting authority.

document_title: The Significance and Management of Natural Carbon Stores in the Open Ocean
notes: The report reviews major open-ocean carbon pools and sinks and explains how atmospheric carbon is captured, stored and mobilized in the ocean. It calls for ocean carbon processes to be incorporated into decision-making and management at multiple scales, but it does not establish a deployment programme, quantify an authorized removal target or prescribe a binding accounting or crediting methodology.
source: IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas and IUCN Global Marine and Polar Programme
status_note: Published in 2014 as an international scientific and policy reference on open-ocean carbon stores.

document_title: Out of the Blue: The Value of Seagrasses to the Environment and to People
notes: The global assessment synthesizes evidence on seagrass carbon sequestration and storage, ecosystem services, threats and management needs, and calls for coordinated conservation, sustainable management and restoration. It is an evidence and policy report rather than a funded restoration programme, binding conservation rule, national inventory methodology or carbon-credit standard.
source: United Nations Environment Programme, GRID-Arendal and UNEP World Conservation Monitoring Centre
status_note: Published on 11 December 2020 as a global seagrass assessment and continuing policy reference.

document_title: Protecting Seagrass Through Payments for Ecosystem Services: A Community Guide
notes: The guide provides community groups and project developers with governance and best-practice advice for seagrass conservation projects financed through payments for ecosystem services, including carbon-based payments. It does not provide country-specific legal approval, create a registry, certify projects, establish a complete carbon-accounting methodology or guarantee the issuance of credits or payments.
source: United Nations Environment Programme
status_note: Published in 2020 as voluntary global guidance for community-based seagrass payment-for-ecosystem-services projects.

document_title: United Nations General Assembly Resolution A/RES/76/265 — World Seagrass Day
notes: The resolution proclaims 1 March as World Seagrass Day and calls for greater awareness and action to conserve seagrasses and maintain their ecosystem functions, including their contribution to climate mitigation and carbon storage. It is a non-binding international observance resolution and does not establish restoration targets, funding, permitting requirements, greenhouse-gas accounting rules or a carbon-credit mechanism.
source: United Nations General Assembly
status_note: Adopted without a vote on 23 May 2022 and establishes an annual international observance on 1 March.

document_title: Benin NDC 3.0 — Mangrove Conservation and Restoration Measures
notes: Benin's NDC 3.0 incorporates mangrove conservation, sustainable use and restoration into national mitigation and adaptation planning. Its implementation annex includes a 2026–2030 mangrove-resilience programme in southern Benin, restoration actions in the Lower Oueme Valley and municipal mangrove projects, with quantified landscape or restoration indicators and a mix of unconditional and conditional activities. The NDC does not itself establish a blue-carbon crediting methodology or verify achieved carbon removals.
source: Government of Benin / United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Submitted as Benin NDC 3.0 for the 2026–2035 period; implementation includes both unconditional actions and measures dependent on external finance or support.

document_title: China's 2035 Nationally Determined Contribution — Blue-Carbon Inventory and Mangrove Methodology
notes: China's 2035 NDC reports carbon-stock surveys across 39 representative mangrove, seagrass and salt-marsh distribution areas and the initial establishment of a national blue-carbon ecosystem carbon-density parameter database. It also records publication of a mangrove-afforestation methodology under the national voluntary greenhouse-gas reduction market and reports coastal-wetland restoration progress. The NDC does not set a separate quantified blue-carbon removal target for 2035.
source: Government of China / United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Submitted to the UNFCCC on 3 November 2025; the blue-carbon surveys, parameter database and mangrove methodology are reported as completed or published, while future implementation remains dependent on domestic measures.

document_title: NDC 3.0 in Latin America and the Caribbean: Ambition, Inclusiveness and Pathways to Sustainability
notes: The regional assessment reviews 22 NDC 3.0 submissions available by December 2025 and examines ambition, governance, finance, inclusion and implementation conditions. It identifies new or expanded treatment of blue carbon, mangroves and coastal ecosystems in several Caribbean NDCs and places those measures within wider regional trends. The report is an analytical reference and does not create national obligations, approve projects or establish a carbon-crediting standard.
source: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Regional Issue-Based Coalition on Climate Change and Resilience
status_note: Published on 11 June 2026 as a regional assessment of NDC 3.0 submissions and implementation needs.

document_title: Blue Carbon Ecosystems Investment Planning Supplement to the Climate Investment Planning and Mobilization Framework
notes: The supplement guides governments in integrating mangroves, seagrass meadows and salt marshes into NDC investment planning. It covers baseline data, tenure and governance conditions, community inclusion, project costing and a diversified finance mix that may include public budgets, donor finance, blue bonds, debt-for-nature swaps, carbon markets, biodiversity credits, payments for ecosystem services and blended finance. It is voluntary planning guidance and does not itself provide finance, approve projects or issue credits.
source: NDC Partnership Support Unit and The Pew Charitable Trusts
status_note: Launched on 19 May 2025 as a voluntary supplement to the Climate Investment Planning and Mobilization Framework.

document_title: Responsible Finance for Blue Carbon Ecosystems
notes: The WWF guidance sets out an approach for designing strategic policy frameworks that can mobilize responsible finance for conserving and restoring blue-carbon ecosystems. It addresses enabling policy, investment quality, community and environmental safeguards, and financing opportunities for mangroves, salt marshes and seagrasses. The publication provides recommendations only and does not create a financing facility, certify projects or authorize carbon-credit issuance.
source: World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF)
status_note: Published in November 2023 as non-binding guidance for responsible blue-carbon investment and finance.

document_title: Deep Blue: Opportunities for Blue Carbon Finance in Coastal Ecosystems
notes: The IFC report assesses emerging coastal blue-carbon markets, project-development barriers, carbon pricing, financing structures and opportunities for financial institutions. It discusses voluntary carbon finance, blended finance, bonds, purchase agreements and integrity requirements such as credible baselines, leakage controls, monitoring, reporting and verification, additionality and permanence. The report is informational and does not constitute investment advice, establish a carbon standard or issue credits.
source: International Finance Corporation (IFC), World Bank Group
status_note: Published in 2023 as a market and financing assessment for coastal blue-carbon projects.

document_title: Mobilising Climate Finance for Oceanic and Coastal Resilience
notes: The Green Climate Fund and GIZ working paper supports accredited entities and other organizations in preparing proposals for the protection, conservation and sustainable use of coastal and marine ecosystems, including mangroves, salt marshes, seagrasses and coral reefs. It reviews financing gaps, GCF instruments, public and private capital, blue bonds and proposal resources for assessing habitat condition, carbon stocks, climate vulnerability and ecosystem services. It is proposal-development guidance and does not itself approve funding or authorize carbon credits.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF) and Deutsche Gesellschaft fuer Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ)
status_note: Published as a Green Climate Fund working paper on 10 March 2026; any financing remains subject to separate GCF proposal and approval processes.

subnational_area: Europe and international marine carbon dioxide removal research and governance communities
document_title: Monitoring, Reporting and Verification for Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal
notes: The European Marine Board Future Science Brief assesses knowledge gaps, observing and modelling needs, accounting challenges, environmental-impact assessment and governance requirements for transparent monitoring, reporting and verification of marine carbon dioxide removal. It concludes that no mCDR method currently has sufficiently robust and comprehensive MRV for credible large-scale implementation and recommends developing standardized protocols before deployment. The brief is science-policy guidance and does not authorize projects, certify removals or establish a carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Marine Board
status_note: Published on 17 November 2025 as European Marine Board Future Science Brief No. 13.

document_title: Best Practice Guidelines for Mangrove Restoration
notes: The guidelines provide step-by-step voluntary best practices for mangrove restoration project design, financing, implementation, monitoring and long-term management. They emphasize community-based ecological restoration, biodiversity safeguards, local participation, sustainability and high-integrity finance, and include modules on alignment with national mitigation targets and the optional use of carbon credits for project maintenance and community benefits. They do not certify projects, issue credits or create legally binding restoration requirements.
source: Global Mangrove Alliance and The Blue Carbon Initiative
status_note: Launched on 18 October 2023 as voluntary international best-practice guidance.

subnational_area: Mangrove restoration projects recorded through Global Mangrove Watch
document_title: Mangrove Restoration Tracker Tool Guide
notes: The guide supports use of the Mangrove Restoration Tracker Tool to record standardized field and desk-based information across a project's lifetime, including the pre-restoration baseline, restoration interventions and post-restoration monitoring. The associated portal and global project database are hosted through Global Mangrove Watch to improve learning and comparison across restoration projects. The tool does not independently verify carbon removals, certify restoration success or issue carbon credits.
source: Global Mangrove Alliance and Global Mangrove Watch partners
status_note: Guide dated 1 August 2023; the Mangrove Restoration Tracker Tool was launched on 10 August 2023.

document_title: Coastal Blue Carbon Habitats and Climate Change: Recommendations for Enhanced Action under the UNFCCC at SB60
notes: The policy brief recommends opportunities for Parties to advance conservation, restoration and sustainable management of mangroves, salt marshes and seagrasses in UNFCCC processes concerning finance, mitigation ambition and adaptation. It promotes coastal nature-based solutions and stronger integration of blue carbon habitats into international climate action. The brief is an advocacy and policy-coordination document and does not constitute a COP decision, binding national commitment, financing approval or carbon-credit methodology.
source: Wetlands International
status_note: Published on 13 May 2024 as a policy brief for the UNFCCC SB60 negotiations.

subnational_area: Blue carbon project developers, investors and implementing partners
document_title: High-Quality Blue Carbon Practitioners Guide, Second Edition
notes: The second edition translates the High-Quality Blue Carbon Principles into practical guidance across the project lifecycle, from early concepts and planning through implementation. It consolidates tools, case studies and due-diligence resources for designing, financing, monitoring and adaptively managing projects that deliver climate, biodiversity and community outcomes. The guide applies to credit-generating and non-credit projects but does not operate a registry, certify compliance, issue credits or authorize project deployment.
source: Conservation International, Ocean Risk and Resilience Action Alliance and partner organizations
status_note: Second edition launched on 22 July 2026 as updated voluntary practitioner guidance.

subnational_area: Blue carbon projects and participating coastal communities
document_title: High-Quality Blue Carbon: Guidance for Benefit-Sharing Agreements
notes: The guidance supports the design of benefit-sharing agreements for blue carbon projects, with attention to meaningful community participation, transparent governance, allocation of project value and revenues, and durable social and environmental outcomes. It is intended to help project developers, investors and communities structure fair arrangements, including in projects linked to carbon finance. It does not prescribe a mandatory revenue share, certify projects, determine land or resource rights, or issue carbon credits.
source: World Economic Forum, Conservation International and CrossBoundary
status_note: Published in May 2026 as voluntary international project-governance guidance.

document_title: Mangrove Breakthrough Financial Roadmap
notes: The Mangrove Breakthrough Financial Roadmap provides a voluntary international financing pathway for scaling mangrove conservation, protection and restoration toward the Mangrove Breakthrough's 2030 objectives. It examines how public budgets, philanthropy, concessional capital and private investment can be combined through blended-finance structures and investable business models, including blue-carbon finance, sustainable aquaculture, fisheries, tourism and other activities linked to healthy mangrove ecosystems. The 2025 Ocean Panel ocean-finance working paper cites the Mangrove Breakthrough as a key blue-carbon finance initiative and describes an ambition to unlock approximately USD 4 billion for mangrove action. Current Mangrove Breakthrough communications likewise frame the USD 4 billion figure as a public-private-philanthropic finance mobilization goal associated with halting mangrove loss, restoring degraded mangroves and expanding effective protection by 2030. The figure should therefore be interpreted as a mobilization target or investment need, not as evidence that a separate USD 4 billion fund has already been fully capitalized or legally appropriated. The roadmap can help shape carbon-credit investment and other financing structures, but it does not itself issue credits, establish a registry, impose a mandatory MRV methodology, approve projects or guarantee investment returns. Project-level additionality, permanence, carbon accounting, biodiversity safeguards, community rights and legal authorization remain dependent on the standards and jurisdictions under which individual activities are implemented.
source: Global Mangrove Alliance, UN Climate Change High-Level Champions and Systemiq
status_note: Published in 2023 and used as an active voluntary finance roadmap for the Mangrove Breakthrough; the widely cited USD 4 billion figure is a finance-mobilization ambition, not proof of fully committed or disbursed fund capital.

subnational_area: Coastal blue carbon policy and project planning
document_title: Actionable Blue Carbon Ecosystems for Climate Mitigation and Adaptation
notes: The policy brief identifies mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrasses as currently actionable blue carbon ecosystems based on available science and management practices. It distinguishes emerging areas such as macroalgae, benthic sediments and mudflats from ecosystems or interventions that do not yet have an established mitigation pathway, and excludes non-ecosystem marine carbon dioxide removal and interventions that substantially move ecosystems away from their natural state. The document provides evidence-based policy framing and does not approve a methodology, authorize restoration or certify mitigation outcomes.
source: International Partnership for Blue Carbon
status_note: Updated policy brief published on 4 December 2023, superseding an earlier 2021 version.

subnational_area: National, subnational and local blue carbon project planning
document_title: Beyond Carbon Credits: Demystifying Non-Carbon Market Approaches for Blue Carbon Ecosystems
notes: The report explains non-carbon market approaches and financing instruments that can support conservation, restoration and sustainable management of mangroves, seagrasses and tidal salt marshes. It compares financing options and enabling conditions, including local context, community engagement and institutional readiness, and provides examples of instruments already being piloted or applied in coastal settings. It is decision-support guidance and does not create a financing facility, approve investment, establish a carbon market or issue credits.
source: Rare, Conservation International and the International Blue Carbon Institute
status_note: Published in 2025 as voluntary guidance on non-carbon market financing approaches for blue carbon ecosystems.

subnational_area: Global Goal on Adaptation indicator development
document_title: The Case for Mangrove-Related Indicators under the Global Goal on Adaptation
notes: The guidance proposes how mangrove-related indicators could contribute to refinement and measurement of progress under the Paris Agreement's Global Goal on Adaptation. It supports consideration of mangrove condition, protection, restoration and resilience within international adaptation monitoring and reporting. The document is an input to indicator development and does not itself amend the Global Goal on Adaptation framework, impose reporting obligations or establish a carbon-credit methodology.
source: Global Mangrove Alliance / Mangrove Breakthrough
status_note: Published on 29 April 2025 as non-binding guidance for ongoing Global Goal on Adaptation indicator refinement.

document_title: A Blue Carbon Sinks Assessment for South Africa
notes: The national technical assessment evaluates the extent, carbon-storage and sequestration potential of South African blue-carbon ecosystems and identifies opportunities for climate mitigation and improved coastal management. It provides an evidence base for future policy and restoration planning but does not establish a mandatory greenhouse-gas inventory method, authorize projects or create tradable carbon credits.
source: South African Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
status_note: Published in November 2021 as a completed national technical assessment.

document_title: Towards an Emissions Reduction Fund Method for Blue Carbon
notes: The report examined whether blue-carbon activities could be incorporated into Australia's Emissions Reduction Fund and identified restoration through the reintroduction of tidal flow to mangrove and tidal-marsh systems as the most promising method-development option. It supported establishment of a Blue Carbon Method Working Group, but the report itself did not create an approved methodology, register projects or issue Australian carbon credit units.
source: Australian Government Department of the Environment and Energy
status_note: Published in September 2019; the exploratory method-development process was later superseded by the 2022 blue-carbon methodology determination.

document_title: Blue Carbon Strategy for South Australia
notes: The five-year state strategy sought to accelerate the protection, restoration and creation of coastal blue-carbon ecosystems through research, partnerships, demonstration projects, investment design and improved policy coordination. It supported development of a Blue Carbon Investment Fund and project pipeline but did not itself establish a carbon-credit methodology, guarantee financing or authorize individual restoration projects.
source: Government of South Australia — Department for Environment and Water
status_note: Released in November 2019 as a five-year strategy; its stated implementation period has elapsed, although related state initiatives may continue.

document_title: NSW Blue Carbon Strategy 2022–2027
notes: The state strategy provides a five-year roadmap for protecting and restoring coastal blue-carbon ecosystems through research, streamlined approvals, investment mobilisation and ten initial implementation projects. It also proposes piloting a government-endorsed Blue Carbon Instrument. The strategy supports project development but does not automatically approve projects, establish a final crediting methodology or issue carbon units.
source: New South Wales Government — Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
status_note: Published in 2022 and operating as the New South Wales blue-carbon roadmap for 2022–2027.

document_title: UK Habitat Natural Capital Accounts: Quality and Methods Guide
notes: The Office for National Statistics guide documents methods and data quality for UK habitat natural-capital accounts, including greenhouse-gas regulation estimates for saltmarsh, seagrass and selected marine sediment habitats. It combines habitat extent, sequestration evidence and environmental-economic valuation. The statistics remain under development and the guide is not a project-level carbon-credit methodology, a national inventory decision or a restoration permit.
source: UK Office for National Statistics (ONS)
status_note: Last revised on 8 July 2026; the associated estimates are published as official statistics in development.

document_title: Responding to the Climate Change Committee's 2022 Progress Report Recommendations
notes: The government response commits to work through the UK Blue Carbon Evidence Partnership on a roadmap for the potential inclusion of saltmarsh and seagrass in the UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory and to address evidence gaps affecting emissions and removal estimates. It establishes a policy-development commitment but does not itself add those habitats to the inventory, prescribe final emission factors or create a project crediting mechanism.
source: UK Government
status_note: Published on 30 March 2023 as the government's formal response; the blue-carbon inventory work remains a policy-development commitment rather than a completed inventory change.

document_title: Climate Action Pathway: Ocean and Coastal Zones — Action Table
notes: The action table provides a voluntary global roadmap for ocean and coastal climate action, including protection and restoration of blue-carbon ecosystems, improved finance, governance, science and monitoring. It is designed to coordinate non-state and governmental action toward 2030 and 2050 milestones. The table does not create binding obligations, allocate funding, approve projects or establish a carbon-crediting standard.
source: UNFCCC Marrakech Partnership for Global Climate Action
status_note: Published on 9 November 2021 as a voluntary action pathway with milestones extending to 2030 and 2050.

document_title: Informal Summary Report of the Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue 2023
notes: The report summarizes the 2023 UNFCCC ocean and climate change dialogue, including discussions on coastal ecosystem restoration, blue-carbon solutions, finance, knowledge gaps and integration into national climate action. It records policy options and stakeholder views for the UNFCCC process but is not a COP decision, does not impose reporting obligations and does not authorize or fund specific restoration projects.
source: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Published on 14 September 2023 as the completed informal summary of the 2023 dialogue.

document_title: State of the Ocean Report 2024
notes: The global assessment reviews major ocean-climate knowledge and capacity gaps and includes blue-carbon ecosystems and marine forests as components of climate mitigation, adaptation and ocean management. It calls for improved observation, science, protection and restoration investment. The report is an evidence and policy assessment and does not set binding national targets, approve projects or establish a carbon-accounting or crediting system.
source: UNESCO Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC-UNESCO)
status_note: Published in 2024 as the first edition of the UNESCO-IOC State of the Ocean Report.

document_title: The United Kingdom's Blue Carbon Inventory: Assessment of Marine Carbon Storage and Sequestration Potential in UK Seas (Including Within Marine Protected Areas)
notes: The commissioned synthesis assesses the extent, distribution, carbon storage and sequestration potential of coastal vegetated habitats and seabed sediments across UK seas, including carbon within marine protected areas. It was funded by WWF, The Wildlife Trusts and the RSPB to inform management decisions. It is not the official UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory, a project-level monitoring methodology, a restoration authorization or a carbon-credit standard.
source: Scottish Association for Marine Science (SAMS)
status_note: Published on 19 September 2024 as a completed commissioned synthesis assessment.

subnational_area: Financial institutions and blue-carbon investment markets
document_title: Turning the Tide: A Financier’s Guide to Investing in Blue Carbon Ecosystems
notes: The guide supports financial institutions seeking to integrate mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrass meadows into investment strategies through sustainability credits, supply chains, infrastructure and insurance. It identifies regulatory complexity, transaction costs and limited project scale as barriers and proposes interventions including blended finance and risk-sharing tools. It is voluntary investment guidance and does not commit capital, certify projects, issue carbon credits or authorize restoration activities.
source: World Economic Forum
status_note: Published on 14 April 2026 as voluntary guidance for financial institutions.

document_title: SDVM003 Coastal Resilience Benefits from Restoration and Protection of Mangroves and Tidal Marshes
notes: The SD VISta methodology quantifies annual reductions in property damage from coastal flooding, expressed in United States dollars, resulting from mangrove and tidal-marsh restoration or protection. It can generate Coastal Resilience Assets and optional People Resilience Benefit claims and may be applied alongside Verra blue-carbon methodologies. The assets cannot be used for offsetting, and SDVM003 does not quantify carbon removals or issue Verified Carbon Units.
source: Verra — Sustainable Development Verified Impact Standard
status_note: Published on 22 April 2026 as an active SD VISta asset methodology.

document_title: Restoration of California Deltaic and Coastal Wetlands Methodology, Version 1.1
notes: American Carbon Registry Version 1.1 provides quantification, monitoring, reporting and verification procedures for greenhouse-gas reductions and removals from California deltaic and coastal wetland restoration, including tidal-wetland creation and specified Delta land-use conversions. ACR made the methodology inactive on 31 December 2022 because its performance-standard additionality test required reassessment. It is currently ineligible for listing new projects and may only become active after review.
source: American Carbon Registry (ACR)
status_note: Version 1.1 was published and made inactive on 31 December 2022; new project listings are not eligible.

document_title: Restoration of Degraded Deltaic Wetlands of the Mississippi Delta Methodology, Version 2.0
notes: American Carbon Registry Version 2.0 provides modular greenhouse-gas accounting and monitoring requirements for restoration of degraded Mississippi Delta wetlands. It quantifies additional carbon in aboveground biomass, belowground biomass and soil organic carbon and requires attributable carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide increases to be deducted. The methodology is inactive and ineligible for new project crediting because its MRV requirements require updating to the current ACR Standard.
source: American Carbon Registry (ACR)
status_note: Version 2.0 was published on 29 March 2023 and is currently inactive and ineligible for new project crediting.

document_title: Blue Carbon — IUCN Issues Brief
notes: The issues brief explains the mitigation, adaptation and long-term carbon-storage functions of mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrass meadows and identifies conservation and restoration as policy responses. It highlights integration through Nationally Determined Contributions, REDD+, national development goals and coastal planning. The brief is non-binding policy guidance and does not create a national target, carbon-accounting methodology, project authorization or crediting system.
source: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
status_note: Published in November 2017 as an IUCN issues brief.

subnational_area: Marine protected areas and ocean-climate finance
document_title: Saving the Ocean and Climate through Innovative Marine Protected Area Finance Mechanisms
notes: The COP27 advocacy brochure links effective marine protected areas with protection and restoration of blue-carbon habitats and calls for ocean finance to be integrated into the climate-finance architecture. It discusses public-private finance, the Blue Natural Capital Financing Facility, the Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund, blue bonds and a proposed Ocean Sustainability Bank. It is non-binding policy and financing guidance and does not itself establish a new fund, approve projects, certify removals or issue credits.
source: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
status_note: Published in November 2022 as an advocacy and policy brochure for UNFCCC COP27.

document_title: Blue Carbon Horizons: Strengthening Climate-Resilient Coastal Planning in Mauritius through Blue Carbon for Ecosystem-Based Adaptation
notes: The GEF and Special Climate Change Fund medium-size project is designed to generate and apply blue-carbon evidence for climate-resilient coastal planning, management and investment in Mauritius. The concept includes a GEF project grant of USD 2,652,295 and co-financing of USD 826,300. Concept approval does not confirm that implementation has begun, quantify achieved carbon removal, establish a national crediting methodology or authorize a specific deployment project.
source: Global Environment Facility (GEF) / International Union for Conservation of Nature
status_note: The concept was approved on 15 June 2026; the GEF page does not confirm that implementation has started.

document_title: Strengthening Nature-Based Solutions to Restore Ecosystems, and Conserve and Enhance Blue Carbon Stocks and Biodiversity in Viet Nam
notes: The concept-approved GEF-8 medium-size project is intended to restore and conserve coastal ecosystems in An Giang while strengthening enabling conditions, financing and institutional capacity for blue-carbon stocks, biodiversity, climate resilience and local livelihoods. The project has a GEF grant allocation of USD 3,502,968 and stated co-financing of USD 23 million. Concept approval does not demonstrate completed restoration, verified carbon removal or an operating carbon-credit mechanism.
source: Global Environment Facility (GEF) / United Nations Development Programme
status_note: The project concept was approved on 15 September 2025; implementation and verified outcomes are not confirmed.

subnational_area: Global carbon dioxide removal research, policy and markets
document_title: The State of Carbon Dioxide Removal, 3rd Edition
notes: The third edition is a global independent assessment of carbon dioxide removal research, demonstration, demand, policy, governance, current removal levels, scenarios, costs and potentials. Its marine coverage includes ocean alkalinity enhancement, ocean fertilization, direct ocean capture, macroalgae-based approaches and biomass sinking, with attention to measurement, monitoring, reporting, verification and environmental uncertainty. The report evaluates the field and does not authorize deployment, certify projects or verify removal claims.
source: State of Carbon Dioxide Removal consortium
status_note: Published in June 2026 as the third edition of the global independent assessment.

subnational_area: Chocó, Valle del Cauca, Cauca and Nariño
document_title: Biomanglar: Empowering Collective Territories through Conservation, Sustainable Use, and Restoration Initiatives of Mangroves to Contribute to Colombia’s National Biodiversity Strategy
notes: The approved Global Biodiversity Framework Fund project supports conservation, sustainable use and restoration of mangroves in Colombia's Pacific region through Afro-Colombian collective-territory governance. Its implementation design includes mangrove restoration, improved monitoring with blue-carbon assessments, community leadership, payments for ecosystem services and exploration of biodiversity-credit and blue-carbon schemes. Project approval does not by itself establish a national carbon methodology, certify credits or confirm completed restoration and carbon outcomes.
source: Global Environment Facility / Global Biodiversity Framework Fund / Development Bank of Latin America
status_note: Approved for implementation on 6 March 2026; the official sources do not yet confirm completed field activities or verified carbon outcomes.

document_title: ReSCUE Oceans Act (H.R. 7656)
notes: The House companion bill would establish a NOAA programme for marine carbon dioxide removal research, field trials, monitoring, research areas, grants and interagency coordination. It directs work on ocean alkalinity enhancement, electrochemical approaches, macroalgae cultivation, nutrient fertilization, artificial upwelling and downwelling, and carbon storage in coastal and estuarine ecosystems, while developing MRV standards, environmental thresholds, community safeguards and technical support for credible voluntary carbon markets. The bill was introduced and referred to committees; it has not been enacted, does not create an operating programme, and does not authorize deployment outside existing environmental law.
source: United States Congress / U.S. Government Publishing Office
status_note: Introduced in the House of Representatives on 24 February 2026 and referred to the relevant committees; not enacted.

document_title: ReSCUE Oceans Act (S. 3910)
notes: The Senate companion bill would establish a NOAA programme for marine carbon dioxide removal research, field trials, monitoring, research areas, grants and interagency coordination. It directs work on ocean alkalinity enhancement, electrochemical approaches, macroalgae cultivation, nutrient fertilization, artificial upwelling and downwelling, and carbon storage in coastal and estuarine ecosystems, while developing MRV standards, environmental thresholds, community safeguards and technical support for credible voluntary carbon markets. The bill was introduced and referred to committee; it has not been enacted, does not create an operating programme, and does not authorize deployment outside existing environmental law.
source: United States Congress / U.S. Government Publishing Office
status_note: Introduced in the Senate on 25 February 2026 and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation; not enacted.

subnational_area: European permanent carbon removal project and financing landscape
document_title: Carbon Removals in the EU — Review of Current Carbon Removal Projects and Early-Stage Financing
notes: The European Commission study reviews permanent carbon removal projects and early-stage financing in the European Union under the policy context of the Carbon Removals and Carbon Farming Certification Framework. Its technology coverage explicitly includes the ocean-based pathways of direct ocean capture and ocean alkalinity enhancement, alongside other permanent removal approaches, and examines the emerging project and investment landscape. The report is an evidence and financing assessment; it does not adopt an EU certification methodology for either ocean pathway, approve a specific project, verify removals or authorize marine deployment.
source: European Commission Directorate-General for Climate Action / Publications Office of the European Union
status_note: Published in 2025 and released by the Publications Office of the European Union on 21 August 2025.

document_title: Northern Ireland Blue Carbon Action Plan 2025–2030
notes: Northern Ireland's first Blue Carbon Action Plan establishes a 2025–2030 framework for protecting, actively managing, restoring and creating blue-carbon habitats in the Northern Ireland inshore area. It provides for habitat prioritisation, spatial and condition baselines, annual monitoring, research on carbon stocks and flows, pilot and demonstration restoration projects, governance arrangements and exploration of green-finance options. The plan covers multiple coastal and marine habitats, including saltmarsh, seagrass, seabed sediments and biogenic habitats. It is an active high-level action plan, but many delivery measures depend on subsequent prioritisation, funding, stakeholder co-delivery and project-specific decisions; it does not itself quantify additional removals, establish a carbon-credit methodology or authorize an individual restoration project.
source: Northern Ireland Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (DAERA)
status_note: Published on 23 April 2025; active action-plan period 2025–2030.

document_title: The NOAA Ocean Acidification Program 2024 National Oceanographic Partnership Program Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal Meeting Summary Report
notes: This NOAA report documents the 2024 meeting of marine carbon dioxide removal research groups funded through the FY2022 and FY2023 National Oceanographic Partnership Program calls managed by the NOAA Ocean Acidification Program. It records project progress and cross-project discussion intended to support completion of the funded research portfolio and strengthen coordination among research teams. The report is a programme-learning and knowledge-sharing output; it does not create a new funding call, certify a removal method, approve field deployment or establish a binding regulatory or carbon-credit framework.
source: NOAA Oceanic and Atmospheric Research / NOAA Ocean Acidification Program
status_note: Published by NOAA in 2025 as a non-series meeting summary report.

document_title: Workshop on Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal (WKmCDR; Outputs from 2024 Meeting)
notes: The ICES Scientific Report synthesizes an international workshop on marine carbon dioxide removal focused on ocean alkalinity enhancement, ocean nutrient fertilization, direct ocean capture, and macroalgae cultivation and sinking. It reviews technology cases, possible effects on fisheries, aquaculture and marine ecosystems, national and international governance, Indigenous considerations and the need for early engagement with affected communities and rightsholders. The report builds an evidence and coordination base for responsible research and development; it does not authorize deployment, create a permitting regime, verify carbon removals or endorse any pathway for commercial-scale use.
source: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
status_note: Published in 2025 as ICES Scientific Reports, volume 7, issue 7; corrected version issued in January 2025.

document_title: Request for Quotations — Blue Carbon Governance Capacity-Building Programme for Commonwealth Governments
notes: The Commonwealth Secretariat issued a request for quotations to appoint a consultant to design and deliver a four-to-six-month capacity-building programme for government officials across Commonwealth member states. The programme focuses on practical policy, legal and institutional enabling conditions for credible and high-integrity blue-carbon initiatives. It is an official procurement and capacity-building measure; the notice does not itself adopt a blue-carbon law, authorize projects, establish a carbon-credit methodology or confirm that a contract has been awarded.
source: Commonwealth Secretariat
status_note: RFQ issued in July 2026; quotations closed on 20 July 2026 and an award was not confirmed on the cited page

document_title: Blue Climate Action in the East Asian Seas Region — Preliminary Policy Paper
notes: UNEP's Coordinating Body on the Seas of East Asia developed a preliminary policy paper on aligning blue-carbon and other nature-based solutions with regional mitigation, adaptation, biodiversity and coastal-resilience goals. The paper was shared with the nine participating countries and experts through an April 2026 regional webinar to support policy harmonization and development under the COBSEA Strategic Directions 2023–2027. The document remained preliminary on the cited page and did not itself establish binding restoration targets, a crediting system or project approvals.
source: United Nations Environment Programme — Coordinating Body on the Seas of East Asia (UNEP-COBSEA)
status_note: Preliminary policy paper presented for regional discussion on 16 April 2026; formal adoption was not confirmed

document_title: Guidance for the Potential Application of Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal (mCDR) in U.S. National Marine Sanctuaries
