CORDIS records early termination in 2020. The project did not establish a restoration programme, accounting standard or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project started on 1 September 2019 and was terminated on 30 June 2020.

document_title: EMMA — Enhancing Mangrove Restoration through Microtopographic Analysis
notes: The planned Marie Skłodowska-Curie project will investigate how fine-scale topography and hydrology control mangrove seedling retention, establishment and survival. UAV LiDAR, hyperspectral surveys, field experiments and biophysical modelling will be used to identify high-potential restoration areas and improve long-term restoration success. The project had not started as of August 2026 and therefore does not represent completed restoration, verified carbon sequestration or issued credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: EC signature date: 30 March 2026; planned project period: 1 February 2027 to 31 January 2030.

document_title: CREC — Coastal Research Network on Environmental Changes
notes: The FP7 network examined climate and land-use pressures on mangrove forests through an international exchange programme, a mangrove reference database, physiological and population studies and ecosystem modelling. Its results included evidence that mangrove crabs can enhance soil aeration and mangrove carbon sequestration. The project was completed research and collaboration; it did not create a restoration target, carbon-accounting method or verified crediting programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2010 to 31 May 2014.

document_title: BLUESURVEY — Underwater Satellite Technology for Seagrass Blue-Carbon Monitoring
notes: The European Innovation Council funded development of an underwater hyperspectral mapping platform for seagrass meadows and other seafloor applications. The project combined underwater imaging, precise navigation and artificial-intelligence processing to map seagrass condition and estimate stored carbon, with the stated aim of reducing verification costs for restoration and carbon-credit projects. The project closed in 2024 and did not itself certify a methodology, issue credits or prove additional carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2022 to 30 April 2024; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: SMART — Sponge Microbiome Adaptation and Resilience to Thermal Stress
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project investigates how sponge-associated microorganisms respond to thermal stress and contribute to host resilience. Marine sponges influence carbon cycling and sequestration through microbial processing of dissolved and particulate organic matter, and the project combines experiments, microbiome analysis and ecological monitoring to support conservation under ocean warming. It is active research and does not constitute an engineered carbon-removal activity, restoration permit or crediting methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2027.

document_title: MARIX — Methane and Ammonium Removal in Marine Redox Transition Zones
notes: The European Research Council funded MARIX to identify microbial pathways that remove methane and ammonium in marine redox transition zones. The project combines field observations, geochemical measurements, isotope tracing and microbial analyses to determine how these processes regulate marine carbon and nitrogen cycling and limit greenhouse-gas release. It is active fundamental research and does not constitute carbon-dioxide removal deployment, a carbon-credit programme or a regulatory standard.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2020 to 31 August 2027.

document_title: DOMAINE — Dissolved Organic Matter in Coastal Ecosystems: Transport, Dynamics and Environmental Impact
notes: The FP5 project investigated the transport, storage and cycling of dissolved organic carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus from land into coastal ecosystems across four climatic zones. It combined field studies, experiments and modelling to assess how land use, hydrology and autochthonous production affect coastal dissolved organic matter and environmental management. The project was completed as scientific research and did not establish a carbon-removal engineering activity, crediting methodology or deployment authorization.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2001 to 31 December 2003.

document_title: CarbEx — Tracing Carbon Exchanges and Fluxes between Arctic and Atlantic Basins
notes: The Horizon 2020 project traced freshwater and terrestrial dissolved-organic-carbon fluxes from the Arctic Ocean through the Fram Strait into the Atlantic. It integrated oceanographic expeditions, satellite ocean-colour observations and numerical modelling and developed optical approaches for monitoring freshwater and carbon dynamics. The project was completed as research and technology development and did not create a negative-emissions project, regulatory MRV standard or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 November 2019 to 31 October 2021.

document_title: CHARMAD — Chemical Characterisation and Cycling of Marine Dissolved Organic Matter
notes: The FP6 project examined the molecular composition, biological production, degradation, bioavailability and export of marine dissolved organic matter. Advanced chemical and molecular-biological methods were used to determine how dissolved organic carbon is transferred from surface waters to the deep ocean and contributes to one of Earth's largest carbon reservoirs. The project did not establish a microbial engineering deployment, certified methodology or verified removal quantity.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2004 to 28 February 2006.

document_title: DIASIN — Integrative Eco-Mechanics of Diatom Sinking and the Biological Carbon Pump
notes: The FP7 project investigated how diatom physiology, sinking behaviour and small-scale fluid dynamics influence the transfer of photosynthetically fixed carbon from surface waters to the deep ocean. It treated phytoplankton as active participants in the biological carbon pump and linked organism responses with environmental change and biogeochemical cycles. The completed research did not authorize ocean fertilization, biomass sinking or carbon-credit issuance.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2012 to 31 December 2015.

document_title: DIADOM — Interactions between Nitrogen-Fixers and Dissolved Organic Matter in the Ocean
notes: The FP7 project studied autotrophic and heterotrophic marine nitrogen-fixing microorganisms and their interactions with dissolved organic matter in illuminated and dark-ocean environments. It addressed previously unaccounted nitrogen inputs, microbial nutrition and consequences for primary production and ocean carbon cycling. The project was completed as fundamental research and did not constitute nutrient fertilization, engineered carbon removal or a crediting system.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2014 to 29 February 2016.

document_title: PHY-GO — Phytoplankton Community Structure and Carbon Export Using BGC-Argo Floats
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project linked direct measurements of phytoplankton community structure with bio-optical observations from biogeochemical Argo floats. Flow cytometry, optical proxies and machine learning were used to estimate group-specific biomass and evaluate how phytoplankton composition affects carbon export to the mesopelagic ocean. The project was completed as research and did not establish an official MRV methodology, engineered sequestration activity or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2023 to 31 May 2025.

document_title: SEAMLESS — Services Based on Ecosystem Data Assimilation: Essential Science and Solutions
notes: The Horizon 2020 project developed an ecosystem-data-assimilation prototype for the Copernicus Marine Environment Monitoring Service. It integrated satellite, biogeochemical-Argo, glider and model data to improve operational indicators including plankton phenology and particulate carbon export. The project strengthened ocean monitoring and forecasting but did not establish a carbon-removal project, mandatory verification standard or crediting methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2023.

document_title: CONSUMALG — Microbial Uptake and Degradation of Marine Macroalgal Biomass
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project studies microbial degradation of Saccharina latissima and traces carbon flow from kelp biomass into dissolved organic matter and bacterial communities. Multi-omics, isotope tracing and nanoSIMS methods are being used to identify primary and secondary degraders and quantify their contribution to coastal marine carbon cycling. The active project does not constitute macroalgae sinking, a deployment permit, verified removal or carbon-credit issuance.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 February 2026 to 31 January 2028.

document_title: SPICE — Submesoscale Processes in a Changing Environment
notes: The Horizon 2020 project quantified how small-scale upper-ocean processes influence air-sea heat and carbon exchange in the Southern Ocean. It combined autonomous marine robot observations with ultra-high-resolution numerical models to assess carbon flux variability and storage in the ocean interior. The project was completed as research and did not establish engineered removal, a project-level accounting methodology or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 August 2021 to 31 July 2023.

document_title: SO-CHIC — Southern Ocean Carbon and Heat Impact on Climate
notes: The Horizon 2020 project quantified Southern Ocean heat and carbon budgets and the processes controlling exchanges among the atmosphere, ocean and sea ice. It combined dedicated observations, long-term time series and advanced modelling, including study of the Weddell Polynya and implications for global climate projections and stocktakes. The project was completed as coordinated scientific assessment and did not authorize engineered ocean carbon removal or create a crediting mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 November 2019 to 31 October 2024.

document_title: SOCCLI — The Role of the Southern Ocean Carbon Cycle under Climate Change
notes: The FP7 project investigated the physical and biogeochemical processes governing the Southern Ocean carbon sink and its response to climate change. It used observations and modelling to improve understanding of carbon uptake, circulation, ecosystem processes and future feedbacks. The completed project supported climate and ocean-carbon assessment and did not constitute an engineered carbon-removal activity, deployment authorization or carbon-credit programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 August 2012 to 31 July 2016.

document_title: ZINCCARB — Zinc Isotopes as Tracers of Nutrient Cycling and Carbon Uptake by Past Oceans
notes: The FP6 project used zinc isotopes to investigate past nutrient cycling, biological productivity and ocean carbon uptake. It addressed how the biological pump transferred carbon to the deep ocean and influenced atmospheric carbon dioxide during Quaternary climate changes. The project was completed as palaeoceanographic research and did not create an ocean-fertilization activity, monitoring standard or carbon-credit method.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2007 to 31 December 2008.

document_title: LAC — Liquid-Aperture Coulter Counter for Sizing Oceanic Particles and Phytoplankton
notes: The FP7 project developed particle-sizing technology for marine particles and phytoplankton. Particle size affects settling, aggregation, remineralisation, carbon biomass and the efficiency of the biological pump and also determines optical signals used for satellite monitoring. The project was completed as sensor and measurement research and did not establish a statutory MRV standard, engineered sequestration project or verified carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2011 to 28 February 2015.

document_title: SCOOBi — Seeking Constraints on Open Ocean Biocalcification
notes: The European Research Council project investigates environmental and biological controls on calcification by coccolithophores and foraminifera, organisms that convert carbon into calcium carbonate and strongly influence the ocean carbonate system. It combines genetics, metabolomics, physiology, isotope geochemistry and sediment records to quantify modern and past pelagic calcification. The active project does not constitute engineered mineralisation deployment, a carbon-credit methodology or verified removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 December 2022 to 30 November 2027.

document_title: SOSiC — Southern Ocean Silicon Cycling Using Modern and Palaeoceanographic Isotope Records
notes: The Horizon 2020 project investigated silicon cycling and its connection to diatom productivity, biological carbon export and atmospheric carbon dioxide in the Southern Ocean. Modern seawater measurements and high-resolution sediment-core isotope records were used to reconstruct nutrient transport and carbon-cycle changes over the last 150,000 years. The completed project was scientific research and did not authorize ocean fertilization or certify carbon removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2016 to 31 March 2018.

document_title: CARBONSINK — Life beneath the Ocean Floor: The Subsurface Sink of Carbon in the Marine Environment
notes: The European Research Council funded CARBONSINK to determine the fate of dissolved inorganic carbon produced in marine sediments and oceanic crust. The project combined experiments, geochemical measurements and numerical modelling to constrain whether subsurface carbon diffuses back to the ocean or precipitates as carbonate minerals. The research was relevant to evaluating long-term marine subsurface storage, but it did not authorize carbon injection, establish a storage permit or verify an engineered removal project.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 December 2012 to 30 November 2017; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: ECO2 — Sub-Seabed CO2 Storage: Impact on Marine Ecosystems
notes: The FP7 ECO2 project assessed leakage risks and ecological impacts associated with sub-seabed carbon dioxide storage. It examined operating and potential storage sites, applied monitoring technologies, studied natural seep analogues and developed a best-practice guide covering site management, environmental monitoring, remediation and the precautionary principle. The project supported risk assessment and governance of offshore storage but did not itself issue a storage permit or certify stored carbon.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2011 to 30 April 2015; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: RISCS — Research into Impacts and Safety in CO2 Storage
notes: The FP7 RISCS project generated evidence for safe management of geological carbon-storage sites by quantifying the environmental effects of exposure to known carbon dioxide fluxes. Field and laboratory experiments, natural-leakage observations and numerical simulations covered both marine and terrestrial ecosystems and supported environmental-impact assessment over different timescales. The project did not authorize a storage site, approve a marine injection activity or certify stored carbon.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2013; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: EPOCA — European Project on Ocean Acidification
notes: The FP7 EPOCA project documented changes in ocean chemistry and biogeography, reconstructed past variability and quantified biological and ecosystem responses to ocean acidification. It integrated laboratory and field experiments with biogeochemical, sediment and coupled ocean-climate models and assessed risks, thresholds and carbon-cycle feedbacks. The project strengthened the scientific basis for ocean-acidification policy but did not constitute ocean alkalinity enhancement, authorize material addition or verify carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2008 to 30 April 2012; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: SEA-THROUGH — Novel In Situ Imaging Technology to Explore the Ladder of Vertical Migrations to the Deep Sea
notes: The European Research Council funded SEA-THROUGH to develop advanced imaging technology for studying vertically migrating organisms and food-web connectivity from surface waters to depths of up to 6,000 metres. These migrations influence deep-sea biodiversity, organic-carbon transport and the functioning of the deep ocean as a carbon sink. The active project is observational research and does not establish an engineered sequestration pathway, deployment authorization or carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2029.

document_title: REDRESS — Restoration of Deep-Sea Habitats to Rebuild European Seas
notes: The Horizon Europe REDRESS project develops and tests restoration approaches for degraded deep-sea habitats, including sea-pen fields, bamboo corals, coral gardens, cold-water coral reefs, sponge fields and cold seeps. It maps damaged areas and refugia, evaluates active and passive restoration and links ecological outcomes with carbon sequestration, climate mitigation and socio-economic value. The project supports demonstration and policy development but does not itself certify carbon credits or authorize commercial carbon-removal deployment.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 February 2024 to 31 January 2028.

document_title: HEALSEA — Innovative Indicators of Resilience to Protect Seagrass Meadows
notes: The Horizon 2020 HEALSEA project tested ecological indicators intended to provide early warning of declining seagrass resilience. Experimental and theoretical work examined critical slowing down, recovery from disturbance and response trajectories under increasing stress, with the aim of producing practical conservation tools. The project was terminated in 2020 and did not establish a restoration programme, quantify additional carbon removal or issue blue-carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 9 April 2018 to 11 October 2020; CORDIS records termination on 31 August 2020.

document_title: SEGRALCS — Predictive Tool of Seagrass Health for Low-Crested Coastal Structures
notes: The Horizon Europe SEGRALCS project developed a quantitative prediction approach for integrating seagrass health into the design of low-crested coastal structures and breakwaters. It focused on Cymodocea nodosa and Posidonia oceanica and examined hydrodynamic, sediment-transport and ecological effects relevant to conserving Mediterranean seagrass habitats and their carbon-storage function. The project was terminated in 2025 and did not authorize restoration, establish a carbon-credit methodology or verify additional removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2023 to 31 October 2025; CORDIS records termination on 1 January 2025.

document_title: SEAPAID — Seagrass Production and Isotopic Discrimination
notes: The FP6 SEAPAID project studied seagrass production, carbon and nitrogen content and isotopic discrimination in relation to environmental conditions. Isotopic signatures were used to trace carbon and nitrogen flows between source and sink systems and to improve understanding of seagrass ecosystem structure and dynamics. The project was completed as scientific research and did not establish a restoration programme, verified blue-carbon accounting method or crediting mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2004 to 30 September 2006; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: BIOSHARE — Bacterial Interactions in One-Carbon Cycling and the Marine Carbon Cycle
notes: The FP7 BIOSHARE project investigated cooperation among heterotrophic marine bacteria involved in cycling one-carbon compounds and the consequences of these interactions for marine carbon processing. It examined microbial pathways that are usually represented incompletely in ocean-carbon models. The project was completed as fundamental microbiological research and did not establish microbial carbon-removal engineering, a deployment programme or verified carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2014 to 30 April 2017; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: MARINEGLYCAN — Marine Chemical Glycobiology and Molecular Carbon Cycling
notes: The Horizon 2020 MARINEGLYCAN project developed chemical-biology tools for tracing the production, transformation and biological functions of sulfated marine glycans. Because marine microalgae channel substantial carbon into carbohydrates, the project sought molecular-level understanding of carbon flow from individual enzymes to interacting microbial communities. The project was completed as research and did not establish a marine glycan sequestration technology, verified removal quantity or crediting standard.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 August 2021 to 31 July 2023; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: MYCO-CARB — Functional Biology and Ecology of Planktonic Marine Fungi in the Carbon Cycle
notes: The European Research Council funded MYCO-CARB to determine the functional roles of marine planktonic fungi in coastal waters, the open ocean and marine-snow particles. The programme examined fungal biomass, saprotrophic activity and contributions to decomposition, particle processing and the biological carbon pump. The project was completed as fundamental research and did not create a fungal carbon-removal technology, deployment authorization or carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2018 to 31 October 2024; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: M&MS — Monitoring and Managing European Seagrass Beds
notes: The FP5 M&MS project defined habitat requirements, pressures, resilience indicators and recovery processes for European seagrass ecosystems. It combined databases, field surveys and experiments to produce monitoring plans, early-warning indicators and management strategies for seagrass conservation. Although seagrass meadows are blue-carbon habitats, the project did not quantify additional carbon removal, establish a carbon-credit methodology or implement a specific restoration project.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2001 to 30 June 2004; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: SEAMET — Multi-Driver Climate Change Effects on Seagrass Metabolism
notes: The Horizon 2020 SEAMET project investigated how ocean acidification, warming and hypoxia affect carbon incorporation, photosynthetic physiology, metabolic balance and acclimation in seagrasses and associated communities. The project used seagrass as a model habitat for scaling organism-level responses to ecosystem functioning and carbon metabolism. It was completed as scientific research and did not establish a restoration programme, accounting method or verified blue-carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 8 January 2018 to 7 January 2020; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: CAENEUS — Crenarchaeota Ecology and Nutrient Utilisation in the Subsurface Ocean
notes: The FP7 CAENEUS project examined marine Crenarchaeota and bacteria responsible for ammonia oxidation and dark carbon dioxide fixation in the deep Atlantic Ocean. It quantified gene abundance, nitrification and chemoautotrophic carbon-fixation rates across depth gradients and contrasting water masses. The completed research improved understanding of microbial carbon fixation in the dark ocean and did not constitute microbial engineering, deployment authorization or a carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2010 to 31 May 2012; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: SCrIPT — Stable Chromium Isotopes as a Productivity Tracer
notes: The European Research Council funded SCrIPT to develop stable chromium isotopes as a proxy for changes in marine export productivity and the strength of the biological carbon pump. The project combined phytoplankton cultures, water-column observations and sediment analyses to calibrate chromium-isotope fractionation and reconstruct past variations in ocean carbon export. It was completed as scientific proxy development and did not establish an engineered sequestration activity, statutory monitoring method or carbon-credit programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2019 to 30 April 2025; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: GOSAC — Global Ocean Storage of Anthropogenic Carbon
notes: The FP4 GOSAC project compared and validated seven independently developed three-dimensional ocean carbon-cycle models and assessed global anthropogenic carbon storage. It also explored modelled deep-ocean carbon-dioxide disposal scenarios as a potential mitigation option. The completed project produced modelling and intercomparison tools and did not authorize ocean disposal, establish a permit pathway, verify stored carbon or create carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 December 1997 to 31 March 2001.

document_title: DEEPOCEANGLACIALCO2 — Deep-Sea Corals and Southern Ocean Carbon Regulation
notes: The FP7 fellowship used deep-sea corals from the Amundsen sector of the Southern Ocean to test how deep-ocean circulation and ventilation influenced atmospheric carbon dioxide during glacial periods. Geochemical records from coral skeletons were used to reconstruct past water-mass changes and carbon storage. The project was completed as palaeoceanographic research and did not constitute engineered sequestration, a deployment authorization or a carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2008 to 28 February 2010.

document_title: ARCADIA — Archaeal Activity Dynamics in Marine Snow and Ambient Coastal Water
notes: The FP7 project compared archaeal activity in marine-snow particles and surrounding coastal seawater to clarify the contribution of particle-associated archaea to dark-ocean carbon and nutrient budgets. Molecular and activity measurements were used to examine previously underrepresented microbial processes linked to sinking particles and remineralisation. The project was completed as fundamental research and did not establish microbial carbon-removal engineering, a deployment programme or verified removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 15 January 2009 to 14 January 2011.

document_title: PCFLUCS — Plankton Community Structure, Seston Quality and Coastal Carbon Fluxes
notes: The FP6 fellowship quantified coastal pelagic carbon fluxes at the Gullmarsfjord and Río de la Plata, including grazing, predation and downward export by phytoplankton, faecal pellets, carcasses and marine snow. It tested how plankton community structure and seston quality regulate carbon-flow variability at seasonal and sub-seasonal scales. The research did not create an engineered-removal project, mandatory accounting method or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2006 to 31 May 2008. A related return-phase grant used a separate CORDIS identifier and was not added as a second database record to avoid duplicating the same research project.

document_title: PLOCEAN — Plastic Impacts on Ocean Biogeochemical Cycles in the Anthropocene
notes: The Horizon 2020 PLOCEAN project examined how microplastics interact with microbial communities, organic matrices and marine particles and how those interactions may alter carbon turnover, nutrient cycling, primary production and downward particle flux. It combined field observations, polymer characterisation, metagenomics, laboratory studies and citizen science. The project was terminated in 2023 and did not establish a carbon-removal activity, regulatory standard or verified sequestration outcome.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Planned project period: 5 July 2021 to 5 July 2025; CORDIS records termination on 31 August 2023.

document_title: EFFECTIVE — Protection and Restoration Management in Mediterranean Marine Protected Areas
notes: The Horizon Europe EFFECTIVE project applies ecosystem-based management, digital tools and nature-based solutions in four Mediterranean pilot areas. It includes real-environment demonstrations of seabed protection and restoration intended to preserve seabed carbon-sequestration capacity, while assessing legislation, connectivity, participation and social implications. The active project supports restoration and governance development but does not itself certify carbon credits or authorize commercial carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2023 to 31 May 2027.

document_title: RETRO-PUMP — Reconstruction of Global Redox Transitions and the Precambrian Biological Carbon Pump
notes: The European Research Council funded RETRO-PUMP to reconstruct how changes in the Precambrian biological carbon pump influenced ocean redox conditions and long-term carbon burial. The project uses geological records, geochemistry and process modelling to examine the evolution of carbon export and oxygenation over deep time. It is active fundamental research and does not constitute an engineered sequestration project, monitoring standard or carbon-credit mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2030.

document_title: SENSEOCEAN — Marine Sensors for the 21st Century
notes: The FP7 SENSEOCEAN project developed integrated, cost-effective in-situ sensors for marine biogeochemistry, including carbon dioxide and carbonate-system measurements. The programme combined microfabrication, self-calibration, system integration and mass-production approaches to improve large-scale ocean observation. It was completed as sensor research and demonstration and did not establish a statutory MRV requirement, authorize a marine CDR project or certify carbon removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2013 to 30 September 2017.

document_title: CARBON14ARCTIC — Terrestrial Carbon Export to the Eurasian Arctic Shelf
notes: The FP7 project assessed the export, burial and degradation of terrestrial organic carbon released to the Eurasian Arctic Shelf under climate warming. It combined molecular characterisation, compound-specific radiocarbon analysis, water and sediment sampling and dated cores to distinguish black carbon and soil-derived material and quantify their fate. The project was completed as Arctic carbon-cycle research and did not establish engineered sequestration or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2008 to 30 September 2010.

document_title: BiPhySO — Biological and Physical Drivers of Southern Ocean Oxygen Budgets
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project uses dissolved-oxygen and particulate-backscatter sensors together with glider and autonomous-platform datasets from the Ross, Amundsen and Weddell Seas. It will estimate net community production and carbon-export rates and compare biological and physical controls on future Southern Ocean oxygen and carbon budgets. The project began in August 2026 and is scientific observation and modelling rather than engineered removal or credit certification.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 August 2026 to 31 July 2028.

document_title: SIPODET — Simultaneous Chemical Imaging of Coastal Seagrass Microenvironments
notes: The Horizon 2020 SIPODET project proposed simultaneous imaging of several chemicals in Zostera marina and Zostera noltei microenvironments using planar optodes and diffusive-equilibrium thin films. The technology was intended to reveal chemical gradients and stress responses in seagrass ecosystems that provide carbon-sequestration and coastal-protection services. CORDIS contains inconsistent termination and planned-date metadata; the record is therefore treated as ended research and not as completed technology validation or verified blue-carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: CORDIS lists planned dates of 1 June 2020 to 31 May 2022 but also records termination on 21 June 2019; this apparent metadata inconsistency is preserved rather than resolved by inference.

document_title: CRYOMICS — Cryosphere-Ocean Effects on Southern Ocean Microbial Communities
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie CRYOMICS project investigates how freshwater, nutrients, trace metals and carbon released by the melting cryosphere affect phytoplankton, sea-ice algae and microbial communities in the eastern Weddell Gyre. Sampling, biogeochemical analysis and metagenomics are used to assess implications for primary production and biological carbon export. The project was active through August 2026 and did not constitute deliberate fertilization, verified removal or carbon-credit issuance.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2026.

document_title: CEFMED — Climate Effects on Deep-Sea Ecosystem Functioning in the Mediterranean Sea
notes: The FP7 CEFMED project investigated how changes in upper-ocean temperature, stratification, primary production and carbon export affect deep-sea ecosystem functioning in the Mediterranean. It examined food availability, benthic communities and climate-driven shifts in organic-matter supply to the seabed. The project was completed as ecosystem and carbon-cycle research and did not establish a seabed carbon-removal activity, restoration programme or crediting method.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 19 September 2013 to 18 September 2015.

document_title: PHYTOCHANGE — Phytoplankton Responses to Global Change
notes: The European Research Council funded PHYTOCHANGE to assess phytoplankton responses to warming, acidification and other global-change pressures. The project addressed diatom-driven organic-carbon export, coccolithophore control of ocean alkalinity through calcification and nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria as regulators of reactive nitrogen and productivity. It was completed as fundamental and experimental research and did not authorize ocean fertilization, alkalinity enhancement or carbon-credit issuance.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2008 to 31 May 2013.

document_title: ABYSS — Assessment of Bacterial Life and Matter Cycling in Deep-Sea Surface Sediments
notes: The European Research Council funded ABYSS to investigate bacterial communities, organic-matter degradation and element cycling in deep-sea surface sediments. The project combined in-situ flux studies, isotope-labelled substrates, molecular tools and long-term Arctic observations to determine how benthic bacteria remineralise sinking organic matter and how the fraction escaping degradation contributes to geological carbon storage. It was completed as fundamental research and did not establish an engineered sequestration project, carbon-credit methodology or deployment authorization.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2012 to 31 May 2018; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: MICROENERGY — Microbial Life under Extreme Energy Limitation
notes: The European Research Council funded MICROENERGY to examine microbial communities buried in marine sediments and living near the energetic limit for cellular activity. The project focused on methanogenesis, turnover of living and dead microbial biomass, metabolic energy fluxes and the role of subsurface carbon mineralisation in seabed methane cycling. It was completed as fundamental deep-biosphere research and did not establish microbial carbon-removal engineering, a deployment programme or verified carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2012 to 31 March 2017; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: DEEP CARBON FLUX — Energy and Carbon Food Webs of the Deep Sub-Seafloor Biosphere
notes: The FP7 project investigated energetic and kinetic controls on organic-matter mineralisation in deeply buried marine sediments. It developed sensitive analytical methods for small organic acids and linked substrate turnover with sulfate reduction, methanogenesis and microbial energy fluxes across coastal, North Pacific and Baltic sediment systems. The project was completed as research and did not create a sub-seafloor carbon-removal technology, storage authorization or carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2013 to 4 November 2015; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: HADES — Benthic Diagenesis and Microbiology of Hadal Trenches
notes: The European Research Council funded HADES to quantify benthic metabolism and microbial processes in some of the deepest ocean trenches. The project developed autonomous in-situ instrumentation and compared trenches from contrasting ocean settings to determine how organic material is deposited, mineralised and processed by microbial and viral communities. It was completed as deep-sea carbon-cycle research and did not establish a biomass-burial engineering project, deployment authorization or crediting method.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2016 to 31 December 2021; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: HYADES — Hydrostatic Pressure and Prokaryotic Activity in the Deep Sea
notes: The Horizon 2020 project examined how hydrostatic pressure affects prokaryotic activity and organic-matter degradation in the deep ocean. It addressed a mismatch between measured deep-sea microbial carbon demand and the supply of sinking organic carbon, using pressure-controlled experiments and microbial and biogeochemical analyses. The project was completed as research and did not create a microbial sequestration technology, official MRV standard or verified removal claim.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 15 April 2016 to 14 April 2018; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: OCTANT — Chronology of Deep-Ocean Circulation Changes during Abrupt Climate Transitions
notes: The Horizon 2020 project used coupled Earth-system and ice-sheet modelling to investigate the chronology, transport pathways and ventilation changes of the deep ocean during abrupt climate transitions. Because deep-ocean circulation controls the storage and release of large quantities of carbon, the research supported more reliable interpretation of sediment records and future climate projections. It did not constitute engineered ocean storage, a deployment activity or a carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 19 March 2016 to 18 March 2018; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: CACH — Equatorial Atlantic Chemistry, Circulation and Deep-Water Habitat Reconstruction
notes: The European Research Council funded CACH to reconstruct abrupt changes in equatorial Atlantic chemistry, circulation and deep-water habitats using deep-sea coral records, geochemical analyses, field expeditions and modelling. The project examined how ocean circulation stores and releases heat and carbon during major climate transitions. It was completed as palaeoceanographic and ecosystem research and did not establish engineered carbon storage, a permit or a crediting mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2011 to 30 September 2017; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: BIODEM — Biogeochemical and Physical Drivers of Deep European Margin Ecosystems
notes: The FP6 BIODEM project investigated sediment transport, organic-matter inputs, seabed composition, currents and biological communities in Mediterranean canyons and cold-water coral systems. Submarine canyons were treated as major pathways for organic-carbon transport and burial from continental margins to the deep sea. The project supported ecosystem understanding and marine-management decisions and did not establish a carbon-removal intervention, restoration credit or deployment authorization.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2006 to 31 March 2008; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: SOCGDGT — Lipid Proxy for Marine Sediment Oxygen Consumption
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project develops a lipid-based proxy for sediment oxygen consumption using branched glycerol dialkyl glycerol tetraethers produced by benthic marine bacteria. The work links biomarker lipids, oxygen microprofiles, microbial communities and geochemistry to quantify organic-matter degradation and preservation in modern and palaeo marine sediments. The project was active in August 2026 and had not established an official monitoring standard, verified carbon storage or a crediting method.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2026; the project remained active as of 6 August 2026.

document_title: SUBSTRATE USE — Carbon-Cycling Microbes in Anoxic Marine Sediments
notes: The FP7 project investigated how sulfate reducers, methanogens and acetogens consume low-molecular-weight carbon compounds in anoxic marine sediments from Denmark, Mexico and the Bering Sea. Stable-isotope probing linked substrate consumption to microbial identity and clarified how organic matter is remineralised or preserved in the seafloor, one of Earth's largest organic-carbon sinks. The completed project did not create a microbial removal technology, storage permit or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2011 to 31 December 2012; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: CARBON TRANSFER — Trophic Carbon Transfer Efficiency under Carbon Dioxide Stress
notes: The FP6 project tested how increased dissolved carbon dioxide and lower seawater pH alter phytoplankton biochemical composition, carbohydrate release, zooplankton feeding, growth and reproduction. The work assessed whether ocean acidification could change coastal food-web efficiency and the transfer of photosynthetically fixed carbon through marine ecosystems. It was completed as experimental research and did not constitute ocean alkalinity enhancement, engineered removal or a carbon-credit programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2007 to 31 December 2008; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: NAUTILOS — Low-Cost Underwater Technologies for Ocean Observation
notes: The Horizon 2020 NAUTILOS project developed, integrated and demonstrated cost-effective sensors and samplers for essential ocean variables, including inorganic carbon, nutrients, oxygen, phytoplankton and zooplankton. The technologies were deployed from coastal settings to the deep sea and were designed to expand the spatial and temporal coverage of European ocean observations and policy applications. The project strengthened monitoring infrastructure but did not establish a statutory marine CDR MRV standard, authorize deployment or verify carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2020 to 30 June 2025; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: BARIUM — Barium Cycling in Antarctic Waters and Ocean Carbon Storage
notes: The FP7 BARIUM project investigated organic and inorganic carbon storage around the West Antarctic Peninsula using modern and palaeoceanographic barium cycling and isotope measurements. The work linked biological productivity, Southern Ocean circulation, nutrient distribution and carbon uptake across present and past climate conditions. It was completed as proxy and carbon-cycle research and did not establish an engineered sequestration activity, official accounting method or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2012 to 30 September 2016; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: ECoCT — Carbon Transformation during Serpentinization in the Oceanic Lithosphere
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project recreates seawater-rock interactions beneath the ocean floor to investigate carbon transformation, migration and reactivity during serpentinization. Open-system experiments, chemical analysis, microstructural characterisation and three-dimensional imaging are intended to clarify how abiotic and biological processes influence carbon storage in oceanic rocks and inform future storage technologies. The project was active in August 2026 and did not authorize injection, certify mineralised carbon or establish a commercial storage pathway.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2026; the project remained active as of 6 August 2026.

document_title: MANGROVE — Ecosystem, Community and Conflict Management in Southeast Asian Mangroves
notes: The FP6 project assessed mangrove ecosystem functions, adjacent coastal areas, household livelihoods, institutions, legislation, stakeholder values and conflicts at sites in Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam. It developed participatory monitoring methods and implemented stakeholder action plans intended to reconcile conservation and resource-use demands. The project did not quantify blue-carbon removal, establish a carbon-credit methodology or report verified sequestration; it is included as foundational governance and management research for a major coastal blue-carbon ecosystem.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 August 2005 to 30 June 2010; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: Environmental Change Effects on European Salt Marsh Structure, Functioning and Coastal Exchange
notes: The European research project examined how environmental change alters the structure and functioning of salt marshes and their exchanges with adjacent coastal waters. It assessed organic and inorganic matter, sediment, nutrient and particulate-organic-matter transfers and sought management criteria for maintaining salt-marsh functions. The project provided foundational evidence for a major coastal blue-carbon habitat, but it did not implement restoration, quantify additional carbon removal or establish a crediting methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 1993 to 30 June 1995; the project is closed.

document_title: Influence of Rising Sea Level on Ecosystem Dynamics of Salt Marshes
notes: The project investigated whether European salt marshes can persist under accelerated sea-level rise by analysing inundation, sediment accretion, surface elevation and interactions between physical and biological processes. The work supported understanding of salt-marsh resilience and future restoration requirements. It was a scientific research project and did not itself restore marshes, certify carbon sequestration or create blue-carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 February 1998 to 31 January 2001; the project is closed.

document_title: STORM — Stemming the Rising Tide: The Protective Role of Saltmarshes
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project examined the capacity of salt marshes to keep pace with sea-level rise and reduce wave energy. It linked sediment accretion, below-ground root growth, organic-matter accumulation and vegetation structure with coastal-protection performance. The completed research strengthened the evidence base for salt-marsh conservation and restoration, but it did not quantify additional carbon removal, approve a restoration project or issue credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2016; the project is closed.

document_title: ForCry — Analysing Frozen Foraminifera by Cryostage LA-ICPMS
notes: The European Research Council project develops cryogenic laser-ablation methods and boron-isotope measurements in foraminifera to improve reconstructions of seawater pH, atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon fluxes during the Neogene. The work strengthens carbonate-system proxies and long-term understanding of ocean carbon-cycle sensitivity. It is active research and does not constitute engineered mineralisation, an official carbon-accounting method or verified carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2022 to 31 May 2027.

document_title: CD-PALEO — Cadmium Isotope Measurements for Marine Sediments and Palaeoceanography
notes: The FP6 project developed cadmium-isotope measurements using a double-spike MC-ICP-MS approach and applied them to marine sediments and palaeoceanography. Cadmium distributions and isotopes provide information on nutrient utilisation, biological productivity, circulation and carbon-cycle changes. The project was completed as analytical and proxy research and did not establish a statutory monitoring requirement, engineered sequestration activity or carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 December 2004 to 30 November 2006; the project is closed.

document_title: VARIO — Natural pH Variability and Ecosystem Response to Ocean Acidification
notes: The Horizon 2020 project was designed to test how natural pH variability affects the response of rhodolith-bed organisms and ecosystems to ocean acidification in Scotland and Greenland. The proposed work included field observations and experiments on calcification, physiology and ecosystem sensitivity. CORDIS records termination before the planned start date, so the record is treated as ended and does not imply completed experiments, an alkalinity intervention or verified carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: CORDIS lists planned dates of 1 August 2019 to 31 July 2021 and records termination on 23 May 2019; the metadata inconsistency is preserved without inference.

document_title: DEstiNi — Dynamic Estuarine and Marine Cycling of Nickel
notes: The Horizon 2020 project investigated nickel cycling and isotope behaviour across estuarine, coastal and marine systems. It linked micronutrient supply, biological uptake, particle transport and sediment preservation with primary production and export carbon, including information from salt-marsh sediment cores. The completed project improved marine-carbon proxy interpretation but did not establish an official accounting method, restoration programme or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2019 to 22 August 2023; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: DINOPRO — Dinoflagellates as Proxies for Climate and Carbon Cycling
notes: The European Research Council project developed dinoflagellate-based signals for reconstructing climate, carbon cycling, surface-ocean carbon dioxide and acidification during past and present rapid carbon-cycle transitions. Culture experiments, carbon-isotope analysis and geological records were used to evaluate proxy performance. The project was completed as palaeoclimate research and did not establish engineered carbon removal, a regulatory accounting standard or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2010 to 31 August 2016; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: IsoMargin — Isotopes of Micronutrients to Trace Margin Sediment Fluxes
notes: The Horizon Europe project used copper, nickel and zinc isotopes to trace micronutrient fluxes from continental-margin sediments to the ocean. These micronutrients influence phytoplankton growth and the biological carbon pump, while isotope measurements help distinguish sedimentary sources and transformations. The project was completed as proxy and process research and did not establish a mandatory MRV method, engineered removal activity or carbon-credit system.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2022 to 30 September 2024; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: MixOCarb — The Role of Mixotrophs in the Oceanic Carbon Cycle
notes: The FP7 project investigated organisms that combine photosynthesis and consumption of organic matter and assessed how mixotrophy changes production, respiration and carbon transfer in marine food webs. The research used molecular, physiological and single-cell methods to quantify diversity and activity and improve representation of mixotrophs in ocean-carbon models. It was completed as fundamental research and did not establish microbial carbon-removal engineering or verified removal credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2018; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: WET HORIZONS — Fast-Tracking Wetland Restoration across Europe
notes: The Horizon Europe project upgrades knowledge and practical tools for restoring European wetlands, including coastal wetlands, while assessing carbon sequestration, greenhouse-gas emissions, biodiversity and ecosystem services. It develops restoration guidance, spatial information, decision-support tools and policy dialogue intended to accelerate implementation. The project was active as of 6 August 2026 and does not by itself certify carbon credits or prove permanent project-level removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2022 to 31 August 2026; the project remained active as of 6 August 2026.

document_title: RESTORE4Cs — Restoring Wetlands for Carbon Pathways and Climate Benefits
notes: The Horizon Europe project assessed European coastal-wetland restoration through pilot sites, harmonised measurements, remote sensing, modelling and machine learning. It developed standardised methods and decision-support tools for evaluating carbon storage, greenhouse-gas abatement, biodiversity, ecosystem services and restoration priorities. The project closed in 2025. Its outputs support planning and accounting, but the funding record does not itself issue carbon credits or certify permanent additional removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2025; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: ECOTIP — Arctic Biodiversity Change and Ecosystem Tipping Cascades
notes: The Horizon 2020 ECOTIP project assessed how climate-driven tipping cascades affect Arctic marine biodiversity, ecosystem functioning, carbon sequestration and dependent human systems. It integrated observations, experiments, ecological models, monitoring indicators and engagement with Indigenous and local communities. The completed project supported international governance and adaptation planning but did not establish an engineered carbon-removal activity, project-level MRV method or crediting programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2020 to 31 May 2024; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

subnational_area: Southern Patagonia and West Antarctic Peninsula
document_title: CoastCarb — Coastal Ecosystem Carbon Balance in Times of Rapid Glacier Melt
notes: The Horizon 2020 CoastCarb network examined carbon budgets and flows in fjord and estuarine ecosystems of Southern Patagonia and the West Antarctic Peninsula. It integrated benthic and pelagic food webs, microbial processes, ecosystem modelling, open data and stakeholder analysis to understand climate-mitigation services under rapid glacier melt and human pressure. The project closed in 2025 and did not establish engineered removal, a crediting method or verified additional sequestration.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2020 to 31 July 2025; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: FROM — Functional Redundancy of the Global Ocean Microbiome
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project evaluated functional redundancy in the global ocean microbiome by integrating taxonomic, genomic, environmental and dispersal information. It assessed how microbial communities maintain biogeochemical functions despite changes in species composition and environmental conditions. The project was completed as foundational marine-microbiome research. It did not directly quantify carbon sequestration, test a negative-emissions intervention or establish a carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2024; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

subnational_area: National mangrove, seagrass and coastal-wetland ecosystems
document_title: Blue Carbon Ecosystems NDC Implementation and Investment Plan 2025–2035 — Final Plan
notes: The Government of Kenya officially launched the final Blue Carbon Ecosystems NDC Implementation and Investment Plan 2025–2035 at the eleventh Our Ocean Conference. The plan consolidates blue-carbon obligations across the 2020–2030 and 2031–2035 NDC cycles into an actionable national investment framework for mangroves, seagrasses and coastal wetlands. It includes restoration and conservation targets, a national MRV architecture, high-integrity carbon accounting aligned with Paris Agreement Article 6, benefit-sharing and institutional coordination measures, and a financing architecture intended to mobilize approximately USD 620 million by 2035. The plan is an implementation and investment framework rather than a project permit; individual restoration, market and infrastructure activities remain subject to applicable approvals and safeguards.
source: Government of Kenya — Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Forestry; Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs
status_note: Officially launched at the eleventh Our Ocean Conference in June 2026; implementation period 2025–2035

document_title: Influencing Climate Policy and Blue Carbon Ecosystems Conservation in Kenya
notes: This Pew- and Fauna & Flora-supported project is designed to increase recognition of mangroves and seagrass ecosystems in Kenyan climate, environment and natural-capital policy processes. Its formal work programme covers stakeholder-validated policy mapping, creation of a national Blue Carbon Working Group, policy advocacy, awareness raising and capacity building for civil society and coastal stakeholders. Expected outcomes include stronger NDC reporting capability, improved institutional coordination and mainstreaming of blue carbon into national accounting and legislative processes. The project supports policy development and conservation governance; it does not itself establish a carbon-credit registry, issue credits or authorize a restoration project.
source: East African Wild Life Society; Fauna & Flora; The Pew Charitable Trusts
status_note: Active project running from January 2025 through August 2026

subnational_area: Pan-African research, governance and innovation network
document_title: Africa’s Roadmap for Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal — From Roadmap to Action
notes: The roadmap process links African marine carbon dioxide removal research with entrepreneurship, sustainable development, governance, community participation and regional capacity building. It emerged from workshops involving participants from thirteen African countries and was further developed through the 2025 WIOMSA special session and post-symposium workshop. The framework prioritizes baseline observations, robust MRV, small and well-monitored pilots, environmental safeguards, benefit-sharing, local-language communication, curriculum and certification development, and alignment with national and regional climate strategies. It is a collaborative research and governance roadmap, not a continent-wide deployment authorization or carbon-crediting standard.
source: Ocean Visions; African academic institutions; WIOMSA partners; Ocean-Climate Innovation Hubs
status_note: Roadmap-development and capacity-building process active following the 2025 WIOMSA sessions

subnational_area: Wellington, New Zealand, with priority for researchers from ODA-recipient countries
document_title: EquiSea 2026 Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal Scientific Cohort
notes: The Ocean Science Equity Initiative convened a funded scientific cohort for mCDR capacity-building workshops and participation in the Ocean in a High-CO2 World Symposium in Wellington. The programme provides travel support, scientific training, project-design tools, networking, mentorship and cross-regional knowledge exchange, with priority for applicants from official-development-assistance recipient countries and other underrepresented regions. The cohort is intended to broaden the geographic and institutional base of mCDR research; it does not fund field deployment, create a permitting pathway or validate a specific removal method.
source: The Ocean Foundation — Ocean Science Equity Initiative (EquiSea); ClimateWorks Foundation; Government Offices of Sweden
status_note: Applications closed on 15 July 2026; workshops and symposium participation scheduled for 12–16 October 2026

subnational_area: Priority for applicants outside Europe, the United States, Canada and Australia
document_title: EquiSea Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal Travel Award — 2026 Rolling Call
notes: EquiSea provides rolling travel grants for participation in mCDR-relevant conferences, symposia and meetings. The call prioritizes researchers from regions that remain underrepresented in the mCDR community and is intended to strengthen access to technical knowledge, professional networks and scientific collaboration. Awards support participation and capacity building only; they do not finance carbon-removal deployment, issue research permits or endorse a particular mCDR pathway.
source: The Ocean Foundation — Ocean Science Equity Initiative (EquiSea); ClimateWorks Foundation
status_note: Rolling applications accepted in 2026 through 15 November 2026

document_title: New Jersey Natural Climate Solutions Grant Program — Round 2 Blue Carbon Funding
notes: New Jersey opened a USD 30 million second round of Natural Climate Solutions grants, with USD 15 million reserved for blue-carbon projects and USD 15 million for green-carbon projects. Eligible coastal activities include living shorelines, restoration of tidal flows, tidal-wetland and salt-marsh vegetation restoration, seagrass or submerged-aquatic-vegetation restoration, and other on-the-ground measures that create or enhance natural carbon sinks. Funding is derived from Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative auction proceeds and is awarded to eligible local governments and nonprofit organizations. The grant programme funds implementation but does not replace coastal permits, environmental review or site-specific carbon-accounting requirements.
source: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection
status_note: Round 2 announced on 29 July 2025 with rolling admission for remaining funds

subnational_area: Scotch Bonnet Island, Stone Harbor, Cape May County, New Jersey
document_title: Natural Climate Solutions Grant Award — Scotch Bonnet Island Tidal Wetland Restoration
notes: The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection awarded The Wetlands Institute nearly USD 2.75 million under the Natural Climate Solutions programme to restore tidal-wetland vegetation on Scotch Bonnet Island near the Cape May Coastal Wetlands Wildlife Management Area. The award supports on-the-ground enhancement of a coastal carbon sink and associated habitat and resilience benefits. The grant is a project-funding decision; construction and restoration activities remain subject to applicable site approvals, engineering design and environmental safeguards.
source: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection; The Wetlands Institute
status_note: Grant award announced on 19 December 2025

subnational_area: Popular Point, Stafford Township, Ocean County, New Jersey
document_title: Natural Climate Solutions Grant Award — Stafford Resiliency Program at Popular Point
notes: New Jersey awarded USD 5 million to Stafford Township for restoration of approximately 23 acres of tidal salt marsh at Popular Point. The project is intended to strengthen natural defenses against sea-level rise and storm surge, enhance wildlife habitat and increase blue-carbon storage. It was identified through the Resilient Stafford planning process and is now supported as an implementation project under the Natural Climate Solutions programme. The award does not itself quantify verified carbon removals or create transferable carbon credits.
source: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection; Stafford Township
status_note: Grant award announced on 19 December 2025

subnational_area: Global field sites, with explicit interest in Global South applicants
document_title: Global Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement Field Research Network — USD 5 Million RFP
notes: Carbon to Sea announced a USD 5 million request for proposals to expand a coordinated global network of ocean alkalinity enhancement field-research sites. The call supports field sites, technical demonstrations and international collaboration to generate real-world evidence on environmental thresholds, removal efficiency, MRV uncertainty, feedstocks, dispersal methods, industry integration, permitting pathways and community engagement. The opportunity encourages hub and consortium proposals and seeks broader participation from the Global South. It is a research-funding call and does not provide regulatory authorization for OAE deployment.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative
status_note: RFP announced on 17 June 2026 for launch in July 2026

subnational_area: Municipal wastewater systems and coastal discharge settings
document_title: Study on Integrating Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement into Municipal Wastewater Treatment Systems
notes: Carbon to Sea awarded USD 225,000 to a cross-sector research team to assess integration of ocean alkalinity enhancement and wastewater alkalinity enhancement with municipal treatment systems. The technical report will examine geographic feasibility, climate impacts, operational requirements, biogeochemical modelling, life-cycle emissions, costs, co-benefits and five international case studies, while incorporating interviews with utilities and project developers. The work is intended to provide foundational evidence for future pilots and policy dialogue. It is an assessment project and does not authorize municipal discharge modifications or claim verified carbon removal from future integrations.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science and project partners
status_note: USD 225,000 award announced on 23 July 2026; final technical report under development

subnational_area: Canada, headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia
document_title: Carbon to Sea Canada — National Ocean-Based Carbon Removal Research and Governance Initiative
notes: Carbon to Sea launched a Canadian entity headquartered in Halifax to expand support for ocean alkalinity enhancement and related ocean-based carbon-removal research. The initiative is intended to fund research, field demonstrations, MRV development, governance work, public transparency and collaboration with Canadian researchers, innovators, communities and Indigenous partners. The launch followed more than USD 15 million in prior grants and research funding in Nova Scotia. The organization is a science-led nonprofit initiative rather than a federal regulatory programme, and its support does not replace research permits or government approval.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative / Carbon to Sea Canada
status_note: Canadian entity formally launched in Halifax on 29 April 2026

document_title: Carbon to Sea 2026 Research Fellowship Program Cohort
notes: The second Carbon to Sea research-fellowship cohort supports four workstreams covering OAE efficiency and scalability, MRV, environmental impacts, and social and community impacts. Fellows will synthesize evidence, update a public MRV database, assess ecosystem effects across laboratory and field research, and develop a framework for monitoring social impacts. The programme informs the initiative’s R&D roadmap and future grant priorities. It is a knowledge-building programme and does not certify OAE performance or authorize field deployment.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative
status_note: Second fellowship cohort announced on 27 April 2026

subnational_area: Halifax Harbour and Bedford Basin, Nova Scotia
document_title: Beyond Toxicity: Impacts of OAE on a Subarctic Zooplankton Community
notes: The award supports research on how realistic ocean alkalinity enhancement exposures affect a subarctic zooplankton community at the Halifax learning site. The project will generate ecological-response evidence needed to identify potential risks and safe operating conditions. It is an experimental research award and does not constitute approval for commercial OAE deployment.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; MEOPAR; Planetary Technologies and named grantee institutions
status_note: Award announced on 28 April 2026; project scheduled from May through autumn 2026, with results expected in early 2027

subnational_area: Halifax Harbour and Bedford Basin, Nova Scotia
document_title: How to Evaluate and Monitor Benthic Impacts at an OAE Point-Source Addition Site
notes: The funded project develops and tests approaches for evaluating and monitoring benthic impacts near an OAE point-source addition site. Its purpose is to improve site-level environmental assessment and monitoring design for future research and demonstration activities. The project creates evidence and methods but does not establish a binding monitoring standard.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; MEOPAR; Planetary Technologies and named grantee institutions
status_note: Award announced on 28 April 2026; project scheduled from May through autumn 2026, with results expected in early 2027

subnational_area: Halifax Harbour and Bedford Basin, Nova Scotia
document_title: Assessing N2O and Trace-Metal Feedbacks from OAE in Halifax Harbour
notes: This award investigates nitrous-oxide and trace-metal feedbacks associated with OAE research in Halifax Harbour. The work addresses potential secondary greenhouse-gas effects and chemical risks that could influence net climate benefit and environmental safety. It is a research assessment and does not quantify certified removals or authorize scale-up.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; MEOPAR; Planetary Technologies and named grantee institutions
status_note: Award announced on 28 April 2026; project scheduled from May through autumn 2026, with results expected in early 2027

subnational_area: Halifax Harbour and Bedford Basin, Nova Scotia
document_title: Quantifying Alkalinity-Driven Biogeochemical and Microbial Responses in Halifax Harbour through Continuous In Situ Measurements
notes: The project funds continuous in-situ measurements to quantify biogeochemical and microbial responses to alkalinity additions in Halifax Harbour. It will strengthen understanding of carbon-cycle behaviour, ecological response and monitoring requirements under realistic field conditions. Results are intended for research and MRV development rather than immediate deployment certification.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; MEOPAR; Planetary Technologies and named grantee institutions
status_note: Award announced on 28 April 2026; project scheduled from May through autumn 2026, with results expected in early 2027

subnational_area: Halifax Harbour and Bedford Basin, Nova Scotia
document_title: Assessing the Biological Impact of OAE on Plankton Communities in Halifax Harbour
notes: The funded study examines biological responses of plankton communities to OAE conditions at the Halifax research site. It is designed to identify potential ecosystem effects and improve the evidence base for responsible field research. The award does not establish ecological safety thresholds as binding rules or authorize commercial deployment.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; MEOPAR; Planetary Technologies and named grantee institutions
status_note: Award announced on 28 April 2026; project scheduled from May through autumn 2026, with results expected in early 2027

subnational_area: Halifax Harbour and Bedford Basin, Nova Scotia
document_title: Integrating First Nations Knowledge and Concerns into Monitoring Frameworks for OAE
notes: The project supports co-development of OAE monitoring approaches that incorporate First Nations knowledge, priorities and concerns. It is intended to strengthen community participation, social safeguards and the legitimacy of monitoring frameworks for field research in Mi’kma’ki. The award does not create a government consultation rule or substitute for formal rights-holder consent and regulatory processes.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; MEOPAR; Planetary Technologies and named grantee institutions
status_note: Award announced on 28 April 2026; project scheduled from May through autumn 2026, with results expected in early 2027

subnational_area: Halifax Harbour and Bedford Basin, Nova Scotia
document_title: Assessing OAE Effects on the Partitioning and Speciation of Metals in Coastal Systems
notes: This research award evaluates how OAE may alter the partitioning and chemical speciation of metals in coastal waters. The work addresses potential environmental-risk pathways and helps define measurements needed for responsible experimentation. It is an evidence-building project and does not itself set regulatory concentration limits.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; MEOPAR; Planetary Technologies and named grantee institutions
status_note: Award announced on 28 April 2026; project scheduled from May through autumn 2026, with results expected in early 2027

subnational_area: Halifax Harbour and Bedford Basin, Nova Scotia
document_title: Turning OAE Research into Storytelling for Climate Impact
notes: The project translates OAE field research into accessible climate storytelling and public-facing communication. It supports responsible-sector development by improving public understanding of research goals, uncertainties and potential impacts. The award is a communication and knowledge-exchange activity; it does not provide evidence of removal performance or authorize deployment.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; MEOPAR; Planetary Technologies and named grantee institutions
status_note: Award announced on 28 April 2026; project scheduled from May through autumn 2026, with results expected in early 2027

subnational_area: Halifax Harbour and Bedford Basin, Nova Scotia
document_title: Investigating Optimal Field Observing for MRV through Novel and Affordable Carbonate-System Sensors
notes: The funded project tests novel and lower-cost carbonate-system sensors and field-observing strategies for OAE MRV in Halifax Harbour. It aims to improve measurement coverage, data quality and affordability for future field trials. The project develops monitoring evidence and tools but does not constitute an approved certification methodology.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; MEOPAR; Planetary Technologies and named grantee institutions
status_note: Award announced on 28 April 2026; project scheduled from May through autumn 2026, with results expected in early 2027

subnational_area: University of Otago; Pacific-region marine species
document_title: Response of Key Ecosystem Species to Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement in the Pacific Region
notes: This 24-month funded project examines realistic OAE exposures across culturally and ecologically important Pacific species, including mussels, cockles, sea cucumbers, sea urchins, abalone and kelp. Short-term experiments are designed to generate Southern Hemisphere evidence on potential effects during sensitive life stages and across different ecological functions. The research supports environmental-risk assessment and does not authorize field deployment or assume that ecological effects will be negligible.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation; University of Otago
status_note: Research award announced on 21 May 2026 for a 24-month project

subnational_area: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution; north-western Atlantic species
document_title: Physiological Impacts of Realistic OAE Exposures on Early Life Stages of American Lobster and Tautog
notes: This 24-month research award evaluates physiological responses and sensitive thresholds in early life stages of American lobster and tautog under realistic OAE exposures using sodium hydroxide as the alkalinity source. The project focuses on species of commercial and recreational importance and is intended to fill evidence gaps on higher-trophic-level ecological effects. It is an environmental assessment study and does not establish deployment limits or certify the safety of sodium-hydroxide-based OAE.
source: Carbon to Sea Initiative; Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation; Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
status_note: Research award announced on 21 May 2026 for a 24-month project

subnational_area: EU coastal and marine blue-carbon ecosystems
document_title: Nature Credits for Blue Carbon Ecosystems — The Role of Geodata to Bridge Science, Policy and Finance
notes: This European Commission Maritime Forum publication examines how geospatial data can connect scientific evidence, public policy and finance in the development of nature-credit approaches for blue-carbon ecosystems. The document contributes to discussion of ecosystem mapping, monitoring, project integrity and the information needed to link restoration outcomes with financial instruments. It is an exploratory publication and does not create an EU nature-credit registry, certification methodology or compliance-market eligibility rule.
source: European Commission — Directorate-General for Maritime Affairs and Fisheries / Maritime Forum
status_note: General publication released on 30 January 2026

document_title: Roadmap towards Nature Credits — Feedback and Next Steps for Coastal and Marine Ecosystems
notes: This European Commission Maritime Forum publication records feedback and next steps for a nature-credit roadmap discussed in the context of coastal and marine ecosystems and the EU blue-carbon workstream. It supports policy learning on how future nature-credit systems could connect restoration outcomes, evidence requirements and finance.
