The project improves observation and modeling infrastructure rather than implementing marine carbon removal. It does not create a mandatory MRV system, verify project-induced uptake or issue carbon credits.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Ocean Acidification Program
status_note: NOAA research award funded during fiscal years 2023–2025; the official project page does not report administrative closure.

document_title: Blue Carbon Ecosystems in Japan's NDC and Its Implementation
notes: This official Ministry of the Environment presentation to the 2026 UNFCCC Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue explains how Japan incorporates coastal wetlands and blue carbon into its NDC, greenhouse-gas inventory and domestic implementation system. It reports national estimation of removals from seagrass meadows and seaweed beds, continued methodology development for offshore blue carbon, institutional arrangements for data collection, local ecosystem initiatives and the role of J Blue Credit. The presentation also identifies expected blue-carbon contributions within Japan's 2035 and 2040 climate-planning framework and discusses possible future seaweed cultivation and deep-sea sequestration research. It is an official policy explanation, not a new permit or methodology, and it does not itself issue credits or authorize offshore deployment.
source: Ministry of the Environment, Japan / United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Official national presentation delivered at the UNFCCC Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue on 10 June 2026, describing active NDC and inventory implementation.

document_title: SAP049: Sustainable Communities for Climate Action in the Yucatán Peninsula (ACCIÓN)
notes: The Green Climate Fund approved ACCIÓN to finance locally led ecosystem-based adaptation across coastal and marine landscapes of the Yucatán Peninsula. The programme covers ecosystems including mangroves and seagrasses that provide coastal protection, biodiversity benefits and carbon sequestration, and will support ten community-level subprojects, sustainable productive practices, knowledge sharing and mobilisation of additional finance. Project-preparation work also examined financial structures for conservation and restoration, including a possible blue-carbon market mechanism. The approved project is primarily an adaptation and community-resilience programme rather than a carbon-credit project. It does not establish a national blue-carbon methodology, register offsets, quantify additional project-level removals or guarantee that individual subprojects will generate tradable credits.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF) / Fondo Mexicano para la Conservación de la Naturaleza
status_note: Approved by the GCF Board on 20 February 2025 and under implementation following effectiveness on 13 August 2025, with completion scheduled for February 2035.

document_title: FP235: Mangroves for Climate — Public, Private and Community Partnerships for Mitigation and Adaptation in Ecuador
notes: FP235 uses public, private and community partnerships to protect, restore and sustainably manage Ecuadorian mangroves while reducing climate vulnerability and emissions associated with ecosystem loss. The programme works with community custodians and shrimp producers, promotes deforestation-free and legally compliant aquaculture, supports active reforestation, strengthens governance and provides results-based payments linked to measurable environmental outcomes. GCF reports a total project value of USD 45.9 million and an anticipated 4.6 million tonnes of carbon-dioxide-equivalent mitigation. The project is under implementation and has received disbursements, but anticipated mitigation is not equivalent to verified carbon-credit issuance. The programme does not itself create a separate national registry or automatically convert restored hectares into tradable offsets.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF) / Conservation International Foundation / Government of Ecuador
status_note: Approved on 18 July 2024, effective from 15 August 2024 and under implementation through August 2030; GCF recorded additional disbursement in January 2026.

document_title: SAP025: Adaptation of Agricultural Production Systems in Coastal Areas of Northwest Guinea-Bissau
notes: SAP025 supports climate-resilient livelihoods and food security in coastal Guinea-Bissau through improved water and soil monitoring, rehabilitation of small-scale water-management systems, climate-adapted agriculture, microenterprise support and functional reforestation of approximately 250 hectares of mangrove swamp. The project responds to seawater intrusion, sea-level rise and tidal surges that threaten mangrove-dependent production systems and coastal communities. It is primarily an adaptation programme, but mangrove reforestation also protects and rebuilds a coastal carbon store. The official project page does not identify an approved carbon-accounting methodology, quantified additional removals, a carbon-rights arrangement or credit issuance. Carbon benefits therefore remain an ecosystem co-benefit that requires separate monitoring and accounting if used for mitigation claims.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF) / Sahara and Sahel Observatory
status_note: Approved on 20 October 2022 and under implementation since September 2023, with project completion scheduled for September 2028.

document_title: FP013: Improving the Resilience of Vulnerable Coastal Communities to Climate Change Related Impacts in Viet Nam
notes: FP013 combined resilient housing, coastal risk assessment and the planting or rehabilitation of approximately 4,000 hectares of mangroves to reduce storm and flood exposure in Viet Nam. The programme also strengthened public- and private-sector climate-risk assessment across the country's coastal provinces and supported ecosystem resources used by local communities. GCF reports an anticipated 1.9 million tonnes of carbon-dioxide-equivalent mitigation over the project lifespan, reflecting the climate value of restored mangrove systems. The project is now completed, but anticipated mitigation figures are not equivalent to a project-level crediting decision. The programme did not establish a transferable blue-carbon methodology, document a separate offset registry or report issuance of carbon credits from the restored mangrove areas.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF) / United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) / Government of Viet Nam
status_note: Approved on 30 June 2016, implemented from July 2017 and recorded by GCF as completed on 11 July 2024; a final evaluation was published in 2025.

document_title: FP084: Enhancing Climate Resilience of India's Coastal Communities
notes: FP084 supports protection and restoration of mangroves, seagrasses and other coastal ecosystems across twenty-four target ecosystems in twelve Indian coastal districts. The programme combines ecosystem restoration with climate-adaptive livelihoods and value chains and is designed to preserve coastal protection and carbon-sequestration services over a long restoration lifespan. GCF reports an anticipated 3.7 million tonnes of carbon-dioxide-equivalent mitigation and more than eleven million people with increased resilience. The project is a large public climate-finance programme rather than a blue-carbon offset scheme. Its portfolio-level mitigation estimate does not establish site-level additionality, permanence or ownership, and the official project page does not report registration under a carbon standard or issuance of tradable credits.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF) / United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) / Government of India
status_note: Approved on 20 October 2018 and under implementation since June 2019, with the current GCF timeline extending to June 2027.

document_title: FP157: Coastal Resilience to Climate Change in Cuba through Ecosystem-Based Adaptation — MI COSTA
notes: MI COSTA applies ecosystem-based adaptation to reduce flooding and sea-level-rise risks in vulnerable Cuban coastal municipalities. The programme restores mangroves, swamp forests and grass swamps and seeks to improve the condition of connected seagrass beds and coral reefs, while training coastal residents in ecosystem protection and climate adaptation. These activities protect and rebuild natural coastal carbon stores, although the project's principal approved result is adaptation and resilience for more than one million people. The GCF portfolio does not present MI COSTA as a carbon-credit programme and does not report a verified volume of additional blue-carbon removals. Restoration outcomes, carbon stocks and durability therefore require project monitoring and should not be interpreted as issued or transferable offsets.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF) / United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) / Government of Cuba
status_note: Approved on 19 March 2021 and under implementation since September 2021, with completion scheduled for September 2029.

document_title: SAP036: Sierra Leone Coastal Resilience Project
notes: The Sierra Leone Coastal Resilience Project finances locally led adaptation, climate-resilient livelihoods, improved water and sanitation, sustainable natural-resource management and conservation and restoration of mangroves. Mangrove activities address coastal erosion, saline intrusion and ecosystem degradation while maintaining habitat and a natural coastal carbon store. The project is explicitly structured as an adaptation and resilience programme, not as a blue-carbon credit project. Its official GCF description does not specify a project-level carbon baseline, expected net removals, permanence arrangements, carbon rights or a registry pathway. Any future mitigation claim associated with restored mangroves would require separate measurement and accounting. The programme's approved finance therefore supports implementation but does not itself constitute carbon-credit certification or issuance.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF) / Save the Children Australia / Government of Sierra Leone
status_note: Approved by the GCF Board on 6 March 2024 and under implementation since December 2024, with completion scheduled for December 2029.

subnational_area: Antigua and Barbuda, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Suriname, and Trinidad and Tobago
document_title: Blue Co Caribbean Umbrella Coordination Programme — GCF Project Preparation Facility
notes: The Green Climate Fund approved project-preparation support for the Caribbean Development Bank to develop the Blue Co Caribbean Umbrella Coordination Programme. The proposed regional mechanism is intended to build a long-term pipeline of low-emission, climate-resilient blue-economy investments, create regional and multi-country coordination frameworks and prepare scalable projects for public and private finance. Subsequent programme development has considered project concepts ranging from coastal ecosystem investments and blue-carbon credits from seagrass to other climate-resilient blue-economy activities. This record concerns preparation funding rather than approval of a full investment programme. It does not establish a regional carbon market, approve individual projects, verify carbon removals or guarantee that the proposed GCF funding proposal will be approved.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF) / Caribbean Development Bank
status_note: GCF approved the project-preparation funding application in November 2023; programme design, feasibility analysis and preparation of a full funding proposal have continued through later procurement and pipeline work.

document_title: Blue Halo S — Blue Ecosystem Adaptation Mechanism (BEAM) Project Preparation Facility
notes: The GCF Project Preparation Facility supports development of Indonesia's Blue Halo S Blue Ecosystem Adaptation Mechanism. The initiative seeks to create a climate-responsive blue economy by financing locally led adaptation, mitigation and investment-readiness measures, improving marine protected-area management and supporting protection and rehabilitation of blue-carbon ecosystems. The preparation package includes baseline studies, stakeholder engagement, financial and economic analysis, implementation arrangements and an environmental and social management framework, while also informing a prospective blue-bond financing structure. This is a preparation and enabling-mechanism record rather than approval of a full GCF investment project. It does not authorize specific restoration sites, establish a national blue-carbon methodology, quantify verified removals or issue carbon credits or bonds.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF) / Conservation International / Government of Indonesia
status_note: GCF approved approximately USD 1.5 million in project-preparation support in 2022; the initiative has continued through Indonesian institutional, financing and knowledge-development activities.

document_title: M0172 Methodology Framework for Seaweed Carbon Projects
notes: Verra's M0172 proposal is a globally applicable framework for seaweed carbon projects. The proposed structure would provide overarching rules used together with activity-specific modules, beginning with a module for creation of seaweed or kelp farms intended to increase carbon sequestration and storage in ocean sediments. The framework is designed to accommodate future modules for restoration and conservation of native seaweed beds and offshore cultivation. Verra lists the proposal at Step 3, Draft Methodology Development, under Sectoral Scope 17 for ocean carbon. It is not an approved VCS methodology and cannot currently be used as the sole basis for project registration or credit issuance. Key accounting, durability, ecological-risk and monitoring requirements remain under development.
source: Verra
status_note: Listed by Verra in 2026 at Step 3, Draft Methodology Development, under development ID M0172; no final methodology approval has been issued.

document_title: M0408 Proposed Revision to VM0033 for Human Controlled Wetlands
notes: M0408 proposed expanding VM0033 to include Human Controlled Wetlands in which tidal water flow is actively managed to optimize carbon sequestration and ecosystem function. Verra formally rejected the proposal on 1 April 2026 after determining that its expected climate impact did not rank as highly as other methodology ideas and that the proposed project activities were already eligible under the existing VM0033 methodology. This is an official methodology-development decision and is distinct from the active VM0033 standard and from other revision proposals. The rejected concept cannot be used as a new methodology, does not create additional project eligibility beyond existing rules, and does not support project registration or issuance of carbon credits.
source: Verra
status_note: Methodology development ID M0408 was formally rejected by Verra on 1 April 2026 and will not proceed through the full development process at this time.

document_title: Source to Sea: Enhancing Blue Carbon Ecosystems and Community Resilience in Kenya
notes: This Green Climate Fund concept note, submitted by the United Nations Environment Programme, proposes a source-to-sea approach for strengthening Kenya's blue-carbon ecosystems and the resilience of coastal communities. Earlier stakeholder development involved national, subnational and international actors and considered project components, climate rationale, site-selection criteria and community needs. As a concept note, the document records a proposed programme rather than an approved GCF investment. It does not confirm a final financing package, implementation area, restoration target, environmental authorization, carbon-accounting methodology or crediting pathway. Any future project would require further feasibility work, safeguards, government and GCF approvals, detailed monitoring and financing arrangements before blue-carbon outcomes could be implemented or claimed.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF) / United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) / Government of Kenya
status_note: Concept note published by the Green Climate Fund in May 2023; the public source does not show approval as a full GCF funding proposal.

document_title: Green Climate Fund Thematic Brief: Oceans
notes: The Green Climate Fund thematic brief describes oceans and coastal ecosystems as major natural assets for climate regulation, carbon absorption, livelihoods, biodiversity and coastal protection. It identifies mangroves, seagrasses, seaweed beds, salt marshes and related coastal systems as blue-carbon ecosystems and explains the finance gap that limits their protection and restoration. The brief outlines policy and financing approaches including grants, concessional and private finance, de-risking instruments, blue bonds, debt swaps, technical assistance and integrated coastal management. It is a strategic financing brief rather than a funding decision or carbon-accounting standard. It does not approve individual projects, define additionality or permanence requirements, establish a registry or guarantee that proposed blue-economy investments will generate verified carbon removals.
source: Green Climate Fund (GCF)
status_note: Published on 26 October 2021 and retained by GCF as an active thematic resource for ocean and coastal climate-finance development.

subnational_area: Selected coastal ecosystems and aquaculture communities
document_title: Innovative Blue-Carbon Finance for Coastal and Aquaculture Resilience in Cuba
notes: This Adaptation Fund large innovation project concept proposes a national blue-carbon finance mechanism to support coastal adaptation, ecosystem restoration and resilient aquaculture in Cuba. The concept includes development of measurement, reporting and verification capacity for mangroves, seagrass meadows and salt marshes, assessment of carbon stocks and fluxes, alignment with international standards, project-pipeline development and exploration of voluntary and compliance carbon-market access. It also links blue-carbon finance with community livelihoods, aquaculture resilience and South-South knowledge exchange. The public record is a project concept and technical review package, not an approved operational crediting programme. It does not confirm full project approval, site-level permits, verified removals, registry acceptance or issuance of carbon credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / International Atomic Energy Agency and Cuban national partners
status_note: Large innovation project concept submitted and technically reviewed in 2026; full financing approval and implementation had not been confirmed on the official project page.

subnational_area: Central Pacific coastal zone and Arco Seco communities
document_title: Strengthening Climate Resilience in Livelihoods and Coastal Ecosystems of the Central Pacific of Panama
notes: This Adaptation Fund programme supports climate-resilient livelihoods, nature-based adaptation and improved management of high-value coastal ecosystems identified as blue-carbon sinks in Panama's Central Pacific region. The approved programme combines ecosystem protection, reforestation, enrichment and restoration with climate-smart production, water-management improvements, climate information, risk-reduction tools, institutional strengthening and knowledge management. It is designed to reduce pressure on coastal ecosystems while improving the adaptive capacity of vulnerable communities and productive sectors. The programme provides formal public climate finance for implementation, but it is not a carbon-credit standard or automatic project registration. Its blue-carbon contribution depends on site selection, ecological performance, monitoring and sustained management, and the official project page does not report verified removals or issued credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / Fundación Natura Panama
status_note: Approved in Adaptation Fund fiscal year 2025 as a USD 10 million coastal resilience programme; implementation outputs remain subject to project monitoring and safeguards.

document_title: GEF Project 12014 — Enhancing Coastal Adaptation and Resilience in Bangladesh (CARB)
notes: The CARB concept approved under the Least Developed Countries Fund proposes community-led mangrove restoration combined with financial inclusion and market access for climate-resilient livelihoods in coastal Bangladesh. The project is designed to strengthen ecosystem and community resilience while improving enabling conditions for locally led restoration, sustainable income generation and inclusive adaptation finance. The official GEF record identifies Conservation International as the implementing agency and lists national forest, environment and community partners. Concept approval authorizes further project preparation rather than full implementation. The public project summary does not identify final restoration sites, verified carbon-removal quantities, an approved blue-carbon methodology or a carbon-crediting arrangement. Detailed safeguards, monitoring, additionality and long-term management requirements remain to be developed during project design.
source: Global Environment Facility (GEF) / Least Developed Countries Fund
status_note: GEF concept approved on 3 June 2026; the project had not yet reached full implementation approval on the official GEF page.

subnational_area: Tanga-Pemba Seascape and eight priority coastal districts
document_title: Sustainable Management of Critical Coastal Habitats in Tanzania
notes: This GEF-supported initiative is intended to strengthen management and community-led restoration of mangroves, seagrass beds, coral reefs and associated fisheries habitats across the Tanga-Pemba Seascape. The programme combines habitat restoration, improved management effectiveness, inclusive blue-economy opportunities, circular-economy activities and community stewardship. UNDP identifies increased blue-carbon sequestration as one of the expected global environmental benefits, alongside reduced ecosystem degradation and strengthened resilience. The public announcement confirms GEF Council approval and a proposed project budget, but does not provide project-level carbon baselines, restoration-area accounting, an approved crediting methodology or verified removal outcomes. The initiative should therefore be treated as an approved programme moving toward implementation, not as a registered carbon project or evidence of credit issuance.
source: Government of Tanzania / United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) / Global Environment Facility (GEF)
status_note: GEF Council approval was announced in December 2025; detailed implementation, verification and crediting arrangements were not reported.

subnational_area: Priority marine protected areas and critical marine habitats
document_title: GEF Project 12125 — Indonesia Critical Marine Habitat Facility
notes: The Indonesia Critical Marine Habitat Facility concept proposes a financing platform that channels resources from multiple blue-finance instruments into conservation and rehabilitation of critical marine habitats in priority marine protected areas. The GEF record identifies the Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries and UNDP as national and implementing partners and describes a medium-size project supported by substantial co-financing. Its relevance to ONCE lies in the proposed rehabilitation and financing of coastal habitats that may include mangroves and seagrass systems, while the public summary does not quantify blue-carbon stocks or specify habitat shares. Concept approval does not authorize individual interventions, certify a carbon methodology or establish credit issuance. Site selection, safeguards, monitoring and carbon-accounting treatment remain subject to later project development.
source: Global Environment Facility (GEF) / United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
status_note: GEF concept approved on 12 May 2026; full implementation approval and site-level investment decisions were not shown on the official project page.

document_title: National Policy Framework Assessment on Nature-based Solutions for Coastal Resilience and Forestry Sectors in Vanuatu
notes: This national policy-framework assessment reviews how Nature-based Solutions can be integrated into Vanuatu's coastal-resilience and forestry policies, legislation, planning and investment systems. For the coastal sector, it identifies rehabilitation of mangroves and coastal vegetation, community-based natural-resource management, climate-resilient livelihoods, ecosystem-based adaptation and stronger environmental governance as priority interventions. The report links ecosystem restoration with carbon sequestration, disaster-risk reduction, biodiversity and customary stewardship and assesses entry points in climate, fisheries, ocean, disaster and foreshore-development instruments. It is a policy assessment and evidence-based roadmap rather than a new binding law. It does not approve a specific restoration project, establish a blue-carbon baseline, quantify verified removals or create a carbon-credit methodology.
source: Government of Vanuatu / Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme (SPREP) / IUCN
status_note: Published in June 2026 as an active national policy-assessment and implementation resource under the Pacific Nature-based Solutions programme.

document_title: Fatumaru Bay Coastal Resilience Roadmap and Action Plan
notes: The Fatumaru Bay roadmap provides a coordinated action framework for addressing coastal erosion, inundation, degraded water quality and climate-related hazards in Port Vila. It combines Nature-based Solutions, site-specific adaptation, governance reform, community participation, monitoring and preparation of a coastal-protection pilot. The roadmap identifies ecosystem management and restoration as part of a broader package intended to strengthen ecological and social resilience and create sustainable coastal livelihood opportunities. Its ONCE relevance is primarily planning for restoration and protection of coastal ecosystems rather than quantified carbon removal. The document is a roadmap, not a construction permit, funded implementation decision or carbon-accounting standard. Detailed pilot design, ecological baseline, carbon benefits, approvals, procurement and long-term maintenance remain future implementation steps.
source: Government of Vanuatu — Department of Urban Affairs and Planning
status_note: Roadmap published in 2026; proposed Nature-based Solutions and coastal-protection pilot actions require subsequent design, financing and approval.

document_title: Empowering Coastal Sri Lanka: Livelihoods and Preparedness for a Climate-Resilient Future (E-COAST Sri Lanka)
notes: The E-COAST Sri Lanka concept proposes climate-resilient coastal livelihoods, preparedness systems and ecosystem-based adaptation for vulnerable coastal populations. Proposed activities include mangrove restoration, dune stabilization, lagoon management, climate-risk information, resilient livelihood support and institutional capacity building. The concept recognizes mangroves and lagoon ecosystems as coastal protection systems and carbon-sequestering habitats, but its primary purpose is adaptation and livelihood resilience rather than carbon-credit generation. Adaptation Fund technical reviews requested additional clarification on site selection, costing, environmental risks and the relationship between proposed interventions and climate hazards. The record therefore represents a project concept under review, not a fully approved programme, site permit or verified blue-carbon project. Final activities and budgets may change during proposal development.
source: Adaptation Fund / World Food Programme / Ministry of Environment of Sri Lanka
status_note: Regular-size project concept reviewed during 2025; the official materials did not confirm full proposal approval or implementation start.

document_title: Batticaloa Climate Smart Adaptation and Resilience through Ecosystems (B-CARE)
notes: B-CARE is a locally led adaptation project concept for Batticaloa District that proposes community-driven restoration of ecosystem services, flood-risk reduction, locally generated climate information and stronger collaboration between communities and local authorities. Proposed interventions include rehabilitation of natural drainage networks connected to lagoons and the ocean, wetland and riparian-buffer restoration, saltwater-intrusion management and other Nature-based Solutions. The project's direct objective is adaptation rather than carbon removal, but restoration of coastal and wetland systems can protect and rebuild blue-carbon functions where eligible habitats are involved. Adaptation Fund reviewers requested stronger hydrological integration, clearer climate justification, prioritization and sustainability arrangements. The concept remains under review and does not constitute final financing approval, environmental authorization, carbon accounting or credit issuance.
source: Adaptation Fund / Sri Lankan national and local implementing partners
status_note: Locally Led Adaptation concept reviewed in 2026, with a proposed 2027–2029 implementation period subject to approval and final design.

document_title: Build Resilience to Climate Change and Climate Variability of Vulnerable Communities in Mullaitivu District of Sri Lanka
notes: This Adaptation Fund project supports climate-resilient livelihoods, small-scale infrastructure, ecosystem restoration and institutional capacity in drought-, flood- and salinity-affected communities of Mullaitivu District. A documented coastal component restores mangrove cover in Nayaru Lagoon through community nurseries, planting and participation of fishing organizations and women. The project links restored mangroves with shoreline protection, fisheries habitat, food security and resilience to coastal hazards. Its principal policy purpose is adaptation rather than quantified carbon removal, and the public project materials do not establish a project-level blue-carbon baseline, additionality test, permanence arrangement or crediting methodology. Mangrove restoration should therefore be treated as an implemented ecosystem-based adaptation measure with potential carbon benefits, not as evidence of verified or issued carbon credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / UN-Habitat Sri Lanka / Government of Sri Lanka
status_note: Approved project implemented during the 2023–2027 period; the official Adaptation Fund story reported active mangrove restoration in March 2026.

document_title: Conservation and Management of Coastal Resources as a Potential Adaptation Strategy for Sea Level Rise
notes: This Adaptation Fund project restored degraded mangroves along the Krishna estuary and demonstrated an Integrated Mangrove Fishery Farming System for vulnerable coastal communities in Andhra Pradesh. The programme included stakeholder organization, capacity building, restoration of approximately 200 hectares of degraded saline and unprotected mangrove areas, mangrove-compatible aquaculture livelihoods and knowledge management. Native mixed-species restoration was intended to reduce saltwater intrusion, support sediment accumulation, improve ecosystem condition and strengthen protection from cyclones and storm surges. The project was designed and funded as an adaptation demonstration rather than a carbon-credit programme. Its public materials do not report a verified blue-carbon baseline, additionality assessment, permanence buffer, registry registration or credit issuance, although restored mangroves are directly relevant to biological carbon storage.
source: Adaptation Fund / National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development / M. S. Swaminathan Research Foundation
status_note: Completed Adaptation Fund mangrove-restoration and livelihood demonstration; the official page retains project and performance documentation.

document_title: Reduction of Vulnerability to Coastal Flooding through Ecosystem-based Adaptation in Southern Artemisa and Mayabeque
notes: This completed Adaptation Fund project used natural regeneration and active planting to recover mangroves and associated coastal ecosystems along an approximately eighty-four-kilometre section of Cuba's Gulf of Batabano coast. The programme combined ecosystem recovery, community adaptation, capacity building and an enabling regional framework to reduce exposure to storm surge, flooding, erosion and saline intrusion. Mangrove restoration was implemented as protective natural infrastructure and is directly relevant to conservation and enhancement of biological carbon stocks. The project was not designed as a market-based carbon-removal programme, and the public materials do not report project registration, a crediting baseline, verified removal volumes or issued offsets. Its primary documented outcomes concern ecosystem structure, coastal protection and adaptation sustainability.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) / Government of Cuba
status_note: Completed ecosystem-based adaptation project with final evaluation documentation available on the official Adaptation Fund page.

document_title: Reducing Vulnerability and Increasing Resilience of Coastal Communities in the Saloum Islands
notes: This Adaptation Fund project addressed coastal flooding, erosion, salinization and degradation of mangrove habitats affecting communities in Dionewar and Fadial within Senegal's Saloum estuary. It combined ecosystem-resilience measures with flood and salinity protection, support for fisheries, oyster farming and forestry livelihoods, local planning and knowledge management. Restoration and improved management of mangrove-dependent habitats were intended to rebuild protective ecosystem services and sustain community livelihoods. The intervention is relevant to blue-carbon conservation because mangrove degradation had reduced ecological function, but the programme's formal objective was adaptation rather than carbon-credit generation. The official project materials do not provide a verified carbon baseline, net removal calculation, registry registration or credit issuance, and carbon benefits remain ancillary to documented resilience outcomes.
source: Adaptation Fund / Centre de Suivi Ecologique (CSE), Senegal
status_note: Completed local adaptation project with multiple performance reports retained on the official Adaptation Fund page.

subnational_area: Mon Choisy, Riviere des Galets and Quatre Soeurs
document_title: Climate Change Adaptation Programme in the Coastal Zone of Mauritius
notes: This Adaptation Fund programme implemented coastal-protection measures in vulnerable locations in Mauritius using a combination of engineered infrastructure, mangroves and other shoreline vegetation, storm-surge warning systems, institutional training, policy mainstreaming and public information. Mangrove planting and shoreline vegetation were intended to reduce erosion and strengthen natural protection, while monitoring assessed the relationship between coastal processes, climate change and intervention effectiveness. The programme is relevant to ecological restoration and biological carbon storage but was designed primarily for adaptation and disaster-risk reduction. The official record does not present a project-level carbon baseline, additionality analysis, permanence requirement, blue-carbon methodology or credit issuance. Its documented policy contribution is integration of long-term climate risk into coastal planning and protection decisions.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) / Government of Mauritius
status_note: Completed national coastal adaptation programme with a completion report and final evaluation listed on the official project page.

subnational_area: Rote Ndao and Sabu Raijua Districts, Savu Sea
document_title: Ecosystem-Based Adaptation to Support Climate Resilience in Rote Ndao and Sabu Raijua Districts in the Savu Sea
notes: This Adaptation Fund project supports ecosystem-based adaptation in small-island communities of Indonesia's Savu Sea through climate-risk information, local capacity building, resilient livelihoods and protection or restoration of coastal ecosystems. Project documentation identifies mangroves, seagrass beds and coral reefs as natural systems that reduce wave energy, stabilize coastlines, sustain fisheries and strengthen food security. Conservation and restoration of mangroves and seagrasses are directly relevant to coastal blue-carbon stocks, although the project's formal objective is adaptation rather than quantified carbon removal. The official project page does not report an approved blue-carbon methodology, project-level carbon baseline, additionality and permanence assessment, registry registration or credit issuance. Carbon benefits should therefore be treated as potential co-benefits of ecosystem recovery.
source: Adaptation Fund / Kemitraan / YAPEKA Consortium and Indonesian local partners
status_note: Approved Adaptation Fund project with project documents available from 2022; the official page does not report project closure.

document_title: Strengthening the Adaptive Capacity of Coastal Communities of Fiji to Climate Change through Nature-Based Seawalls
notes: This Adaptation Fund project combines mangrove forests, locally sourced boulders and vetiver grass to construct nature-based seawalls for sixteen climate-vulnerable coastal communities in Fiji. The programme also strengthens cross-ministerial coordination, engineering capacity, community participation, safeguards, maintenance arrangements and knowledge transfer so that similar interventions can be replicated elsewhere. The official project page records approval in April 2024, implementation beginning in May 2026 and expected completion in November 2031. Mangrove establishment and protection can conserve and increase biological carbon stocks, but the programme is formally an adaptation and coastal-protection investment. It does not establish a blue-carbon baseline, additionality test, crediting methodology, registry registration or verified carbon-credit issuance.
source: Adaptation Fund / Pacific Community / Government of Fiji
status_note: Approved on 19 April 2024 and officially listed as under implementation from 4 May 2026 to the expected completion date of 4 November 2031.

subnational_area: Selected coastal communities in both countries
document_title: Improved Resilience of Coastal Communities in Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana
notes: This regional Adaptation Fund programme supports coastal-risk assessment, planning, community resilience and green or hybrid infrastructure in Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana. Its nature-based portfolio includes protection and restoration of mangroves, seagrass planting and other coastal habitat interventions alongside livelihood support, institutional strengthening and regional knowledge exchange. The programme was approved in August 2023, began implementation in September 2024 and is scheduled to continue through March 2029. The ecosystem measures can conserve or rebuild coastal biological carbon stocks, but the programme is primarily designed for adaptation and protection from erosion, flooding and sea-level rise. Its public project materials do not establish a carbon-credit methodology, quantify verified net removals, register offsets or report issuance of tradable credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / UN-Habitat / Governments and partners of Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana
status_note: Approved on 28 August 2023 and officially listed as under implementation from 26 September 2024, with expected completion on 26 March 2029.

document_title: Enhancing the Resilience of Coastal Livelihoods through Marine Ecosystem-Based Adaptation on the Gulf of Thailand
notes: This Adaptation Fund concept proposes a five-year marine ecosystem-based adaptation programme for coastal communities around the Gulf of Thailand. The concept combines protection and restoration of mangroves, seagrass beds and coral reefs with climate-risk information, resilient livelihoods, institutional coordination and exploration of sustainable financing, including blue-carbon-related approaches and public-private cooperation. The requested grant is USD 10 million and the official project page identifies UNDP and Thailand's Department of Climate Change and Environment as the implementing and executing entities. The proposal remains at the concept-submission stage. It does not authorize restoration at a specific site, establish a national blue-carbon methodology, confirm project additionality or permanence, register carbon units or report verified removals and issued credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Development Programme / Government of Thailand
status_note: Officially listed in 2026 as a submitted five-year project concept requesting USD 10 million; full approval and implementation had not been confirmed.

document_title: Enhancing Coastal Resilience in the South-East Asia Seas
notes: This regional Adaptation Fund concept proposes a six-year programme combining coastal observation, hazard prediction, early warning, decision support and nature-based restoration across participating South-East Asian countries. The institutional partnership includes national marine, meteorological and research agencies, UNESCO ocean-observation bodies, UNIDO and regional technical organizations. Proposed ecosystem measures address degraded coastal habitats, including mangrove and seagrass systems, while digital monitoring and forecasting are intended to guide site selection, evaluate resilience outcomes and improve disaster preparedness. The official page records a requested grant of approximately USD 29.3 million and a concept-submitted status. The proposal is not yet an implementation authorization or blue-carbon standard and does not establish verified removal quantities, credit eligibility, registry approval or carbon-credit issuance.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Industrial Development Organization and regional partners
status_note: Listed in 2026 as a submitted regional concept requesting USD 29,324,647 for six years; final approval and implementation had not been reported.

document_title: Enhancing the Climate Resilience of Coastal Communities in Limón and Bocas del Toro through Nature-Based Solutions for Local Livelihoods
notes: This endorsed regional Adaptation Fund concept targets the connected coastal landscape of Limón in Costa Rica and Bocas del Toro in Panama. It proposes nature-based adaptation within a seagrass, coral and mangrove ecosystem mosaic, combined with climate-risk information, local livelihood measures, community participation and transboundary coordination. The programme requests USD 12.1 million for a four-year implementation period and is to be implemented by UNEP with national executing partners. Endorsement permits preparation of a fuller proposal but does not constitute final financing approval or authorization of individual restoration activities. The concept does not provide an approved blue-carbon accounting method, project-level additionality and permanence assessment, independently verified carbon removals, registry registration or evidence that carbon credits have been issued.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Environment Programme / Costa Rican and Panamanian partners
status_note: Officially listed in 2026 as an endorsed four-year regional concept requesting USD 12.1 million; a complete approved implementation proposal was not shown.

document_title: Enhancing Adaptive Capacity of Communities to Climate Change-Related Floods in the North Coast and Islands Region of Papua New Guinea
notes: This completed Adaptation Fund project combined coastal and inland flood early-warning systems, preparedness planning, institutional strengthening and support for community-led mangrove reforestation and conservation. The coastal component created observation, information-management and response arrangements while enabling local mangrove projects to improve shoreline protection and ecosystem resilience. The programme was approved in March 2012, began in July 2012 and reached its revised completion date in December 2017. Mangrove activities can protect and rebuild biological carbon stocks, but the project was formally designed for disaster-risk reduction and adaptation. Its official materials do not establish a blue-carbon baseline, additionality assessment, permanence buffer, carbon-credit registry, verified removal volume or issued offsets.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Development Programme / Government of Papua New Guinea
status_note: Approved on 16 March 2012, implemented from 26 July 2012 and officially recorded as completed on 31 December 2017.

subnational_area: Coastal municipalities of Holguín and Las Tunas
document_title: Climate Smart Aquaculture Systems and Resilient Blue Food Industries
notes: This Adaptation Fund concept proposes climate-smart and regenerative aquaculture systems for coastal communities and blue-food industries in eastern Cuba. Planned measures include integrated multi-trophic aquaculture, resilient production and processing infrastructure, circular resource use, ecosystem-based adaptation and maintenance or restoration of supporting coastal ecosystems such as mangroves. The concept refers to oyster, shrimp and sea-cucumber production and seeks to reduce vulnerability to warming, salinization, drought, sea-level rise and extreme weather while supporting food security and inclusive livelihoods. The requested grant is USD 3.9 million for four years. The concept remains under review and does not authorize marine farming sites, define creditable carbon removals, approve a blue-carbon methodology, register units or demonstrate issued credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Industrial Development Organization / Cuban partners
status_note: Officially listed in 2026 as a submitted four-year project concept requesting USD 3.9 million; full approval and implementation had not been confirmed.

document_title: Ecosystem-Based Adaptation of the Comoros Coastal Zone
notes: This Adaptation Fund proposal requests approximately USD 9.98 million for ecosystem-based adaptation along the Comoros coast. The project design includes restoration of degraded coastal ecosystems, community-based management, climate-resilient livelihoods, institutional strengthening and monitoring. Proposal materials identify restoration of approximately thirty hectares of mangroves and improved management of associated coastal habitats as concrete measures for reducing erosion, flooding and ecosystem vulnerability. The programme is relevant to coastal blue carbon because mangrove recovery can rebuild biomass and soil-carbon stocks, but its formal objective is adaptation rather than carbon-credit generation. The official project page does not show final approval or implementation status, and the proposal does not establish verified removals, an approved crediting methodology, registry registration or issued carbon units.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Environment Programme / Government of Comoros
status_note: Adaptation Fund proposal materials were published in 2022; the official project page did not display confirmation of final approval, implementation or closure.

subnational_area: Asilulu, Ureng and Lima villages, Central Maluku
document_title: Enhancing the Adaptation Capability of Coastal Communities in Asilulu, Ureng and Lima, Central Maluku
notes: This Adaptation Fund project supports coastal adaptation in three Central Maluku villages through fisheries resilience, coastal-ecosystem repair, alternative livelihoods and infrastructure for flooding and tidal-wave risks. Implementation materials include rehabilitation of coastal habitats and development of floating seaweed cultivation as a livelihood option, while the broader project strengthens local capacity and management of climate-sensitive marine resources. The project was approved in October 2021, began in August 2022 and is still listed by the Fund as under implementation despite an original expected completion date in August 2025. Seaweed cultivation and habitat rehabilitation can contribute to biological carbon pathways, but the project does not provide a crediting baseline, permanence framework, verified removal volume, registry registration or issued credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / Kemitraan / Harmony Alam Indonesia Foundation
status_note: Approved on 21 October 2021, started on 29 August 2022 and officially remains listed as under implementation on the current project page.

document_title: Building Urban Climate Resilience in South-Eastern Africa
notes: This regional Adaptation Fund programme supports participatory urban resilience planning and priority adaptation subprojects in four cities across south-eastern Africa. The Morondava component includes community-based mangrove restoration and nursery development to strengthen coastal protection, while the wider programme covers flood management, resilient infrastructure, governance capacity, knowledge exchange and support for vulnerable urban populations. The programme was approved in July 2019, began in June 2020 and remains officially listed as under implementation after a revised completion date in April 2025. Its mangrove component can conserve and increase biological carbon stocks, but the regional programme is not a blue-carbon credit project. Public materials do not establish additionality, permanence, a carbon registry, verified removals or issued carbon credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / UN-Habitat / National and municipal partners in south-eastern Africa
status_note: Approved on 15 July 2019, started on 23 June 2020 and remains officially listed as under implementation following a revised completion date of 21 April 2025.

subnational_area: Lembar and Sekotong, West Lombok, West Nusa Tenggara
document_title: Village-Based Coastal Adaptation and Resilience in Lombok Province of West Nusa Tenggara
notes: This Adaptation Fund proposal targets coastal villages exposed to tidal flooding, shoreline change and livelihood disruption in West Lombok. Proposed activities include village climate-risk planning, community field schools, early-warning and preparedness measures, livelihood diversification, rehabilitation of coastal ecosystems and mangrove planting across approximately one hundred hectares with community-based nurseries. The official project page lists a requested grant of USD 998,739, a two-year duration and a proposal-submitted status. The project therefore remains under review rather than under implementation. Its mangrove work could restore coastal biological carbon stocks, but the proposal does not establish a project-level carbon baseline, additionality or permanence rules, an approved crediting methodology, registry registration, verified removal outcomes or issued carbon credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / Kemitraan / Indonesian local partners
status_note: Officially listed as a submitted two-year proposal requesting USD 998,739; final approval, financing transfer and implementation start had not been confirmed.

document_title: Safekeeping-Surviving-Sustaining towards Resilience: 3S Approach for Pekalongan City
notes: The Pekalongan 3S programme combines climate-risk assessment, coastal-protection interventions, local adaptation planning, livelihood support, sanitation improvements, institutional coordination and monitoring in a low-lying Indonesian coastal city. Project implementation includes soft and hard shoreline measures and rehabilitation of coastal vegetation, including mangrove-related protection activities, to address tidal flooding, erosion and land subsidence. The Adaptation Fund approved the programme in September 2020, implementation began in July 2021 and the completion date was revised to November 2026. The programme remains officially listed as under implementation. Although ecosystem rehabilitation may protect coastal carbon stocks, the project is not registered as a carbon-removal activity and does not report a blue-carbon baseline, verified removals, methodology approval or issued credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / Kemitraan / Government and communities of Pekalongan City
status_note: Approved on 23 September 2020, started on 15 July 2021 and remains under implementation with a revised completion date of 12 November 2026.

subnational_area: Coastal wetland and mangrove areas of former Trà Vinh and Bến Tre
document_title: Innovative Financial Incentives for Adaptation in Wetland Livelihoods (IFIA) — Implementation Phase
notes: The IFIA project was formally launched in November 2025 to pilot and institutionalize financing mechanisms for climate adaptation in coastal wetland livelihoods. The USD 5 million initiative supports approximately 21,000 vulnerable people engaged in eco-aquaculture, eco-tourism and sustainable use of mangrove and wetland resources. Activities include an adaptation research and innovation fund, tailored financial products, private-sector partnerships, policy learning and mechanisms intended to expand sustainable wetland and mangrove management. The implementation period runs from 2025 to 2029. The project concerns adaptation finance and ecosystem stewardship rather than carbon-credit generation. It does not establish a blue-carbon methodology, determine project additionality or permanence, register offsets, quantify independently verified removals or report issued carbon credits.
source: Government of Viet Nam / International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)
status_note: Formally launched on 12 November 2025 for implementation during 2025–2029, with a mid-term review planned for 2027 and terminal evaluation in 2029.

document_title: Peraturan Menteri Kelautan dan Perikanan Nomor 1 Tahun 2025 tentang Tata Cara Penyelenggaraan Nilai Ekonomi Karbon Sektor Kelautan
notes: This binding ministerial regulation establishes procedures for implementing carbon economic value instruments in Indonesia's marine sector. It links marine mitigation activities to national climate targets and the wider national carbon economic value system. Its chapters address implementation arrangements, measurement, reporting and verification, official recording, greenhouse-gas emission-reduction certification, management of funds, monitoring and evaluation. The official preparatory materials identify mangroves and seagrass ecosystems as principal blue-carbon assets and contemplate market and non-market mechanisms, including carbon trading, offsets and results-based payments. The regulation creates a governance and compliance framework, but it does not automatically approve individual projects, establish project baselines, verify removals or issue carbon credits without subsequent registration, certification, permitting and regulatory oversight.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Enacted on 6 January 2025, promulgated on 14 January 2025 and officially listed as in force.

document_title: Keputusan Menteri Kelautan dan Perikanan Nomor 52 Tahun 2024 tentang Peta Jalan Mitigasi Perubahan Iklim Sektor Kelautan dan Perikanan
notes: This ministerial decision adopts a climate-change mitigation roadmap for Indonesia's marine and fisheries sector. The roadmap provides an official planning basis for sectoral mitigation priorities, institutional coordination, programme sequencing and implementation through marine and fisheries policies. Its blue-carbon dimension includes protection, management and restoration of mangrove and seagrass ecosystems and development of the evidence, monitoring and governance needed to recognize their mitigation contribution. The decision is an internally binding national planning instrument rather than a project-level authorization or carbon-credit methodology. It sets strategic direction and can support later regulations, investment programmes and market instruments, but it does not by itself designate every implementation site, determine additionality and permanence, certify quantified removals, register projects or issue tradable carbon units.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Adopted on 28 July 2024 and officially listed by the ministry's legal information system as in force.

document_title: Kajian Teknis Penyusunan Rancangan Peraturan Menteri Kelautan dan Perikanan tentang Penyelenggaraan Nilai Ekonomi Karbon Sektor Kelautan atau Blue Carbon
notes: This technical study supplied the analytical basis for Indonesia's later marine-sector carbon economic value regulation. It identifies the need for complete maps and datasets, a measurement, reporting and verification framework, methodologies for calculating blue-carbon units, market mechanisms, non-market mechanisms and recording through the national climate registry. The study discusses mangrove and seagrass mitigation, risks from seagrass degradation, restoration scenarios, integration of blue carbon into the Nationally Determined Contribution and use of IPCC wetland guidance. It is a preparatory assessment rather than a binding rule and its policy-development function was substantially fulfilled by the 2025 regulation. It does not itself establish legal project eligibility, certify a methodology, authorize restoration, verify removal quantities or issue carbon units.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Prepared as a 2023 technical analysis supporting the regulation that was subsequently enacted in January 2025.

document_title: Keputusan Menteri Kelautan dan Perikanan Nomor 82 Tahun 2025 tentang Program Penyusunan Peraturan Menteri dan Keputusan Menteri di Lingkungan Kementerian Kelautan dan Perikanan Tahun 2026
notes: This ministerial decision adopts the Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries' formal regulatory drafting programme for 2026. One scheduled instrument is a 2025–2030 marine and fisheries carbon-trading roadmap covering blue-carbon ecosystems, specifically mangroves and seagrass, carbon trading related to fisheries vessels and aquaculture areas, results-based payments, carbon levies, governance, methodologies and monitoring systems. The decision therefore documents an official commitment to develop a more detailed sectoral carbon-market roadmap and assigns a timetable within the ministry's legal work programme. It is not the roadmap itself and does not establish trading eligibility, issue allowances or credits, approve blue-carbon projects or quantify removals. Its function is regulatory planning and coordination, and completion of the scheduled downstream instrument requires a separate formal decision.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Adopted on 16 December 2025 as the ministry's binding legal-drafting programme for calendar year 2026.

document_title: Peraturan Presiden Nomor 110 Tahun 2025 tentang Penyelenggaraan Instrumen Nilai Ekonomi Karbon dan Pengendalian Emisi Gas Rumah Kaca Nasional
notes: This presidential regulation replaces the previous national carbon economic value framework and establishes Indonesia's current system for carbon allocation, Nationally Determined Contribution preparation, carbon economic value instruments, transparency, monitoring, evaluation, supervision and financing. It expressly recognizes blue-carbon management as a mitigation subsector coordinated by the minister responsible for marine affairs and fisheries, while mangrove management remains connected with the forestry subsector. The regulation therefore supplies the national legal architecture within which marine-sector rules, targets, registries, trading and results-based mechanisms operate. It is a binding cross-sector framework rather than a project permit. Individual blue-carbon activities must still comply with sectoral rules, baselines, MRV, safeguards and registration requirements, and the presidential regulation does not itself verify project removals or issue credits.
source: President of the Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Enacted and promulgated on 10 October 2025, officially in force and replacing Presidential Regulation No. 98 of 2021.

document_title: Rancangan Peraturan Menteri Kelautan dan Perikanan tentang Tata Cara Penyelenggaraan Nilai Ekonomi Karbon Sektor Kelautan
notes: This official draft set out the proposed legal design for implementing carbon economic value instruments in Indonesia's marine sector before adoption of the final ministerial regulation. It described eligible marine mitigation activities, including management of mangrove, seagrass and other qualifying blue-carbon ecosystems, domestic and international carbon trading, emissions trading, offsets, direct transactions, buffer requirements, registration in the national climate registry, results-based payments, MRV, certification and monitoring. The draft is retained as a distinct formal rulemaking version because it documents the design considered during legal preparation. It no longer has an independent operational role after enactment of Ministerial Regulation No. 1 of 2025. It did not itself create binding project rights, verify removals or issue carbon credits.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Formal 2025 draft superseded by the final ministerial regulation promulgated on 14 January 2025.

subnational_area: Four pilot provinces to be selected during project preparation
document_title: GEF Project 12073 — Enhancing Policy Coherence for a Sustainable Blue Economy in Indonesia
notes: This GEF full-size project concept proposes a unified data, ocean-accounting and decision-support framework for marine and coastal policy in Indonesia. Planned activities include strengthening ocean accounts in four provinces, standardizing methodologies and datasets, improving cross-ministerial and land-sea policy coherence, integrating ecosystem values into spatial and development planning and aligning public and private investment with biodiversity and climate resilience. Project documentation also anticipates better evidence for restoration monitoring, natural-capital valuation and potential blue-finance or blue-carbon investment cases. The concept was approved with a GEF grant and substantial co-financing, but it has not yet reached full implementation approval. It does not independently restore a defined blue-carbon site, establish a crediting methodology, verify removals or issue carbon credits.
source: Global Environment Facility (GEF) / United Nations Environment Programme
status_note: GEF concept approved on 19 December 2025; full project approval and implementation were not shown on the official project page.

document_title: UK Marine Strategy Part One: 2026 Update
notes: This policy update provides the current assessment of the environmental status of United Kingdom seas and establishes objectives, targets and indicators for the next six-year Marine Strategy cycle. It supplies an overarching monitoring and governance framework for protecting, preventing deterioration of and restoring marine ecosystems where practical or necessary. Climate change is treated as a cross-cutting pressure, and the accompanying government response recognizes continued work on marine carbon evidence, coastal habitats and the potential treatment of blue-carbon ecosystems in wider climate and inventory policy. The strategy is not a dedicated carbon-removal programme and does not approve salt-marsh or seagrass projects, quantify additional removals, establish a blue-carbon crediting method or issue credits. Its ONCE role is primarily policy coordination, ecosystem monitoring and evidence development.
source: UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs and devolved administrations
status_note: Published on 7 April 2026 as the active Part One framework for the next six-year UK Marine Strategy cycle.

document_title: UK Marine Strategy Part One — Summary of Responses and Government Response
notes: This official consultation outcome records stakeholder evidence and the United Kingdom administrations' response before finalization of the 2026 Marine Strategy Part One update. It discusses climate change as a core pressure on marine environmental status and explains continuing research, assessment and policy development concerning marine carbon, salt marshes, seagrass and greenhouse-gas inventory treatment. The response distinguishes issues included directly in Part One from mitigation and adaptation measures that may be developed through later Marine Strategy stages, national adaptation programmes and devolved blue-carbon initiatives. It is a separate policy-response document rather than the strategy itself. It does not authorize restoration, establish project baselines, certify carbon stocks, create a crediting methodology or demonstrate verified carbon removals, but it documents the government's evidence position and future policy direction.
source: UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs and devolved administrations
status_note: Published with the final Marine Strategy update on 7 April 2026 as the official consultation and policy-response record.

document_title: Wilder Humber Multi-Habitat Restoration Programme
notes: Wilder Humber is a five-year, data-led restoration programme operating across the Humber Estuary. It is led by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust and Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust with corporate and public-sector support and combines planting of salt marsh and seagrass, native-oyster reintroduction and reconnection of sand-dune systems. Programme reporting states that eighteen hectares of seagrass had been restored since 2021 and that extensive ecological monitoring is used to measure habitat condition and biodiversity outcomes. Carbon is presented as an emerging future investment pathway because restored habitats can protect sedimentary carbon and compensate for ecosystem carbon loss. The programme is not a carbon-credit methodology or registered offset project and does not report verified removal units or issued credits.
source: Yorkshire Wildlife Trust / Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust and programme partners
status_note: Five-year programme initiated in 2021 and reported as active through its January 2026 European Commission presentation.

subnational_area: Eligible high-nutrient, low-chlorophyll ocean areas within national exclusive economic zones
document_title: Puro Standard Microalgae Carbon Fixation and Sinking Methodology, Edition 2025
notes: This Puro Standard methodology establishes voluntary carbon-removal certification rules for Microalgae Carbon Fixation and Sinking. Eligible activities enhance local microalgae growth on engineered substrates containing bound nutrients and then sink the substrate and attached biomass rapidly into the deep ocean for storage exceeding two hundred years. The methodology specifies site eligibility, scale and deployment limits, environmental impact assessment, baseline data, ecological monitoring, quantification, modeling, uncertainty treatment, third-party verification and safeguards. Puro distinguishes the pathway from uncontrolled ocean fertilization because nutrients remain bound and export is deliberately controlled. Publication creates a crediting pathway but does not authorize marine deployment. Individual projects must secure applicable permits, demonstrate net removal and durability, pass independent audit and satisfy registry requirements before CO2 Removal Certificates can be issued.
source: Puro.earth
status_note: Approved by the Puro.earth Advisory Board on 30 September 2025 and active under the Puro Standard.

document_title: Puro Standard Marine Anoxic Carbon Storage Methodology, Edition 2025
notes: This Puro Standard methodology defines a voluntary certification pathway for Marine Anoxic Carbon Storage. The approach deposits sustainably sourced, lignin-rich terrestrial biomass in deep, oxygen-depleted marine basins where microbial decomposition and animal disturbance are strongly limited, supporting storage for more than two hundred years. The methodology includes site screening, biomass sourcing requirements, baseline and counterfactual assessment, lifecycle greenhouse-gas accounting, durability analysis, monitoring, modeling, field sampling, adaptive management and environmental and social safeguards. It is an active crediting standard but not a dumping permit or deployment authorization. Puro reported that projects remained at the field-trial stage and that no MACS credits had yet been issued; every project must obtain all applicable permits and complete independent audit before CORCs are eligible for issuance.
source: Puro.earth
status_note: Approved by the Puro.earth Advisory Board in April 2025 and active with a conservative durability category exceeding two hundred years.

subnational_area: Permitted coastal or marine storage settings using controlled reactor systems
document_title: Puro Standard Direct Air Capture and Ocean Storage Methodology, Edition 2025 Version 1.1
notes: This Puro Standard methodology provides voluntary certification rules for Direct Air Capture and Ocean Storage. The pathway uses a controlled electrochemical reactor to split seawater into acidic and alkaline streams, exposes the alkaline stream to ambient air so that it absorbs carbon dioxide, re-equilibrates the acidic stream with alkaline rocks and stores carbon as dissolved bicarbonate and solid carbonate. The methodology applies lifecycle accounting, measurement, uncertainty, additionality, durability exceeding one thousand years, environmental impact assessment, water-quality controls, community engagement and third-party verification. It is a private crediting standard rather than a government marine permit. Project-specific intake, discharge, mineral use and storage activities must comply with applicable law, and no credits can be issued without validated net removal, monitoring, independent verification and registry approval.
source: Puro.earth
status_note: Edition 2025 Version 1.1 is listed as an active Puro Standard methodology with a durability category exceeding one thousand years.

document_title: BCR0012 Blue Carbon Methodology, Version 1.0
notes: BCR0012 provides a globally applicable voluntary methodology for quantifying greenhouse-gas emission reductions and removals from conservation, restoration and sustainable management of mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrass meadows. It defines eligible activities, project boundaries, baseline selection, additionality, mandatory and optional carbon pools, treatment of carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide, uncertainty, leakage, reversal risk, monitoring and social and environmental safeguards. Projects must apply the wider BioCarbon Standard and applicable national law and undergo validation, verification and registry procedures. Version 1.0 creates an operational certification pathway but does not approve any particular project, authorize ecosystem intervention or guarantee credit issuance. Verified Carbon Credits can only be issued after project-specific conformity assessment and programme review.
source: BioCarbon Standard / BioCarbon Cert
status_note: Version 1.0 was issued on 7 November 2025 following public consultation and is available as an approved BioCarbon methodology.

document_title: Mangrove Breakthrough Submission to the COP30 Presidency Forest Roadmap
notes: This formal Mangrove Breakthrough submission responds to the COP30 Presidency roadmap on halting and reversing deforestation and forest degradation by 2030. It identifies financial, institutional, technical and social barriers that prevent mangrove conservation and restoration from reaching scale and proposes stronger project pipelines, shared valuation frameworks, investment mechanisms, community transition finance, remote-sensing support and science-based restoration. The submission emphasizes ecosystem integrity, natural hydrological processes, biodiversity, Indigenous and local knowledge and protection of existing mangroves before restoration is considered. It is an external organization submission published through the UNFCCC document system rather than a negotiated COP decision. It does not bind Parties, approve projects, allocate finance, establish a crediting methodology or verify carbon outcomes.
source: Mangrove Breakthrough / United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Published by the UNFCCC on 13 April 2026 as a formal contribution to the COP30 Presidency forest roadmap process.

document_title: Conservation International SB64 Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue Plenary Statement
notes: Conservation International's formal statement to the 2026 UNFCCC Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue focuses on conservation and restoration of mangroves, seagrasses and salt marshes as coastal Nature-based Solutions. It recommends stronger blue-carbon ambition in Nationally Determined Contributions, better greenhouse-gas inventories, seagrass inclusion, improved finance access, policy coherence across climate and biodiversity processes and an Ocean Focal Point within the Standing Committee on Finance. The statement also calls for an implementation-oriented Ocean Dialogue roadmap and finance pathways for coastal nature-based and green-gray infrastructure solutions. It is an observer submission rather than an adopted UNFCCC decision. The document does not create national targets, distribute climate finance, approve restoration projects, establish project-level accounting or issue carbon credits.
source: Conservation International / United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Submitted as a written plenary statement on 30 June 2026 and published through the UNFCCC Ocean Dialogue process.

document_title: Wetlands International Written Intervention for the 2026 Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue
notes: Wetlands International's written intervention urges Parties to move coastal-wetland commitments from policy language into financed and monitored implementation. It addresses mangroves, salt marshes and seagrasses and highlights the need for baselines, targets, technical assistance, monitoring systems, investment-ready pipelines and landscape-scale country propositions. The intervention also recommends alignment of indicators and reporting across the UNFCCC, Convention on Biological Diversity and Ramsar Convention, stronger cooperation among national focal points and integrated national mangrove or coastal-wetland strategies. It is a formal observer contribution to the UNFCCC dialogue, not a treaty decision or binding reporting rule. It does not allocate funds, approve national strategies, establish a carbon-credit methodology, validate projects or demonstrate issued carbon units.
source: Wetlands International / United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Submitted to the 2026 Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue on 10 June 2026 as a non-binding written intervention.

document_title: Ocean Conservancy Submission to the 2026 Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue
notes: Ocean Conservancy's submission recommends strengthening the annual UNFCCC Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue as an implementation platform for ocean-related Nationally Determined Contributions. It calls for greater integration of ocean mitigation and adaptation, technology transfer, capacity building, equitable stakeholder engagement and predictable finance. Specific proposals include exploring dedicated blue-finance windows within multilateral climate funds, connecting Dialogue findings with the Standing Committee on Finance, technology and capacity-building bodies, advancing the Blue NDC Challenge and linking outputs with the second Global Stocktake and COP31. The submission is an observer policy recommendation rather than a Party decision or finance approval. It does not create a funding window, amend NDCs, authorize projects, establish a blue-carbon accounting method or issue carbon credits.
source: Ocean Conservancy / United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Submitted following the 10–11 June 2026 Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue and published by the UNFCCC on 30 June 2026.

document_title: Global Climate Action Agenda Activation Group 7 Ocean Dialogue Intervention
notes: Activation Group 7's intervention presents the ocean component of the Global Climate Action Agenda and describes work to update the Blue Package with indicators and benchmarks through 2028. It calls for measurable mitigation and adaptation outcomes across marine conservation, aquatic food systems, shipping, ports, tourism and ocean renewable energy. For blue-carbon ecosystems, it explicitly includes seagrass, salt marsh, kelp and mangroves and promotes greater finance, improved governance, coastal and ocean planning and stronger integration of ocean actions into Nationally Determined Contributions and National Adaptation Plans. The intervention is a non-state action-agenda statement rather than a binding work programme. It does not establish project eligibility, authorize restoration, quantify additional removals, certify methods or issue credits.
source: Global Climate Action Agenda Activation Group 7 / United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Delivered during the 2026 Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue on 10 June 2026 as a non-binding action-agenda intervention.

document_title: African Group of Negotiators Intervention at the 2026 Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue
notes: The African Group of Negotiators intervention focuses on translating ocean-related Nationally Determined Contribution commitments into implementation across African coastal and island states. It describes priorities including integrated coastal management, marine spatial planning, remote sensing, seagrass protection, blue-carbon accounting, blue bonds, ocean observation and early warning. The statement emphasizes that many commitments are conditional on external support and calls for predictable concessional finance, dedicated funding channels, technical capacity, baseline integration into national greenhouse-gas inventories and resolution of fragmented marine governance. It is a formal negotiating-group intervention but not an adopted UNFCCC decision. It does not bind individual African governments, establish a common blue-carbon methodology, approve projects, verify removals or issue carbon units.
source: African Group of Negotiators / United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Delivered on behalf of the African Group during the June 2026 Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue.

document_title: Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue 2026 Information Note by the Co-Facilitators
notes: This official information note defines the topics, guiding questions and implementation focus for the 2026 UNFCCC Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue. The three themes are ocean-based priorities in Nationally Determined Contributions, means of implementation and ocean-climate-biodiversity synergies and international cooperation. The note directs attention to restoration and protection of marine ecosystems, implementation barriers, regulatory and technical conditions, capacity building, multilateral finance, blue carbon and the potential and limitations of the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism. It also identifies the Blue NDC Challenge and other international initiatives as cooperation platforms.
