The note structures an official UNFCCC dialogue but is not itself a negotiated decision, crediting methodology, funding approval or authorization for marine or coastal projects.
source: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Ocean Dialogue Co-Facilitators
status_note: Issued on 22 May 2026 to guide the Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue held in Bonn on 10–11 June 2026.

document_title: Ocean Visions Statement to the 2026 Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue
notes: Ocean Visions' statement calls for sustained research, development and demonstration capacity for ocean-based climate responses, including marine carbon dioxide removal, seaweed-based climate solutions and marine ecosystem repair. It argues that governments and international organizations need stronger monitoring, environmental assessment, governance, scientific cooperation and institutional readiness before emerging approaches can be evaluated responsibly or considered at meaningful scale. The statement highlights the Africa mCDR Road Map and emerging Africa mCDR Partnership as examples of regionally led scientific and policy capacity building. It is a formal observer statement advocating evidence development rather than deployment. The document does not endorse a specific mCDR technology, authorize field trials, establish crediting rules, quantify removals or report issued carbon credits.
source: Ocean Visions / United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Published by the UNFCCC on 15 June 2026 as an Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue statement.

document_title: Climate Action Network Ecosystems Working Group Intervention at the 2026 Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue
notes: This Climate Action Network intervention advocates a precautionary distinction between established ocean-climate measures and unproven marine geoengineering. It prioritizes emissions reduction and restoration of blue-carbon ecosystems while warning that carbon capture, offsets and marine manipulation can create ecological and governance risks if treated as substitutes for fossil-fuel phaseout. The statement also calls for stronger UNFCCC treatment of ocean acidification, improved coordination among the Rio Conventions and a concrete COP31 roadmap for ocean policy. It is a civil-society intervention rather than a binding prohibition or negotiated decision. The document does not establish a legal moratorium, approve or reject an individual research project, define environmental assessment requirements, create a carbon market or verify blue-carbon outcomes.
source: Climate Action Network Ecosystems Working Group / United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
status_note: Delivered and published during the June 2026 Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue as a non-binding civil-society intervention.

document_title: Can Phytoplankton Help Close the Carbon Dioxide Removal Gap? Research and Development Plan
notes: Ocean Visions' assessment and research plan evaluates whether phytoplankton-based marine carbon dioxide removal pathways could contribute safely and effectively at climate-relevant scale. It synthesizes available evidence and identifies priority work on net-removal quantification, uncertainty reduction, ocean biogeochemical models, biological carbon-pump response, environmental and social impacts and carefully designed field trials. The report recommends a coordinated research, development and demonstration programme using stage-gate decision points that can advance, refine, pause or stop individual approaches as evidence develops. It is an evidence-building roadmap rather than support for immediate commercial deployment. The report does not conclude that phytoplankton interventions are ready for scale, authorize ocean fertilization, establish project-crediting rules or verify any removal quantity.
source: Ocean Visions
status_note: Released on 3 February 2026 as an active research and development roadmap for phytoplankton-based mCDR assessment.

document_title: Delivering the NSW Blue Carbon Strategy — 2026 Implementation Update
notes: This New South Wales Government implementation update reports continued delivery of the NSW Blue Carbon Strategy 2022–2027. It describes work to conserve and restore seagrass, mangrove and salt-marsh ecosystems, support demonstration sites, embed blue carbon in coastal and marine planning, develop a research prospectus and seek additional funding. The update also explains that restoration projects may generate emissions reductions and may become eligible for carbon credits where applicable requirements are satisfied. It is a distinct implementation-stage update to the existing strategy rather than a new strategy or project permit. The page does not identify verified removal volumes, approve a particular restoration site, establish an Australian Carbon Credit Unit method or report that credits have been issued.
source: New South Wales Government — Marine Estate Management Strategy
status_note: Implementation page updated on 7 July 2026 and reports continued delivery of the NSW Blue Carbon Strategy through 2027.

document_title: Blue Carbon Cost Tool
notes: The Blue Carbon Cost Tool is a publicly accessible project-development and finance decision-support resource created to estimate the costs, financing needs and potential carbon-revenue characteristics of blue-carbon conservation and restoration projects. It helps users compare development scenarios, identify where restoration or conservation may be needed, examine cost components and contribute additional data to improve future estimates. The tool is intended to make early project screening more transparent for communities, developers, buyers and investors and to support high-integrity capital mobilization. It is not a carbon-accounting methodology, registry or investment approval. Tool outputs do not establish additionality, permanence, legal rights, project eligibility or verified removals and cannot substitute for site assessment, safeguards, validation or independent verification.
source: The Nature Conservancy / Vizzuality and project partners
status_note: Publicly launched in 2025 as an active global planning and finance tool for blue-carbon project development.

document_title: Notice Issuing the CCER Methodologies for Coastal Salt-Marsh Vegetation Restoration and Seagrass-Bed Vegetation Restoration
notes: This joint notice of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment and the Ministry of Natural Resources formally releases two methodologies for China's national voluntary greenhouse-gas emission-reduction market: CCER-14-003-V01 for coastal salt-marsh vegetation restoration and CCER-14-004-V01 for seagrass-bed vegetation restoration. It encourages eligible projects to seek registration and revenue from certified reductions, requires project proponents to attest to project uniqueness and documentary integrity, and establishes supervision by provincial and municipal environmental and natural-resource authorities. Multiple eligible mangrove, salt-marsh and seagrass restoration sites within one province may be combined in one registration application, subject to separate quantification and ownership authorization. The notice creates an operational market framework but does not register projects or issue reductions automatically.
source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment and Ministry of Natural Resources, People's Republic of China
status_note: Issued on 28 November 2025, published on 3 December 2025 and effective from the date of issuance.

document_title: CCER-14-003-V01 — Methodology for Coastal Salt-Marsh Vegetation Restoration
notes: This official CCER methodology establishes eligibility, baseline, quantification, monitoring, validation and verification rules for artificial restoration of coastal salt-marsh vegetation on suitable unvegetated tidal flats or areas vacated after specified human uses. Project-area and emission-reduction ownership must be clear, planted areas must be at least 400 square metres and the crediting period must be between twenty and forty years. The methodology accounts for soil organic carbon and, where woody vegetation is used, biomass carbon, while deducting methane, nitrous-oxide and non-permanence risks. It allows additionality to be deemed for qualifying public-interest restoration and requires geospatial boundaries, field or remote-sensing monitoring and auditable records. The methodology enables certification but does not replace land, sea-use or environmental approvals and does not itself issue CCER units.
source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment and Ministry of Natural Resources, People's Republic of China
status_note: Final Version 01 was released in December 2025 and is active for eligible projects in China's national voluntary emission-reduction market.

document_title: CCER-14-004-V01 — Methodology for Seagrass-Bed Vegetation Restoration
notes: This official CCER methodology provides project-design and carbon-accounting rules for artificial seagrass restoration in suitable unvegetated intertidal or subtidal areas. It requires clear marine-area or land rights and emission-reduction ownership, compliance with applicable law and a minimum continuously planted area of 400 square metres. Eligible projects use a twenty- to forty-year crediting period and a baseline of continued absence of vegetation. The methodology quantifies changes in soil organic carbon, deducts methane and nitrous-oxide emissions and applies a non-permanence deduction, while allowing additionality to be deemed for qualifying public-interest restoration. Spatial boundaries and carbon strata must be tracked through high-resolution geospatial information and field monitoring. The document creates an accounting pathway but does not authorize planting, register a project or independently issue CCER credits.
source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment and Ministry of Natural Resources, People's Republic of China
status_note: Final Version 01 was released in December 2025 and is active for eligible seagrass-restoration projects in the national CCER market.

document_title: Public Consultation on Draft CCER Methodologies for Coastal Salt-Marsh and Seagrass-Bed Vegetation Restoration
notes: This Ministry of Ecology and Environment consultation formally invited public comments on three proposed CCER methodologies, including the draft coastal salt-marsh vegetation restoration and seagrass-bed vegetation restoration methodologies. The consultation was part of the national procedure for expanding the voluntary greenhouse-gas emission-reduction methodology system and covered project design, implementation, validation, emission-reduction calculation and verification. Government bodies, organizations, enterprises and individuals could submit comments before 15 October 2025. The document records a distinct rulemaking stage preceding final adoption and provides evidence of stakeholder participation and methodological review. It did not make the draft rules operational, authorize restoration or allow credit issuance. The consultation ended when comments closed and the two blue-carbon methodologies were subsequently finalized and released in December 2025.
source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment, People's Republic of China
status_note: Public consultation opened on 30 September 2025, closed on 15 October 2025 and was followed by final methodology issuance in December 2025.

document_title: Draft CCER Methodology for Coastal Salt-Marsh Vegetation Restoration
notes: This consultation draft set out the proposed CCER eligibility, accounting and monitoring framework for artificial coastal salt-marsh vegetation restoration before final methodology adoption. It covered ownership, minimum planting area, project boundaries, carbon pools, methane and nitrous-oxide emissions, baseline conditions, additionality, non-permanence risk and periodic field and geospatial monitoring. The draft was a formal public rulemaking version and is therefore recorded separately from the final methodology because it documents the design exposed to stakeholder review. It did not have independent crediting force, approve a site or authorize issuance of CCER units. The consultation version was superseded by CCER-14-003-V01 in December 2025, and projects must use the final methodology and other applicable legal and registry requirements rather than this draft.
source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment, People's Republic of China
status_note: Published for consultation on 30 September 2025 and superseded by final Methodology CCER-14-003-V01 in December 2025.

document_title: Draft CCER Methodology for Seagrass-Bed Vegetation Restoration
notes: This official consultation draft proposed the project rules later used to establish China's seagrass-restoration CCER methodology. It addressed artificial planting in suitable intertidal and subtidal areas, ownership of marine areas and reductions, minimum project scale, project boundaries, baseline absence of vegetation, soil-carbon accounting, greenhouse-gas deductions, non-permanence and long-term monitoring. The draft was published for comments as a distinct formal version and helps document how the national blue-carbon crediting framework developed before adoption. It was not legally sufficient for project registration, did not constitute planting or environmental authorization and could not support credit issuance on its own. The document was superseded by final Methodology CCER-14-004-V01 in December 2025, which now governs eligible projects together with registry and verification rules.
source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment, People's Republic of China
status_note: Published for consultation on 30 September 2025 and superseded by final Methodology CCER-14-004-V01 in December 2025.

document_title: Haikou Blue Carbon Economy Development Action Plan 2025–2035
notes: This municipal action plan sets a ten-year framework for building a blue-carbon economy in Haikou. Jointly issued by the municipal ecology and environment and natural-resources and planning authorities, it establishes a goal of forming a substantially developed blue-carbon economic system by the end of 2035. The plan contains twenty actions covering ecosystem protection and restoration, resource monitoring and accounting, research and technology, ecological-product value realization, finance and a proposed blue-carbon trading market. The implementation context includes extensive mangrove planting and restoration since 2020 and an earlier local blue-carbon ecological-product transaction. The plan is strategic rather than a project-level crediting methodology or permit. It does not establish additionality, verification or registry requirements and does not demonstrate that future restoration credits have been issued.
source: Haikou Municipal Government and Haikou Jiangdong New Area Administration
status_note: Jointly issued by the responsible Haikou municipal authorities in 2025 for implementation through 2035.

document_title: DENR Administrative Order No. 2026-30 — Institutionalization of the IUCN Global Standard for Nature-Based Solutions
notes: This Department of Environment and Natural Resources administrative order institutionalizes the IUCN Global Standard for Nature-based Solutions across current and future departmental policies, plans, programmes and budgets. It prioritizes rehabilitation of mangroves, coral reefs and wetlands, protection of seagrass beds and other ecosystem-based measures in climate-vulnerable coastal, watershed and urban areas. The order requires localized indicators and self-assessment, creates a technical working group, mandates a roadmap, monitoring and evaluation system, technical standards and a national Nature-based Solutions Registry, and promotes participation by local governments, Indigenous Peoples, civil society, academia and business. Funding may include public appropriations, development assistance, ecosystem-service payments and carbon or blue-carbon finance. The order does not automatically approve projects, determine carbon additionality or issue credits.
source: Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Philippines
status_note: Signed on 29 June 2026 and publicly announced by the Philippine Government on 3 July 2026.

subnational_area: Northern Samar and Southern Leyte, Eastern Visayas
document_title: Eastern Visayas Mangrove Climate-Risk Parametric Insurance Pilot
notes: The Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation and GIZ launched development of a pilot parametric climate-risk insurance product for mangrove ecosystems in Eastern Visayas. Local government units are intended to serve as policyholders, while storm-surge height and tropical-cyclone wind signals are being examined as index triggers representing damage and restoration costs. Product design, data assessment and simulation are planned for Northern Samar and Southern Leyte under the wider E4DR ecosystem-based adaptation programme. The mechanism seeks to finance rapid mangrove recovery after extreme events and reduce economic risks to coastal communities and livelihoods. It is an insurance-development pilot rather than a carbon-crediting scheme or restoration permit. The official announcement does not confirm final product approval, insurance payouts, quantified carbon benefits, verified removals or issued carbon credits.
source: Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation / GIZ / Philippine Government
status_note: A cooperation agreement was signed on 9 March 2026, with product development, simulation and a potential pilot launch planned during 2026.

document_title: Great Barrier Reef Ecosystem Accounts, Experimental Estimates, 2022–23 Financial Year
notes: These Australian Bureau of Statistics ecosystem accounts measure extent, condition and selected services across terrestrial, coastal and marine ecosystems of the Great Barrier Reef region using the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting–Ecosystem Accounting framework. The release reports seagrass extent and condition and estimates carbon retention and sequestration across mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass meadows. For 2021–22, the accounts estimate that blue-carbon ecosystems stored 196 million tonnes of carbon and sequestered 2.56 million tonnes of carbon-dioxide equivalent during the year, alongside monetary estimates and coastal-protection services. The statistics are explicitly experimental, combine multiple data sources and methods and may be revised. They support policy and natural-capital accounting but do not constitute national inventory certification, project-level baselines, verified removals or carbon credits.
source: Australian Bureau of Statistics
status_note: Released on 26 May 2026 as the first experimental Great Barrier Reef Ecosystem Accounts publication.

document_title: National Ecosystem Accounts, Experimental Estimates, 2022–23 Financial Year
notes: This Australian Bureau of Statistics release provides experimental national accounts for ecosystem extent, condition and selected services across terrestrial, freshwater, coastal and marine realms. Coastal components include salt-marsh land-use condition, mangrove canopy condition, coastal protection and carbon-retention services within the wider national accounting framework. The release reports that salt-marsh area associated with conservation or natural environments declined between 2010–11 and 2020–21, while the proportion of mangroves with high canopy cover increased. The accounts apply the international System of Environmental-Economic Accounting–Ecosystem Accounting framework and are designed to connect environmental information with policy and economic analysis. Estimates are experimental and methods may change, so the release does not establish project additionality, provide a mandatory blue-carbon inventory method, certify site-level removals or issue carbon credits.
source: Australian Bureau of Statistics
status_note: Released on 23 April 2026 as the current experimental national ecosystem-accounting publication.

document_title: National Ocean Account, Experimental Estimates, November 2022
notes: This Australian Bureau of Statistics publication consolidates experimental physical and ecosystem-service accounts for mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass. Phase Two added national estimates for salt-marsh and intertidal seagrass extent and updated coastal-protection measures, complementing earlier mangrove and broader seagrass accounts. The publication connects ecosystem extent with carbon storage and sequestration, coastal protection and economic replacement-value estimates using the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting approach and earth-observation and ecological datasets. It is a major national evidence resource for blue-carbon planning and economic accounting. The estimates are experimental, depend on mapped data coverage and generalized assumptions and are not directly equivalent to project-level greenhouse-gas accounting. The account does not establish additionality, permanence or ownership, certify national inventory submissions, validate projects or issue carbon credits.
source: Australian Bureau of Statistics
status_note: Released on 29 November 2022 as Phase Two of Australia's experimental National Ocean Account and retained as an active evidence resource.

document_title: BioCarbon Standard Version 4.1
notes: BioCarbon Standard Version 4.1 is the overarching normative framework governing certification, registration and ex-post issuance of Verified Carbon Credits under the BioCarbon greenhouse-gas crediting programme. It applies alongside approved methodologies, including the programme's blue-carbon methodology, and establishes requirements for legal compliance, baselines, additionality, uncertainty, leakage, permanence, validation, verification, registry operation and credit issuance. The revision strengthens safeguards for Indigenous Peoples and local communities, including participation, benefit sharing, grievance mechanisms, data sovereignty and Free, Prior and Informed Consent where applicable. It is a programme-wide standard rather than a marine methodology or government permit. A blue-carbon activity must still satisfy the applicable methodology, national rules and independent conformity assessment, and no credits are issued solely because the umbrella standard is published.
source: BioCarbon Cert
status_note: Version 4.1 took effect on 13 April 2026 and is the current umbrella standard for BioCarbon greenhouse-gas projects.

document_title: BioCarbon Multi-Methodology Framework Version 1.0
notes: This normative BioCarbon framework governs use of two methodologies within one project document when both belong to the same BioCarbon sectoral scope. It requires distinct accounting units, baselines, causal mechanisms and greenhouse-gas outcomes, with consistent and traceable attribution and safeguards against overlapping quantification, double counting and double claiming. The framework is relevant to integrated coastal and blue-carbon projects that may combine qualifying activities under separate methodologies within the same sector, but it does not authorize cross-sector combinations or override the rules of either methodology. It is mandatory for projects choosing the multi-methodology structure, yet it is not a standalone carbon-removal methodology, project approval or environmental permit. Registration, validation, monitoring, verification and credit issuance remain subject to the underlying methods and full programme requirements.
source: BioCarbon Cert
status_note: Version 1.0 was published and became effective on 3 July 2026 for applicable BioCarbon projects.

document_title: Sri Lanka Coast Guard Blue-Green Domain Mangrove and Coastal Plantation Programme
notes: The Sri Lanka Coast Guard's Blue-Green Domain initiative integrates coastal and marine ecosystem stewardship into operational activities and community engagement. Its plantation programme works with national research, coastal-conservation and forest authorities to establish mangrove and native coastal trees at selected sites, operate local nurseries and improve survival through location-appropriate species and management. The official programme page describes a partnership intended to plant 10,000 mangrove and 10,000 Mudilla trees annually, alongside community events, shoreline restoration and broader coral, turtle and pollution-control activities. The programme directly implements coastal habitat enhancement, but it is not registered as a carbon project. The source does not provide a blue-carbon baseline, additionality assessment, permanence buffer, independently verified removals or issued credits.
source: Sri Lanka Coast Guard and national conservation partners
status_note: Active institutional programme in 2026, with ongoing nursery, planting and community-engagement activities along Sri Lanka's coast.

document_title: Training Workshop on Conservation, Restoration and Sustainable Use of Blue Carbon Ecosystems in Mullaitivu District
notes: Sri Lanka's Ministry of Environment and Forest Department organized this two-day capacity-building programme for approximately eighty officers from stakeholder institutions in Mullaitivu and Kilinochchi. Classroom and field activities covered mangroves, salt marshes and seagrasses in the Nayaru Lagoon area and included a practical demonstration using the national guidelines for mangrove ecosystem restoration. Technical experts emphasized that mangrove projects must avoid damaging adjacent seagrass and salt-marsh ecosystems, reinforcing ecosystem-level planning and safeguards rather than single-habitat planting. The programme transferred approved restoration practice and improved institutional coordination, but it was not a restoration permit, funded landscape-scale intervention or carbon-credit project. It did not establish project baselines, quantify net removals, validate a methodology or issue credits.
source: Ministry of Environment and Forest Department, Sri Lanka
status_note: Completed on 20–21 June 2025, with the official ministry record subsequently updated in July 2026.

document_title: Independent Review of Greenhouse Gas Removals
notes: This independent review assesses the role of greenhouse-gas removals in the United Kingdom's pathway to net zero and includes a dedicated assessment of marine carbon dioxide removal. It reviews ocean alkalinity enhancement, ocean fertilization, direct removal of CO2 from seawater, and macroalgae cultivation and sinking, while emphasizing low technology readiness, immature MRV systems, uncertain long-term environmental effects, and the need for coordinated research, investment, and adaptive governance. The review concludes that marine approaches are not yet deployable at commercial scale and were not included among the UK's low-regret deployment options because the evidence base remains insufficient. Its recommendations are advisory and do not constitute agreed government policy, a deployment authorization, or a carbon-crediting methodology.
source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
status_note: Published independent review; recommendations are advisory

document_title: A Metadata Template for Ocean Carbon, Ocean Acidification, and mCDR Data Management, Version 4.5
notes: NOAA's Ocean Carbon and Acidification Data System published Version 4.5 of a standardized metadata template for ocean-carbon, ocean-acidification, and marine carbon-dioxide-removal data. The template supports consistent documentation, archival quality control, long-term accessibility, interoperability, and reuse of observations, experiments, and model outputs, including data from ocean alkalinity enhancement research. It strengthens the data and metadata foundation needed for monitoring and future MRV development, but it does not establish a carbon-accounting formula, certify project performance, authorize field deployment, or create credits.
source: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information — Ocean Carbon and Acidification Data System
status_note: Published metadata template in active use

document_title: Studies in Support of the Implementation of the Mission — Wetlands and Blue Carbon Workshop Report
notes: This CINEA workshop report records stakeholder review of the evidence developed under the EU study on wetlands and blue carbon. The workshop was organized to test, validate, and supplement preliminary findings and to collect technical and policy feedback relevant to wetland carbon assessment, restoration, monitoring, and implementation of the EU Mission framework. The report is an evidence-building and consultation output rather than an adopted methodology, binding restoration target, funding award, or project permit; it does not itself quantify verified additional removals.
source: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency
status_note: Published workshop report supporting an ongoing EU study

document_title: Japan–Brazil Technical Meeting on Blue Carbon
notes: Japan's Ministry of the Environment and Brazil's environment and fisheries ministries held the first sector-specific policy dialogue under their 2025 environmental cooperation memorandum. The meeting exchanged information on blue-carbon policy, greenhouse-gas inventories, accounting approaches, mangrove conservation, seaweed aquaculture, evaluation of carbon fixation, possible blue-carbon credit design, and future joint development of scientifically grounded assessment methods. The meeting strengthens bilateral coordination and knowledge sharing, but it did not adopt a common accounting methodology, establish a bilateral crediting mechanism, allocate project funding, authorize deployment, or quantify removals.
source: Ministry of the Environment, Japan; Ministry of the Environment and Climate Change, Brazil; Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture, Brazil
status_note: Technical policy-dialogue meeting completed on 29 June 2026; bilateral cooperation continues

document_title: Province of Iloilo–ZSL Philippines Partnership for Coastal Protection and Blue Carbon Capacity Building
notes: The Provincial Government of Iloilo and ZSL-Philippines signed a memorandum of understanding for mangrove and beach-forest rehabilitation, improved management of marine protected areas, blue-carbon research, technical assistance, training, community capability building, and sharing of monitoring reports. Iloilo is to identify suitable planting sites, support protective policies, and work with local communities and people's organizations, while ZSL-Philippines provides technical and research support. The partnership is an active restoration and capacity-building framework, but the official announcement does not specify a quantified carbon-removal target, a carbon-credit methodology, a financing amount, or issuance of verified credits.
source: Provincial Government of Iloilo
status_note: Signed memorandum of understanding under implementation

subnational_area: Selected coastal habitats in West Bengal, Odisha and Chilika Lake
document_title: Carbon Storage in Seagrass and Mangrove Habitats in India and Its Implications for Global Estimates of Blue Carbon Ecosystem Service
notes: This nationally funded research project measures sedimentary carbon stocks, sequestration rates, and carbon sources in salt marsh, mangrove, and seagrass habitats in eastern India. The work uses sediment cores, elemental analysis, stable isotopes, and radiometric dating to reduce uncertainty in national and global blue-carbon estimates and to inform possible economic valuation. The official project page lists a 2023–2026 timeline and a budget of INR 5,101,360. It is a scientific assessment project rather than a restoration deployment, legal accounting method, crediting programme, or verified claim of additional carbon removal; completion had not been confirmed on the cited page.
source: India Science, Technology & Innovation Portal; Anusandhan National Research Foundation / Science and Engineering Research Board
status_note: Funded research project with a listed 2023–2026 project window; completion not confirmed

subnational_area: Vellar and Coleroon estuarine complex, Tamil Nadu
document_title: Mangrove Carbon Stock Assessment in the Vellar and Coleroon Estuarine Complex, Tamil Nadu
notes: This ANRF/SERB-funded project investigates mangrove carbon stocks and the lateral export of dissolved inorganic carbon, dissolved and particulate organic carbon, alkalinity, pCO2, and CO2 fluxes from the Vellar and Coleroon estuarine complex to adjacent coastal waters. It addresses a major evidence gap by examining carbon and alkalinity pathways in addition to sediment burial. The official page lists a 2023–2026 timeline and a budget of INR 2,752,200. The project is research and monitoring only; it does not authorize restoration, establish a national inventory factor or crediting methodology, or demonstrate verified additional removals, and completion was not confirmed on the cited page.
source: India Science, Technology & Innovation Portal; Anusandhan National Research Foundation / Science and Engineering Research Board
status_note: Funded research project with a listed 2023–2026 project window; completion not confirmed

document_title: Seagrass Greenhouse-Gas Emissions Baseline and Marine-Sector Emissions Data Governance Process
notes: Indonesia's Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries initiated a technical process to agree a greenhouse-gas emissions baseline for seagrass ecosystems and to strengthen integrated governance of marine and fisheries emissions data. The process aligns calculation approaches, supports transparent reporting, monitoring and evaluation, and is intended to improve activity data, develop nationally specific emission factors, and reduce uncertainty through field verification. It is an initial methodological and data-governance foundation for national blue-carbon policy. The announcement does not show that a final national methodology has been legally adopted, that a crediting mechanism has been created, or that any project removals have been verified.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Indonesia
status_note: Technical baseline and data-governance development process underway

document_title: Integrated Blue Carbon GHG Reporting, Validation and Verification, and Blue Carbon Economy Training Series
notes: Indonesia's Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Climateworks Centre–Monash University, and PKSPL IPB University launched an integrated three-part capacity-building series covering greenhouse-gas reporting from blue-carbon ecosystems, validation and verification of mitigation projects, and development of the blue-carbon economy. Training includes IPCC and UNFCCC standards, field-data collection, carbon-stock analysis for mangroves and seagrass, credible MRV, and high-integrity project assessment. The programme strengthens institutional competence and cross-sector coordination but does not itself accredit validation bodies, approve a project methodology, issue credits, or verify a specific quantity of removals.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Indonesia
status_note: Integrated national capacity-building series launched in 2026

country_or_region: European Union and European Economic Area
document_title: PluriCarb — Transnational Carbon Governance: Legal Pluralism and Cross-Border CCS Regulation in the North Sea
notes: PluriCarb is an EU-funded socio-legal research project examining regulatory fragmentation, jurisdictional overlap, and institutional responses affecting cross-border carbon capture and storage in the North Sea. It compares the Greensand, Northern Lights, and Porthos projects and is intended to produce legal analysis, policy briefs, and actionable recommendations for EU/EEA and EFTA regulators and civil society. The project runs from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2028 with an EU contribution of EUR 263,393.28. It studies governance rather than approving storage operations, changing treaty obligations, or demonstrating that the referenced CCS projects deliver atmospheric carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: EU-funded research project active from April 2026 to March 2028

subnational_area: Deep and open ocean, including areas beyond national jurisdiction
document_title: OceanSOS — Creating a Safe Operating Space for the Deep and Open Ocean
notes: OceanSOS is a Horizon Europe research and innovation project that evaluates how existing and emerging human activities affect deep and open-ocean food webs, bentho-pelagic coupling, the biological carbon pump, climate regulation, and biodiversity. It combines fieldwork, models, regional workshops, socioeconomic analysis, and public-risk research to create a safe-operating-space framework for European, regional, and global ocean management, including areas beyond national jurisdiction. The project runs from 1 May 2026 to 30 April 2030 with an EU contribution of EUR 6,494,831.25. It is a research and precautionary-governance programme, not a marine CDR deployment project, removal-credit method, or authorization for an emerging ocean activity.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Horizon Europe project active from May 2026 to April 2030

document_title: Floresta Viva Grouped Blue-Carbon Certification Model for Manguezais do Brasil Projects
notes: BNDES and the Floresta Viva programme launched procurement for specialist support to structure a grouped carbon-project certification model for small and community-based mangrove-restoration initiatives financed through the Manguezais do Brasil call. The selected consultancy is expected to prepare a project design document, organize multiple restoration initiatives under a common structure, and develop reference materials intended to reduce certification costs and improve access to carbon-credit markets. Eight restoration projects had received combined support of BRL 53.3 million under the existing call. The certification model was still being developed at the cited stage; no final methodology, validated grouped project, registered credits, or verified removal volume was reported.
source: Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES); Floresta Viva; Funbio
status_note: Procurement launched and certification model under development; final approval not evidenced

document_title: Floresta Viva Sergipe Ecological Restoration Initiative
notes: BNDES and the Government of Sergipe announced a Floresta Viva initiative intended to mobilize up to BRL 100 million for ecological restoration across the state's hinterland, agreste, and coastal areas, including mangroves and restingas. The programme is framed around recovery of degraded areas, carbon capture, water security, employment, family agriculture, and the local bioeconomy. At the cited announcement stage, the funding envelope was potential rather than fully contracted and detailed project calls, sites, baselines, monitoring rules, and quantified blue-carbon removal targets were not yet evidenced. The record therefore represents a planned enabling programme, not verified carbon removal or an approved crediting mechanism.
source: Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES) and Government of Sergipe
status_note: Programme announced with a potential funding envelope; detailed contracting not yet evidenced

document_title: ISO/WD 21205 — Requirements for Determining Short-Term Blue Carbon Increment of Tidal Wetlands
notes: ISO/WD 21205 is a working draft specifying approaches for determining short-term changes in tidal-wetland blue-carbon stocks using surface elevation tables, incremental carbon calculations, and associated network requirements. The work is intended to improve measurement consistency for changes in surface-sediment carbon stocks. As of the cited ISO status, the project remained under development in the preparatory stage and had not become an International Standard. It therefore provides a draft technical direction only and cannot yet be treated as a final certification rule, adopted accounting method, or basis for issued carbon credits.
source: International Organization for Standardization — ISO/TC 8/SC 13
status_note: Working draft under development; not an International Standard

document_title: ISO/AWI 26715 — Vegetation Distribution Monitoring for Intertidal Blue Carbon Ecosystems Using Optical Remote-Sensing Imagery
notes: ISO/AWI 26715 is an approved work item to develop technical requirements for monitoring vegetation-distribution changes in intertidal blue-carbon ecosystems using high-resolution optical imagery, field validation, data analysis, and quality control. It is intended for natural, restored, and managed intertidal wetlands and for use by researchers, policymakers, carbon-project developers, and other monitoring stakeholders. The project was registered in the ISO work programme in June 2026 and remained at an early preparatory stage. No final standard had been published, so it does not yet create mandatory MRV obligations, certify a project, or support credit issuance by itself.
source: International Organization for Standardization — ISO/TC 8/SC 13
status_note: Approved work item at an early preparatory stage; final standard not published

document_title: Carbon Removal and Methane Reduction from Eutrophic Systems — Draft Methodology Consultation
notes: Gold Standard opened public consultation on a draft methodology for quantifying carbon removal through sediment burial and methane avoidance from mitigation of harmful algal blooms in eligible eutrophic freshwater, brackish, and similar coastal systems. The proposal includes conservative baselines, remote sensing validated by field sampling, sediment-core verification, third-party verification, uncertainty deductions, reversal rules, buffer contributions, deferred crediting for removals, and environmental and community safeguards. The consultation closed in May 2026, but the cited page describes a methodology under review rather than a final approved standard. No project is authorized, no credits are issued, and applicability to a specific coastal intervention remains subject to the final rules and project-level validation.
source: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
status_note: Public consultation closed; draft methodology not yet evidenced as finally approved

document_title: Japan's National Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Removals in FY2024 — Blue Carbon Reporting
notes: Japan's official FY2024 greenhouse-gas inventory release reports approximately 0.32 Mt-CO2 of removals attributed to blue-carbon ecosystems, broadly unchanged from the preceding fiscal year. The figure is presented as an aggregate national inventory estimate rather than a project-level credit issuance, deployment authorization or verified additional removal claim. The release strengthens national reporting and accounting evidence for coastal blue carbon but does not itself establish a new restoration programme or carbon-market methodology.
source: Ministry of the Environment, Government of Japan
status_note: Official national inventory results released in April 2026

document_title: Project for Advancing Nationally Determined Contributions Targets through Innovative Mangrove Blue Carbon Management as a Nature-based Solution
notes: The project was provisionally selected for Japan's FY2026 SATREPS programme to develop innovative mangrove blue-carbon management in Indonesia as a nature-based solution supporting nationally determined contribution targets. Planned work combines scientific assessment, management methods, monitoring and bilateral capacity building. Selection remains conditional on the conclusion of intergovernmental and technical-cooperation agreements, and the official notice states that the project may be modified or terminated. It therefore represents a planned research and management programme, not a deployment permit, operational carbon-credit system or verified carbon-removal outcome.
source: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) / Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST)
status_note: Provisionally selected for FY2026 SATREPS; implementation remains subject to required agreements

document_title: Mangrove Methane Cycling and National Blue-Carbon Accounting — ARC DECRA DE240100305
notes: This Australian Research Council Discovery Early Career Researcher Award supports Southern Cross University research on methane cycling in mangrove ecosystems. The active grant runs from July 2024 through December 2026 and has current funding of AUD 500,199. It is intended to produce the first Australian-scale estimate of mangrove methane emissions and improve the treatment of methane in blue-carbon accounting. The activity is scientific research and national evidence development only; it does not authorize restoration, establish a carbon-credit methodology or demonstrate net carbon removal.
source: Australian Research Council
status_note: Active research grant scheduled from July 2024 to December 2026

document_title: Our Marine Environment 2025 — National Coastal Blue-Carbon Assessment
notes: New Zealand's national marine-environment assessment provides the country's first nationwide estimate of vegetated coastal blue-carbon habitat and sequestration. It identifies approximately 20,932 hectares of saltmarsh, 30,533 hectares of mangroves and 61,340 hectares of seagrass, with estimated annual sequestration of about 57,800 tonnes of carbon; it also reports a larger estimated contribution from unvegetated estuarine sediments. The report evaluates restoration potential and estimates that restoring historical habitat could raise annual sequestration, but these figures are national-scale estimates and scenarios rather than verified project removals, issued credits or implementation authorizations.
source: New Zealand Ministry for the Environment / Stats NZ
status_note: Official national environmental assessment published in October 2025

subnational_area: Te Tauihu / top of the South Island
document_title: Core and Restore — Te Tauihu Coastal Blue-Carbon Pilot
notes: The Core and Restore pilot was launched in November 2021 to measure, protect and restore saltmarsh and seagrass habitats in Te Tauihu. It is presented within New Zealand's emissions-reduction planning as an applied nature-based pilot that builds local evidence while testing practical restoration and stewardship approaches. The programme supports habitat protection, monitoring and restoration, but the cited government material does not establish a national carbon-credit methodology, quantify verified additional removals or confer a regulatory authorization for wider deployment.
source: New Zealand Ministry for the Environment
status_note: Pilot launched in November 2021; no official closure identified in the cited programme material

subnational_area: Seaflower Biosphere Reserve, Archipelago of San Andrés, Providencia and Santa Catalina
document_title: Seaflower Biosphere Reserve Mangrove Blue Carbon Project
notes: The regional environmental authority reported formal socialization of a mangrove blue-carbon project for the Seaflower Biosphere Reserve. The initiative is designed to strengthen conservation and sustainable management of mangrove ecosystems through community participation, project activities, implementation scheduling and local participation mechanisms. It is an active subnational conservation and management project, but the official material reviewed does not document issued carbon credits, a quantified verified removal result or an independent deployment permit beyond the project framework.
source: Corporación para el Desarrollo Sostenible del Archipiélago de San Andrés, Providencia y Santa Catalina (CORALINA)
status_note: Project socialization and implementation engagement reported in June 2026

country_or_region: Colombia / ASEAN / Association of Caribbean States
document_title: Colombia–ASEAN–Caribbean Blue Carbon and Coastal Resilience Capacity-Building Phase
notes: This international cooperation phase strengthens technical and institutional capacity on blue carbon and coastal resilience among Colombia, ASEAN participants and members of the Association of Caribbean States, with participation from specialized Colombian and international partners. Its substantive role is knowledge exchange, training, cooperation and policy-capacity development rather than direct ecosystem deployment. The programme does not itself create a carbon-credit mechanism, approve a marine intervention or report quantified carbon-removal results.
source: Presidential Agency for International Cooperation of Colombia (APC-Colombia)
status_note: International capacity-building phase reported as active in 2025

document_title: São Paulo Mangrove Blue-Carbon and Toxic-Elements Inventory Project
notes: São Paulo State entered a two-year technical cooperation agreement with the University of São Paulo's carbon research centre to inventory blue carbon and toxic elements in coastal mangroves. The project plans approximately 2,000 soil samples across the São Paulo coast and will generate technical reports intended to support environmental policy, biodiversity protection and bioeconomy decisions. It is an active research and inventory programme focused on carbon stocks and environmental condition; it does not constitute a carbon-credit issuance programme, a quantified additional-removal claim or authorization for a new intervention.
source: Secretariat for Environment, Infrastructure and Logistics of the State of São Paulo
status_note: Two-year cooperation agreement signed in 2025

document_title: Conectando Sociobiodiversidade, Biodiversidade e Carbono Azul — SinBiose Project
notes: The project titled 'Conectando Sociobiodiversidade, Biodiversidade e Carbono Azul' was listed among the preliminarily approved proposals under Brazilian Call CNPq/MMA/CONFAP/FAPs No. 15/2025 for synthesis research on biodiversity and ecosystem services. The broader call announced a total funding envelope of BRL 6 million for nine projects, but the official result reviewed does not identify a final project-specific award amount or confirm completion of all contracting steps. The record is therefore classified as under review and evidence-building, not as an operational restoration programme, deployment authorization or carbon-credit activity.
source: National Council for Scientific and Technological Development (CNPq), Brazil
status_note: Preliminarily approved under Call No. 15/2025; final contracting and project-specific funding were not confirmed in the cited result

document_title: Integrative Approaches for Preservation and Restoration of Blue-Carbon Ecosystems in Southern Santa Catarina
notes: This collaborative research project between the State University of Santa Catarina and the Municipality of Laguna applies integrated approaches to assess blue-carbon ecosystems and generate evidence for their preservation and restoration in southern Santa Catarina. Its planned outputs include scientific data capable of informing local conservation and restoration policy. The initiative is primarily a research and policy-support project; the official description does not establish a carbon-credit methodology, quantify verified additional removals or authorize a specific large-scale restoration deployment.
source: Municipality of Laguna / State University of Santa Catarina (UDESC)
status_note: Collaborative research project reported as active in November 2025

document_title: Iskandar Puteri Blue Carbon Initiative
notes: The Iskandar Puteri Blue Carbon Initiative is a local-government programme for conserving and restoring mangroves, seagrass and coastal wetlands through ecosystem mapping, public education, partnerships and community-oriented support. It provides an implementation and coordination platform for local blue-carbon action rather than merely describing the ecosystems. The available official project page does not establish a formal carbon-credit methodology, report issued credits or quantify independently verified net carbon removal.
source: Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP)
status_note: Local blue-carbon initiative launched and reported as active in 2025

subnational_area: Twelve coastal states and union territories assessed by the Forest Survey of India
document_title: Parliament Question: Blue Carbon Mapping Initiatives
notes: The official parliamentary answer describes blue-carbon mapping and assessment undertaken by the Forest Survey of India across twelve coastal states and union territories. It links the resulting evidence to national carbon budgeting, India's nationally determined contribution and implementation priorities under the Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes programme. The answer consolidates official mapping and policy-use information but does not itself create a new law, funding award, carbon-credit mechanism or quantified project-level removal claim.
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
status_note: Official parliamentary answer issued in August 2025

document_title: Thailand Advances Blue Carbon Strategy to Support Net Zero Goal
notes: The Thai government announced a national blue-carbon strategy centred on mangrove conservation and restoration, institutional alliances and the contribution of coastal ecosystems to the country's 2050 net-zero objective. The announcement provides a supportive national policy direction and coordination framework for blue-carbon action. The cited government page does not supply a standalone legally binding strategy text, a quantified blue-carbon removal target, a complete MRV methodology or an operational crediting mechanism, so the record is classified as a non-binding active strategy rather than a regulatory or market instrument.
source: Government Public Relations Department, Thailand
status_note: Government strategy announcement published in July 2026

subnational_area: Masinloc and Oyon Bay Protected Landscape and Seascape, Zambales
document_title: MOBPLS Mangrove Blue Carbon Stock Monitoring Report 2024
notes: The official protected-area monitoring report records a 10.62 percent increase in measured mangrove blue-carbon stock between the 2023 and 2024 monitoring rounds and reports a total stock of approximately 97,283.36 Mg CO2e for the assessed sites. It provides site-level monitoring evidence for mangrove condition and carbon storage in the protected landscape and seascape. The reported change is a monitoring result for ecosystem carbon stock and should not be treated as an independently verified additional-removal credit, a national accounting factor or authorization for a new restoration project.
source: Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Philippines
status_note: Completed 2024 monitoring report; added to the official e-library in 2026

document_title: Abu Dhabi Blue Carbon Demonstration Project
notes: The Abu Dhabi Blue Carbon Demonstration Project assessed the distribution, carbon stocks, ecosystem services and economic value of mangroves, saltmarshes, seagrass and other coastal blue-carbon habitats. A later Environment Agency summary reports that the assessed ecosystems stored more than 41 million tonnes of CO2e, which is a standing carbon-stock estimate rather than an annual removal rate. The completed project established a scientific and policy evidence base but did not issue carbon credits, authorize a new marine intervention or verify additional project removals.
source: Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi
status_note: Completed demonstration project initiated in 2012

document_title: UAE National Blue Carbon Project — Phase II
notes: Phase II expanded the blue-carbon assessment beyond Abu Dhabi to northern and eastern parts of the United Arab Emirates, broadening national understanding of coastal carbon stocks, ecosystem services and economic value. The completed project functioned as a national evidence and valuation exercise supporting policy development. It did not itself establish a mandatory national accounting standard, authorize restoration deployment or create an operational carbon-credit issuance mechanism.
source: Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi / Government partners of the United Arab Emirates
status_note: Completed national blue-carbon assessment phase initiated in 2015

document_title: UAE Mangroves Annual Carbon Sequestration Trial Study
notes: The completed trial study estimated an annual mangrove soil carbon-sequestration rate of approximately 0.5 tonnes per hectare per year. Its purpose was to improve empirical understanding of annual sequestration in UAE mangrove settings and support blue-carbon science and accounting. The official January 2022 announcement confirms completion but does not state an earlier formal publication year, so 2022 is used as the documented completion-reporting year. The result is a study-specific estimate and is not identified as a legally adopted national emission factor, a verified project-credit quantity or proof of large-scale deployment.
source: Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi
status_note: Completed trial study documented in the official January 2022 completion announcement

document_title: Blue Carbon Environmental and Social Responsibility Project — Mirfa Lagoon
notes: The completed project used drone technology to plant more than 35,000 mangrove seeds in Mirfa Lagoon and reported a success rate exceeding 35 percent. It is a concrete restoration and technology-demonstration activity with environmental and social-responsibility objectives. The official summary does not provide a quantified net CO2-removal result, permanence assessment, independent verification or carbon-credit issuance, so the record reflects implemented restoration rather than a certified removal project.
source: Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi
status_note: Completed mangrove planting and drone-technology demonstration project

document_title: Abu Dhabi Mangrove Initiative
notes: Launched in February 2022, the Abu Dhabi Mangrove Initiative is an umbrella programme bringing together mangrove protection, restoration, scientific research, innovation and international collaboration. The Environment Agency describes it as a comprehensive platform for Abu Dhabi's mangrove and blue-carbon projects, with an emphasis on applying the best available science and technology. The cited initiative page does not establish a carbon-credit methodology or quantify verified additional removals, so its principal role is enabling restoration, research coordination and policy implementation.
source: Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi
status_note: Comprehensive initiative launched in February 2022 and reported as active

document_title: Jebel Ali Beach Development Project — Mangrove Beach Component
notes: Dubai approved a 6.6-kilometre, 330-hectare Jebel Ali beach development plan that includes a 1.6-kilometre mangrove beach component intended to support the area's blue-carbon footprint while protecting turtles and other coastal ecosystems. The record concerns an approved public master plan whose mangrove component is planned rather than a completed restoration outcome. The official announcement does not provide a quantified carbon-removal target, project MRV system or carbon-crediting arrangement, and implementation remains dependent on subsequent design and construction work.
source: Government of Dubai Media Office
status_note: Master plan approved in July 2024; mangrove component remained planned in the cited announcement

document_title: Delta Wetland Resilience and Blue Carbon
notes: This completed California research project received an award of USD 819,998 and ran through the 2019–2023 period to model wetland carbon storage, greenhouse-gas fluxes, land-surface elevation and restoration or rice-management scenarios in the Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta. The work developed decision-support evidence for resilient wetland management and blue-carbon planning. It was a modelling and assessment project rather than an implemented restoration authorization, an issued carbon-credit programme or a verified project-level removal outcome.
source: Delta Stewardship Council, State of California
status_note: Completed research project awarded in 2019 and implemented through 2023

subnational_area: Northwest Shelf and northern coast of Western Australia
document_title: Blue Carbon Seascapes Project
notes: The AUD 20 million Blue Carbon Seascapes Project, jointly funded by the Australian Institute of Marine Science and BHP, investigates how carbon moves through and is stored in coastal and deeper marine environments along Western Australia's northern coast. After approximately one year of fieldwork, the official 2025 update reported 6,052 samples collected from 81 sites. The project is intended to improve understanding of carbon protection and enhancement opportunities, but it remains a research programme and does not itself authorize marine carbon-removal deployment, report verified net removals or create a crediting methodology.
source: Australian Institute of Marine Science / BHP
status_note: Active multi-year research project documented in the official February 2025 progress update

document_title: Ejido Médanos de San Esteban Mangrove Payment for Environmental Services Project
notes: The Ejido Médanos de San Esteban in Ahome, Sinaloa applied in 2023 and obtained support under Mexico's Payment for Environmental Services programme through 2028. The agreement covers conservation of 702 hectares of mangrove and finances community surveillance, monitoring, cleaning and protection activities. It provides an economic incentive for stewardship of an existing mangrove ecosystem and therefore combines conservation implementation with ecological-compensation finance. It is not identified as a carbon-credit project, does not report issued offsets and does not quantify additional carbon removal attributable solely to the payment contract.
source: National Forestry Commission (CONAFOR), Mexico
status_note: Payment for Environmental Services support awarded following the 2023 application and scheduled through 2028

document_title: Direct Air Capture and Blue Carbon Removal Technology Program — FY2020 NDAA Section 223
notes: Section 223 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 directed the U.S. Department of Defense to establish a programme for research, development, testing, evaluation, study and demonstration of direct air capture and blue-carbon removal technologies. The statutory definition of blue-carbon capture includes engineered or inorganic removal of dissolved carbon dioxide from seawater, and the programme may use grants and military test locations; subsequent amendments require reporting by September 30, 2026. The law supports technology research and demonstration but does not itself authorize a particular marine discharge, establish environmental permitting conditions or demonstrate successful net removal at scale.
source: United States Congress
status_note: Enacted on December 20, 2019 and subsequently amended; statutory programme and reporting duties remain active

document_title: Blue Carbon Policy Road Map 2025–2028
notes: The national roadmap formalises blue-carbon conservation as a climate-policy priority for 2025–2028 and links protection of mangroves and seagrass meadows with coastal-community resilience, national climate strategies and international climate objectives. It was developed through consultations involving national and provincial authorities, research institutions, civil-society organisations and coastal communities. The roadmap provides a policy and coordination framework rather than a project permit, an approved carbon-credit methodology or evidence of verified additional removals. Implementation outcomes will depend on subsequent programmes, financing, monitoring arrangements and legally effective measures.
source: Papua New Guinea Climate Change and Development Authority (CCDA)
status_note: Published on 18 December 2025; the roadmap applies to the 2025–2028 period.

document_title: National Blue Carbon Task Force
notes: The Government launched the National Blue Carbon Task Force to coordinate public agencies, researchers and other stakeholders working on blue-carbon policy, capacity building and nature-based solutions. The initiative is connected to national work on seagrass conservation and rehabilitation and on determining the carbon-sequestration capacity of Mauritian seagrass ecosystems. It is intended to develop recommendations and identify adaptation-finance opportunities, but the launch announcement does not establish a carbon-credit registry, approve a financing mechanism, authorise a restoration project or report verified carbon removals.
source: Government of Mauritius — Ministry of Blue Economy, Marine Resources, Fisheries and Shipping
status_note: Launched on 4 June 2024 as an active national coordination mechanism.

document_title: Wise Use of Caribbean Wetlands for Climate Change Mitigation and Conservation of their Ecosystem Services
notes: The regional project supported eight Caribbean countries in improving the management and wise use of internationally important wetlands for climate mitigation, adaptation and ecosystem-service protection. Its work included status, ecosystem-service and climate-vulnerability assessments for 21 Ramsar sites, identification of priority sites, establishment of monitoring programmes in eight wetlands, stakeholder capacity building and policy engagement intended to strengthen national legal and institutional frameworks. The programme ended in July 2026. It did not create a regional carbon-credit standard or document verified net carbon removals, and the participating wetlands are broader than a single blue-carbon ecosystem type.
source: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) / International Climate Initiative (IKI)
status_note: Implemented from July 2020 to July 2026; the stated project period has ended.

country_or_region: Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu
document_title: Strengthening Coastal Biodiversity Conservation and Management through Protection and Rehabilitation Incentives for Coastal Carbon Sinks in Pacific Island Countries
notes: The completed regional programme mapped mangrove and seagrass stocks, modelled their carbon-sink functions and estimated the economic value of associated ecosystem services in four Pacific island countries. It supported governments in developing protection, management and rehabilitation measures and in strengthening measurement, reporting and verification approaches that could underpin future incentive systems. The project combined evidence building, policy development and practical restoration support, but its official project description does not state that it issued carbon credits, established a binding regional methodology or verified a quantified volume of additional removals.
source: International Climate Initiative (IKI) / Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ)
status_note: Implemented from December 2018 to May 2026; officially listed as completed.

country_or_region: India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand and Timor-Leste
document_title: Conservation of Seagrass Ecosystems — Safeguarding Food Security and Resilience in Vulnerable Coastal Communities
notes: The Indo-Pacific programme supports seagrass conservation while addressing food security, livelihoods, biodiversity and carbon sequestration. Local organisations and communities are trained in participatory science to collect data, identify important seagrass areas and use the resulting evidence in engagement with decision makers. The programme also develops alternative business models intended to contribute funds for long-term conservation. It remains active through December 2026. The official description does not report a quantified restoration target, verified additional carbon removal, a formal carbon-accounting methodology or issuance of seagrass carbon credits.
source: International Climate Initiative (IKI) / Convention on Migratory Species Secretariat
status_note: Implemented from January 2019 through December 2026; officially listed as open.

document_title: Ensuring Sustainable Coastal Protection by Means of Biodiversity Conservation in Marine Ecosystems Affected by Typhoons in the Philippines
notes: The completed programme supported participatory coastal-zone management and restoration of mangrove and coastal forests in typhoon-affected areas. It developed site-specific protected-area management and mangrove-rehabilitation plans for eight sites in Bohol, strengthened local capacities and contributed to improvements in the policy and legal framework for coastal and species protection. Its primary framing was biodiversity conservation, climate resilience and coastal protection rather than quantified carbon removal. The programme did not establish a blue-carbon crediting methodology, report verified net removals or provide a continuing deployment authorisation after project completion.
source: International Climate Initiative (IKI) / Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ)
status_note: Implemented from November 2018 to July 2022; officially listed as completed.

document_title: Kwale–Tanga Coast — Transboundary Conservation and Sustainable Management of Coastal and Marine Biodiversity
notes: The active transboundary programme establishes participatory governance and sustainable-management arrangements for coastal and marine biodiversity in Kenya and Tanzania. In Kenya, project partners have implemented mangrove conservation and restoration with Mikoko Pamoja and the Kenya Marine and Fisheries Research Institute and have analysed blue-carbon and sustainable-fisheries potential in Kwale County. The project also strengthens community participation, livelihoods and protected-area governance. Although carbon-finance opportunities are relevant to the programme, the project page does not itself create a crediting mechanism, quantify verified removals or approve a separate commercial carbon project.
source: International Climate Initiative (IKI) / Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ)
status_note: Implemented from January 2023 through March 2027; officially listed as open.

document_title: Protection of Carbon Pools and Sinks in Wetlands and Protected Areas in Panama
notes: The completed project supported management of approximately 13,800 hectares of protected wetlands and generated information on the amount of carbon stored by Panamanian mangrove ecosystems. It strengthened national and local capacities, developed mangrove-management and climate-adaptation materials, supported carbon-monitoring protocol development and implemented practical conservation and restoration activities. These outputs created an evidence and management foundation for future blue-carbon action. The programme did not establish a national carbon-crediting standard, issue credits or report an independently verified volume of additional removals attributable to the project.
source: International Climate Initiative (IKI) / United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
status_note: Implemented from March 2013 to February 2018; officially listed as completed.

country_or_region: Fiji, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga and Vanuatu
document_title: Pacific Mangroves Initiative for Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation
notes: The regional initiative supported Pacific island communities in adapting to climate change and maintaining livelihoods through improved mangrove management. It collected and analysed ecosystem data, developed climate scenarios, reviewed or prepared national and local management and restoration strategies, applied management measures at selected pilot sites and delivered an extensive capacity-building programme. The project treated mangrove conservation and restoration as both adaptation and mitigation measures. It ended in 2014 and did not establish a regional carbon market, certify a carbon-accounting methodology or report verified project-level removals.
source: International Climate Initiative (IKI) / International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
status_note: Implemented from December 2009 to June 2014; officially listed as completed.

document_title: Blue Carbon Ecosystems in South Africa — A First Comprehensive Assessment
notes: The national assessment describes South Africa's mangroves, salt marshes and seagrasses as blue-carbon ecosystems and evaluates their relevance to ocean carbon cycling, climate adaptation and coastal resilience. It provides examples and recommendations for estuaries that could be prioritised for restoration, creating a policy and planning evidence base across multiple ecosystem types. The report does not itself establish a restoration programme, set a binding target, approve a carbon-accounting methodology or quantify verified additional removals. It should therefore be treated as an assessment and prioritisation document rather than deployment authorisation.
source: International Climate Initiative (IKI) / South African Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment
status_note: Published in March 2024 as a completed national assessment.

document_title: Blue Carbon Pilot Project South Africa
notes: The report describes a participatory pilot approach intended to combine restoration of marine ecosystems with nature-positive recovery measures in South Africa. The pilot focuses on renaturation of naturally occurring salt marshes and on involving local stakeholders in the design and implementation of local measures. It represents practical restoration planning and early pilot support rather than a national legal instrument. The publication does not provide a verified carbon-removal total, create a carbon-credit methodology or show that the pilot constituted a permanently authorised commercial removal project.
source: International Climate Initiative (IKI) / South African Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment
status_note: Published in March 2023; the report documents a pilot approach rather than a continuing legal instrument.

document_title: Blue Carbon and Fishery Potential in Kwale and Lamu Counties, Kenya
notes: The study assesses mangrove and seagrass ecosystems in Kwale and Lamu Counties, which together contain a large share of Kenya's mangrove and seagrass habitats. It links ecosystem condition, fisheries and blue-carbon potential and is intended to improve the evidence available for conservation, sustainable development and possible future participation in blue-carbon markets. The study does not itself register a project, establish national accounting rules, issue credits or demonstrate verified additional removals. Any trading activity would require separate project design, safeguards, methodology approval, validation and monitoring.
source: International Climate Initiative (IKI) / Kenya Marine and Fisheries Research Institute and project partners
status_note: Published in December 2024 as a completed subnational study.

document_title: Climate Resilient Seaweed Blue Economy in Madagascar (SeaBlue)
notes: The GEF medium-size project concept proposes a climate-resilient seaweed blue-economy programme in Madagascar, implemented through the United Nations Industrial Development Organization. The GEF database records a proposed project grant of USD 4,476,210 and co-financing of USD 10,350,000. The concept is relevant to macroalgae-based coastal livelihoods and mitigation-oriented seaweed development, but concept approval is not evidence that implementation, cultivation expansion or carbon-removal monitoring has begun. The record does not establish a seaweed carbon-credit methodology, quantify durable sequestration or authorise biomass sinking or burial.
source: Global Environment Facility (GEF) / United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO)
status_note: GEF concept approved in 2026; implementation and final project arrangements remain pending.

document_title: BRICS — Biology's Role in Ocean Carbon Storage: A Gap Analysis
notes: The NERC-funded BRICS project reviewed major knowledge gaps affecting predictions of biologically mediated ocean carbon storage. It examined changes in seawater buffering associated with calcifying phytoplankton, variability in net primary production and the efficiency with which organic matter is transferred and respired in the ocean interior. Literature review, model comparison, expert assessment and community prioritisation were used to identify observations and model improvements needed for future research programmes. The award supported science and research coordination only; it did not test an engineered removal pathway, authorise deployment or produce carbon credits.
source: UK Research and Innovation — Natural Environment Research Council / National Oceanography Centre
status_note: Funded from June 2022 to June 2023; the project has been reported as completed.

document_title: VALUATION — Valuing Blue Carbon in Scotland's Marine Protected Area Network
notes: The six-month NERC award supported research on the value and climate relevance of blue carbon within Scotland's Marine Protected Area network. Its policy relevance lies in improving the evidence available for marine natural-capital valuation, spatial management and consideration of carbon stores in protected-area decisions. The award was a research project rather than an adopted Scottish valuation standard. It did not create a statutory accounting method, change protected-area rules, authorise restoration or generate tradable carbon credits.
source: UK Research and Innovation — Natural Environment Research Council / University of St Andrews
status_note: Funded from December 2017 to May 2018; the research award has ended.

document_title: Climate Support Programme — Phase III
notes: The programme supported South Africa's national climate-policy development and implementation, including governance, mitigation, adaptation and measurement, reporting and verification. Among its completed outputs, it launched a dedicated activity to identify marine and coastal carbon sinks, creating an institutional and research basis for subsequent national blue-carbon assessments and pilot work. The programme was broader than blue carbon and did not itself establish a blue-carbon crediting standard, approve a restoration project or quantify verified marine removals. Its ONCE relevance is therefore limited to the formally supported blue-carbon identification and policy-capacity component.
source: International Climate Initiative (IKI) / Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) / South African DFFE
status_note: Implemented from February 2017 to March 2022; officially listed as completed.

document_title: GLOBESINK — Global Ocean Sinking Carbon Flux and Variability
notes: The NERC-funded project applied statistical methods to tens of millions of particle measurements from a global fleet of biogeochemical Argo floats to increase the number of usable sinking-particle flux estimates by roughly an order of magnitude. It produced a global evidence base on the magnitude and variability of sinking carbon and on drivers such as particle size, fragmentation, temperature and oxygen, with the aim of improving representations of the biological carbon pump in climate models. The project measured and modelled natural carbon transport; it did not deploy a removal technology or establish a crediting or MRV standard for commercial projects.
source: UK Research and Innovation — Natural Environment Research Council / National Oceanography Centre
