notes: Decree No. 2025-851 of 27 August 2025 establishes the current French procedural framework for mining titles and underground-storage titles and expressly applies to activities both on land and at sea, including the maritime public domain, territorial waters, the seabed of the exclusive economic zone and the soil and subsoil of the continental shelf. The decree defines the principal title types as exclusive exploration permits and concessions and sets common rules for applications, applicant and titleholder obligations, selection, environmental and socio-economic review, renewals, extensions, surrender, withdrawal and other title-management procedures. It is directly incorporated into France's geological carbon dioxide storage regime: the Environment Code now provides that applications, examination and grant of an exclusive permit to explore formations suitable for geological CO2 storage follow the corresponding underground-storage exploration-title procedures under this decree, and that relevant parts of the decree apply to CO2-storage concessions. The decree requires competent authorities to consider technical and financial capacity, planned work, protected environmental interests and the environmental memorandum in title decisions. For underground-storage concessions it requires the granting decision to identify the applicable geological formations, maximum storage capacity, the substance to be stored and the protection perimeter. This is therefore a binding permitting and safeguard framework relevant to marine geological CO2 storage, but it is not itself an exploration permit, a storage concession or an injection authorization. It does not identify a specific offshore reservoir, prove injectivity or containment, quantify actual carbon dioxide removal, or create an MRV-based carbon-crediting mechanism. Those project-level facts and operating conditions must be established through subsequent title, environmental and operational approvals.
source: French Republic — Légifrance / Ministry responsible for ecological transition and mining
status_note: Published on 28 August 2025 and in force from 29 August 2025 as the procedural regulation for mining and underground-storage titles, including titles used by the geological CO2-storage regime.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Resource Management and Administration) Amendment (Release of Documentary Information) Regulations 2025
notes: These amending regulations revise the Commonwealth offshore petroleum and greenhouse-gas storage information-release framework under the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006 and the Resource Management and Administration Regulations. They affect when documentary information and data associated with offshore greenhouse-gas titles can be made publicly available and therefore support regulatory transparency, data stewardship and later technical assessment of offshore storage activities. The instrument does not grant a greenhouse-gas assessment permit, holding lease, storage formation declaration or injection licence, and it does not authorize CO2 injection or demonstrate that a storage project has commenced.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: In force; registered in November 2025 under the Commonwealth offshore petroleum and greenhouse-gas storage framework.

document_title: Developing a Greenhouse Gas Resource — Greenhouse Gas Holding Lease Application Fact Sheet (31 March 2026)
notes: This NOPTA fact sheet explains the regulatory pathway and application expectations for a Commonwealth offshore greenhouse-gas holding lease after an assessment permit holder has identified a potentially viable storage resource but needs additional time to evaluate commercial or technical feasibility. It supports title administration, evidence submission and continued appraisal of an offshore storage opportunity. A holding lease preserves and regulates rights during the evaluation stage; it is not an injection licence and does not itself authorize routine CO2 injection, permanent storage operations or commercial deployment.
source: National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator (NOPTA)
status_note: Current NOPTA guidance updated for the Resource Management and Administration Regulations commencing on 31 March 2026.

document_title: Greenhouse Gas Search Authority, Special Authority and Research Consent Fact Sheet (31 March 2026)
notes: This NOPTA fact sheet describes Commonwealth offshore greenhouse-gas search authorities, special authorities and research consents, including the circumstances in which limited exploration, information-gathering or research activities may be authorized outside the ordinary title pathway. Its practical function is to clarify application, scope and administrative requirements for controlled investigation of offshore greenhouse-gas storage resources. These authorities are exploratory or research-oriented instruments and should not be treated as storage licences: they do not by themselves authorize commercial CO2 injection or permanent geological storage.
source: National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator (NOPTA)
status_note: Current NOPTA guidance updated in connection with the offshore resource-management reforms commencing on 31 March 2026.

document_title: Notification of Eligible Greenhouse Gas Storage Formation Fact Sheet (31 March 2026)
notes: This NOPTA fact sheet sets out the information and procedural expectations associated with notifying the regulator that a geological formation may qualify as an eligible greenhouse-gas storage formation under the Commonwealth offshore regime. The process requires technical characterization and supports regulatory review of storage-resource evidence, formation boundaries and suitability before later title or project decisions. Notification of an eligible formation is an evidentiary and regulatory step; it is not equivalent to a final declaration of a storage formation, an injection licence or authorization to commence CO2 storage operations.
source: National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator (NOPTA)
status_note: Current NOPTA guidance updated for the regulatory framework applying from 31 March 2026.

document_title: Key Greenhouse Gas Operations Fact Sheet (31 March 2026)
notes: This NOPTA fact sheet explains how key greenhouse-gas operations are treated within the Commonwealth offshore title and environmental-management framework and identifies regulatory interfaces that may require approval before specified operations proceed. It is relevant to the transition from resource appraisal toward operational activity because it clarifies which activities attract enhanced regulatory scrutiny and how title obligations interact with other offshore approvals. The document is administrative guidance rather than a project approval and does not independently authorize injection, storage, construction or a specific offshore CCS development.
source: National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator (NOPTA)
status_note: Current NOPTA guidance applying under the offshore regulatory framework updated on 31 March 2026.

document_title: Surrender of Offshore Greenhouse Gas Titles Fact Sheet (31 March 2026)
notes: This NOPTA fact sheet explains the process and regulatory expectations for surrendering Commonwealth offshore greenhouse-gas titles. It is relevant to the full lifecycle of marine geological CO2 storage because title surrender can depend on satisfaction of reporting, data, rehabilitation, closure or other outstanding obligations and therefore helps prevent regulatory responsibilities from ending automatically when a titleholder wishes to exit. The fact sheet does not establish a new storage project, authorize injection or certify permanent containment; it provides guidance on ending or relinquishing title rights under the existing legal framework.
source: National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator (NOPTA)
status_note: Current NOPTA lifecycle guidance updated in connection with the 31 March 2026 regulatory changes.

document_title: Transfers, Dealings, Change in Control and Other Titleholder Transactions Guideline (March 2026)
notes: This NOPTA guideline describes Commonwealth requirements and administrative expectations for transfers, dealings, changes in control and related transactions involving offshore titles, including greenhouse-gas storage titles. Its function is to preserve regulatory oversight when ownership, control or interests in an offshore storage title change and to clarify when approval, registration or supporting information is required. The guideline governs titleholder transactions rather than storage performance and does not create an injection right, approve a storage formation or authorize a particular CCS project.
source: National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator (NOPTA)
status_note: Current NOPTA guideline updated in March 2026.

document_title: Annual Title Assessment Report Fact Sheet (31 March 2026)
notes: This NOPTA fact sheet explains annual title assessment reporting for offshore titleholders and supports standardized submission of information used by the regulator to assess compliance, work-program progress and resource-development activity. For greenhouse-gas titles, the reporting framework contributes to continuing oversight and the accumulation of technical and administrative evidence across the assessment and storage lifecycle. It is a reporting and compliance guidance document, not a carbon-accounting methodology for tradable credits and not an approval for CO2 injection or permanent storage.
source: National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator (NOPTA)
status_note: Current NOPTA reporting guidance issued for the framework applying from 31 March 2026.

document_title: Notes on Completing Mandatory Templates for Annual Title Assessment Reports (31 March 2026)
notes: This NOPTA document provides completion instructions for mandatory annual title assessment report templates used within the Commonwealth offshore petroleum and greenhouse-gas regulatory system. It standardizes how titleholders structure and submit required information, improving consistency, traceability and regulatory assessment of greenhouse-gas title performance and activities. Although the underlying reporting obligations can be legally mandatory, these completion notes function as guidance for the prescribed templates. They do not establish a separate monitoring programme, issue carbon credits or authorize CO2 injection or storage.
source: National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator (NOPTA)
status_note: Current template-completion guidance associated with the reporting regime applying from 31 March 2026.

document_title: 二酸化炭素の貯留事業に関する法律施行規則（令和八年経済産業省令第五十号）
notes: This ministerial ordinance implements procedural and administrative provisions of Japan's Act on Carbon Dioxide Storage Businesses after the storage-business regime entered its operational phase in May 2026. It prescribes forms, applications, notifications and operator-facing requirements relevant to exploration and geological CO2 storage and therefore provides the detailed regulatory machinery needed to administer storage rights and compliance. The ordinance is a general implementing rule rather than an individual project decision: it does not by itself designate a specific offshore reservoir, approve a particular operator or authorize CO2 injection at a named site.
source: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) / e-Gov Japan
status_note: Promulgated in May 2026 and in force as part of the operational CCS Business Act regime.

document_title: 海域の貯留層における貯留事業に係る貯留事業実施計画等に関する省令（令和八年経済産業省・環境省令第七号）
notes: This joint METI-MOE ordinance establishes detailed requirements for implementation plans and related regulatory submissions specifically for CO2 storage businesses using reservoirs beneath marine areas. It operationalizes the marine-storage component of Japan's CCS Business Act framework by specifying information and conditions relevant to storage plans, environmental protection, monitoring and regulatory review. Because it is a generally applicable rule, it should not be read as an approval of any particular offshore CCS project; project-specific rights and approvals must still be obtained through the statutory authorization process.
source: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) and Ministry of the Environment (MOE) / e-Gov Japan
status_note: Promulgated and brought into force in May 2026 with the marine-storage provisions of the CCS Business Act framework.

document_title: 自然環境保全法施行規則の一部を改正する省令（令和八年環境省令第十七号）
notes: This Ministry of the Environment amendment coordinates Japan's nature-conservation rules with the new CCS Business Act regime for drilling and storage-related work affecting offshore seabed areas subject to nature-conservation controls. It introduces or adjusts permit criteria and environmental safeguards so that CCS-related seabed activity remains subject to ecological review rather than being treated solely as an industrial authorization question. The amendment is restrictive and procedural in character: it does not authorize a named storage site or establish that offshore injection has begun.
source: Ministry of the Environment, Japan
status_note: Promulgated and effective on 22 May 2026 as part of the legal transition to the CCS Business Act regime.

document_title: 二酸化炭素の貯留事業に関する法律の施行に伴う関係政令の整備及び経過措置に関する政令（令和八年政令第百五十二号）
notes: This Cabinet Order provides consequential amendments and transitional arrangements required when the storage-business provisions of Japan's CCS Business Act came into force. It aligns existing environmental and administrative rules with the new statutory authorization system, including provisions relevant to marine CO2 storage, regulatory jurisdiction and technical conditions such as the treatment of injected CO2 streams. Its function is legal integration and transition, not project deployment: it neither awards a specific offshore storage right nor independently permits injection at a particular reservoir.
source: Cabinet of Japan / Ministry of the Environment
status_note: Cabinet Order No. 152 of 2026; effective with the relevant CCS Business Act provisions from 22 May 2026.

document_title: 特定二酸化炭素ガスに含まれる二酸化炭素の濃度の測定の方法を定める省令及び特定二酸化炭素ガスの海底下廃棄の許可等に関する省令を廃止する省令（令和八年環境省令第十六号）
notes: This Ministry of the Environment ordinance repeals legacy subordinate rules governing measurement of CO2 concentration and permitting for sub-seabed disposal of specified carbon dioxide as Japan transitions to the newer CCS Business Act framework. The repeal is therefore part of a regulatory handover rather than a withdrawal of government oversight over marine geological CO2 storage. The instrument does not legalize unrestricted seabed injection and does not itself approve a project; marine storage remains governed by the replacement statutory and implementing regime.
source: Ministry of the Environment, Japan
status_note: Promulgated in May 2026 and effective from 22 May 2026 as a transition from the former marine-pollution permitting rules to the CCS Business Act framework.

document_title: 特定二酸化炭素ガスの海底下廃棄の許可の申請に関し必要な事項を定める件及び海洋汚染等及び海上災害の防止に関する法律第十八条の十五第一項の規定に基づく指定海域の公示を廃止する告示
notes: This Ministry of the Environment notice repeals earlier notices that specified application requirements and designated-area arrangements for permits covering sub-seabed disposal of specified carbon dioxide under the former marine-pollution-control framework. The repeal accompanies the May 2026 transition to regulation of marine geological storage under the CCS Business Act and related implementing instruments. It is a legal housekeeping and transition measure, not a relaxation of environmental safeguards, and it does not authorize injection or storage at any specific marine site.
source: Ministry of the Environment, Japan
status_note: Effective from 22 May 2026 as part of the transition to the replacement CCS Business Act regulatory framework.

document_title: 特定二酸化炭素ガスの海底下廃棄の許可の申請（令和8年2月17日付）に係る公告及び縦覧
notes: This Ministry of the Environment public notice opened inspection and public-comment procedures for a February 2026 application concerning a permit for sub-seabed disposal of specified CO2 under the pre-transition marine-pollution regime. The notice provides formal project-stage scrutiny and makes the application materials available for review, but it is not the final permit decision. The official materials indicated no planned injection during the requested 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031 period for the formations described, so the record must not be interpreted as evidence of newly authorized or operating CO2 injection.
source: Ministry of the Environment, Japan
status_note: Public inspection and comment process conducted in February–March 2026; the notice itself was not a final storage authorization.

document_title: 이산화탄소 포집ㆍ수송ㆍ저장 및 활용에 관한 법률 [Act No. 20203]
notes: The Act establishes the Republic of Korea's integrated legal framework for carbon capture, transport, storage and utilization and expressly defines geological storage to include injection into subsurface formations on land or beneath marine areas. It creates planning, approval, site-selection, operational, monitoring, closure and administrative structures for CCS and provides continuity rules for relevant pre-existing marine storage permissions. The law enables regulated deployment but does not itself approve a particular offshore storage reservoir or guarantee that a project has reached injection; project-specific approvals and technical conditions remain necessary.
source: Government of the Republic of Korea / Korean Law Information Center
status_note: Enacted on 6 February 2024 and in force from 7 February 2025.

document_title: 이산화탄소 포집ㆍ수송ㆍ저장 및 활용에 관한 법률 시행령 [대통령령 제35243호]
notes: This Presidential Decree supplies implementing detail for the Republic of Korea's integrated CCS Act, including administrative procedures, technical and institutional requirements, and matters delegated by the statute for capture, transport and geological storage. It supports practical licensing and oversight of storage activities that may occur beneath marine areas and clarifies the regulatory treatment of transport and storage infrastructure. The decree is a framework-level implementing instrument and does not itself select an offshore storage formation or confer an injection licence on a named project.
source: Government of the Republic of Korea / Korean Law Information Center
status_note: In force from 7 February 2025; forms part of the active implementing framework for the CCS Act.

document_title: 이산화탄소 포집ㆍ수송ㆍ저장 및 활용에 관한 법률 시행규칙 [산업통상자원부령 제597호]
notes: This ministerial enforcement rule provides detailed forms, procedural requirements and administrative standards for implementing the Republic of Korea's CCS Act and its Enforcement Decree. It translates the statutory storage-authorization and compliance framework into operator-facing submissions and regulatory processes relevant to geological storage, including storage that may take place below marine areas. The rule is binding subordinate legislation, but it is not an individual offshore storage permit and does not establish that any particular project is authorized to inject CO2.
source: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy / Korean Law Information Center
status_note: In force from 7 February 2025 as part of the CCS Act implementing package.

subnational_area: Peninsular Malaysia and Federal Territory of Labuan
document_title: Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage Act 2025 [Act 870]
notes: Malaysia's federal CCUS Act establishes a statutory framework for carbon capture, transportation, utilization and geological storage and assigns regulatory functions to the national CCUS authority. The framework is materially relevant to offshore storage because commenced provisions support licensing and regulatory control of offshore assessment and storage activities in the federal jurisdiction, including the Labuan area. The Act creates the legal architecture rather than approving a specific injection project. At commencement, the onshore-storage Part was not brought into force, so the active scope should not be overstated as a uniform nationwide onshore and offshore regime.
source: Government of Malaysia / Malaysia Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage Agency (MyCCUS)
status_note: Gazetted on 1 August 2025 and brought into force on 1 October 2025 for the commenced provisions; the onshore-storage Part was not commenced at that time.

subnational_area: Peninsular Malaysia and Federal Territory of Labuan
document_title: Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (Offshore Permit and Licensing) Regulations 2025 [P.U. (A) 346]
notes: These 2025 regulations operationalize the offshore permitting and licensing provisions of Malaysia's federal CCUS framework. They establish a staged system in which an offshore geological assessment permit precedes any storage licence and set application, technical, safety, monitoring, operational, closure and post-closure requirements for permanent geological storage beneath offshore areas. The regulations are enabling but conditional: an assessment permit is not a storage licence, and neither the existence of the regulations nor completion of assessment establishes that CO2 injection is authorized at a particular site.
source: Federal Government Gazette of Malaysia (gazette copy hosted by ZUL RAFIQUE & partners)
status_note: Gazetted on 30 September 2025 and in force from 1 October 2025.

document_title: Offshore Assessment Permit for the Duyong CCS Area
notes: MyCCUS granted PETRONAS CCS Ventures an offshore assessment permit for the Duyong area in October 2025, described by PETRONAS as the first permit issued under Malaysia's new federal CCUS framework. The permit gives the holder regulated rights to undertake geological and technical assessment of the offshore storage area and is therefore an independent project-level administrative decision rather than another copy of the enabling legislation. Its scope is assessment: it does not by itself constitute the later offshore storage licence required for permanent injection and should not be counted as evidence that commercial CO2 storage has begun.
source: Malaysia Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage Agency (MyCCUS) / PETRONAS
status_note: Offshore assessment permit granted on 10 October 2025; assessment authorization only, not a storage or injection licence.

document_title: Land (Carbon Storage) Rules, 2022 [Swk. L.N. 349/2022]
notes: Sarawak's Land (Carbon Storage) Rules create a detailed licensing and operational framework for geological CO2 storage and expressly extend relevant concepts to offshore land comprising seabed and subsoil within the applicable continental-shelf jurisdiction. The Rules address storage-site rights, applications, development plans, operating duties, monitoring and reporting, closure and post-closure responsibilities, financial obligations and the treatment of carbon-credit plans. They provide a binding regulatory pathway but do not themselves approve a named offshore storage project or quantify achieved carbon removals; project-specific licences and permits remain necessary.
source: Government of Sarawak — Sarawak LawNet
status_note: Published in December 2022 and in force from 1 January 2023.

document_title: Natural Resources and Environment (Control of Conveyance of Scheduled Gases) Rules, 2024 [Swk. L.N. 265/2024]
notes: These Sarawak rules establish controls over the conveyance of scheduled gases, including CO2 moved by vessel or pipeline for storage, and cover activities connected with Sarawak waters and the continental-shelf setting. They provide for permits, operational conditions, incident or leakage reporting, financial security and regulatory supervision, making them directly relevant to the transport-to-storage chain for offshore CCS. The text provides that commencement occurs on a date appointed by the responsible Minister; no separate commencement notification was identified in the official LawNet materials reviewed, so the Rules are recorded as adopted but not yet confirmed in force rather than assumed to be active.
source: Government of Sarawak — State Attorney-General's Chambers
status_note: Gazetted in July 2024; commencement depends on a separate ministerial Gazette appointment, which was not identified in the official materials reviewed.

document_title: Environment (Reduction of Greenhouse Gases Emission) Ordinance, 2023 [Cap. 85]
notes: This Sarawak Ordinance establishes a broader greenhouse-gas governance and carbon-market framework and links permanent CO2 storage carried out under the state's carbon-storage rules to the treatment of carbon credits and regulated climate actions. Its territorial and legal setting includes Sarawak waters and continental-shelf activities, making the Ordinance relevant to offshore geological storage even though it is not limited to marine CCS. The law creates accounting, crediting and governance structures rather than a site-specific storage approval. It entered into force in March 2024 except for Part IV, so implementation is active but not every Part commenced simultaneously.
source: Government of Sarawak — Sarawak LawNet
status_note: In force from 1 March 2024 except for Part IV.

document_title: Peraturan Menteri ESDM Nomor 2 Tahun 2023 tentang Penyelenggaraan Penangkapan dan Penyimpanan Karbon, serta Penangkapan, Pemanfaatan, dan Penyimpanan Karbon pada Kegiatan Usaha Hulu Minyak dan Gas Bumi
notes: This Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources regulation establishes a CCS and CCUS framework within Indonesia's upstream oil and gas sector, including requirements for identifying injection targets, technical evaluation, safe and permanent geological storage, monitoring and regulatory approval. Because Indonesia's upstream petroleum operations include extensive offshore fields and subsurface formations, the rule is directly relevant to marine geological CO2 storage where such activities are undertaken under offshore upstream rights. It is a sector-wide regulation, not an authorization for a particular offshore injection project, and project-specific plans and approvals remain necessary.
source: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Established and in force from 3 March 2023.

document_title: Peraturan Presiden Nomor 14 Tahun 2024 tentang Penyelenggaraan Kegiatan Penangkapan dan Penyimpanan Karbon
notes: This Presidential Regulation creates a national framework for carbon capture and geological storage beyond the earlier upstream-oil-and-gas-only route. It provides for Carbon Storage Permit Areas and a staged authorization structure covering exploration and storage operations, together with monitoring, safety, administrative and cross-border elements relevant to the development of Indonesian storage hubs, including offshore geological formations where the designated area and permits apply. The regulation enables regulated CCS development but does not itself award a specific marine storage site, authorize injection at a named reservoir or demonstrate operational carbon removal.
source: President of the Republic of Indonesia / Audit Board Regulations Database
status_note: Promulgated and in force from 30 January 2024.

document_title: Peraturan Menteri ESDM Nomor 16 Tahun 2024 tentang Penyelenggaraan Kegiatan Penyimpanan Karbon pada Wilayah Izin Penyimpanan Karbon dalam Rangka Kegiatan Penangkapan dan Penyimpanan Karbon
notes: This Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources regulation implements the Carbon Storage Permit Area pathway created under Indonesia's national CCS framework. It governs preparation, designation and offering of storage-permit areas and requires technical, economic, efficiency and risk considerations that build the evidence base for later exploration and storage authorizations. The rule can apply to offshore geological storage areas within Indonesian jurisdiction, but it is a general area-designation and licensing instrument rather than a permit for a named offshore project; no injection or achieved storage volume follows merely from its adoption.
source: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Promulgated and in force from 24 December 2024.

document_title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 on Establishing a Framework of Measures for Strengthening Europe's Net-Zero Technology Manufacturing Ecosystem (Net-Zero Industry Act)
notes: The Net-Zero Industry Act establishes a Union-level objective of at least 50 million tonnes of annual CO2 injection capacity by 2030 in geological storage sites located within the Union's territory, exclusive economic zones or continental shelves. It also creates transparency, planning and producer-contribution mechanisms intended to accelerate development of storage capacity, making the Regulation directly relevant to offshore geological CO2 storage. The target concerns available injection capacity and supporting infrastructure; it is not a site-specific storage permit and does not mean that 50 million tonnes of CO2 have already been injected, stored or removed from the atmosphere.
source: European Union / EUR-Lex
status_note: Binding EU Regulation in force; the statutory CO2 injection-capacity objective applies toward 2030.

document_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1477 Supplementing Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 as Regards Identification of Obligated Oil and Gas Producers and Calculation of Their Contributions to the Union CO2 Injection Capacity Objective
notes: This Delegated Regulation operationalizes the Net-Zero Industry Act's 2030 CO2 injection-capacity objective by identifying the basis for determining which Union oil and gas producers are subject to contribution obligations and how their pro-rata shares are calculated. The measure creates a binding allocation and reporting methodology that supports development of geological storage capacity, including sites in Union exclusive economic zones and continental shelves. It does not itself license a particular offshore reservoir or authorize injection; obligated entities must contribute toward capacity while storage projects remain subject to the separate CCS permitting and environmental framework.
source: European Commission / EUR-Lex
status_note: Binding delegated legislation implementing the producer-contribution mechanism for the 2030 Union CO2 injection-capacity objective.

document_title: Commission Decision (EU) 2025/1479 Specifying Pro-Rata Contributions of Obligated Entities to the Union CO2 Injection Capacity Objective
notes: This Commission Decision assigns entity-specific pro-rata contributions toward the Union's 2030 CO2 injection-capacity objective under the Net-Zero Industry Act, converting the general producer obligation into quantified responsibilities for identified companies. Because eligible storage capacity may be developed in Union exclusive economic zones and continental shelves, the Decision is materially relevant to offshore CCS infrastructure and market formation. The assigned contribution is an obligation to support or provide injection capacity, not a permit for an individual storage site and not evidence that the stated capacity has already been constructed or used for CO2 injection.
source: European Commission / EUR-Lex
status_note: Binding Commission Decision applicable from July 2025 and implementing quantified producer contributions toward the 2030 capacity objective.

document_title: Lei nº 14.993, de 8 de outubro de 2024
notes: Law No. 14,993/2024 establishes Brazil's federal legal basis for carbon capture, transport and geological storage and assigns the National Agency of Petroleum, Natural Gas and Biofuels regulatory responsibilities for storage authorization and oversight. The framework includes long-duration storage authorizations, monitoring, contingency and leakage-accounting obligations and is materially relevant to Brazil's significant offshore geological storage potential recognized by the regulator. The statute is not limited to marine storage and does not itself approve an offshore site; a project still requires the applicable authorization, technical assessment and environmental approvals before injection.
source: Presidency of the Republic of Brazil / National Agency of Petroleum, Natural Gas and Biofuels (ANP)
status_note: Federal law enacted on 8 October 2024; CCS provisions form the legal basis for subsequent ANP regulation and authorization.

document_title: Public Consultation on the Proposed Decree Regulating CCS, CCUS and BECCS Activities
notes: This Ministry of Mines and Energy consultation sought public input on a proposed decree to implement Brazil's statutory framework for CCS, CCUS and BECCS. The draft addressed a two-stage structure for research and evaluation followed by storage-operation authorization, together with regulatory, technical and environmental requirements that would also shape future offshore geological CO2 storage. The consultation is evidence of active rulemaking, not an enacted storage decree or project permit. Its inclusion therefore records the formal policy-development process without treating draft provisions as currently binding authorization for offshore injection.
source: Ministry of Mines and Energy, Brazil
status_note: Formal public consultation conducted from 17 November to 16 December 2025; the consulted text was a proposed decree rather than a final storage authorization.

document_title: Relatório sobre a Implementação do Marco Regulatório de CCUS no País — Updated after Law No. 14,993/2024
notes: This ANP regulatory report was updated after enactment of Law No. 14,993/2024 to assess and organize the implementation of Brazil's new CCUS legal framework. It supports rulemaking by examining regulatory responsibilities, authorization architecture and technical issues for geological CO2 storage and is relevant to offshore deployment because ANP has identified substantial Brazilian offshore storage potential. The report is an official assessment and policy-development input rather than binding secondary legislation, a carbon-credit methodology or a project permit; it does not authorize injection or quantify verified removals.
source: National Agency of Petroleum, Natural Gas and Biofuels (ANP), Brazil
status_note: Updated regulatory implementation report approved by ANP in December 2024 and published as an active reference for development of the CCUS framework.

document_title: Nota Técnica nº 3/2024/STM-AUT/STM/ANP-RJ — Enquadramento de Projetos de PD&I Relacionados ao Armazenamento Geológico de CO2
notes: This ANP technical note establishes an administrative approach for classifying and handling research, development and innovation projects related to geological CO2 storage within the agency's regulatory and R&D framework. It helps distinguish research activities, data acquisition and technical work that support storage-resource characterization and future regulatory decisions, including work relevant to Brazil's offshore geological storage potential. The note is primarily an evidence-building and R&D governance instrument: it does not grant a commercial storage authorization, approve a named offshore reservoir or demonstrate that permanent CO2 injection has commenced.
source: National Agency of Petroleum, Natural Gas and Biofuels (ANP), Brazil
status_note: ANP Technical Note No. 3/2024; publicly released following agency approval in 2025 and used as an active technical-administrative reference.

document_title: RMA Regulations 2025 — Transitional Arrangements FAQs
notes: This NOPTA FAQ explains transitional arrangements associated with commencement of the remade Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Resource Management and Administration) Regulations 2025. It assists offshore petroleum and greenhouse-gas titleholders in determining how existing applications, reporting obligations, forms, data requirements and regulatory processes move from the former 2011 regulations to the 2025 framework. Because greenhouse-gas storage titles are expressly within the regulatory system, the FAQ is relevant to marine geological CO2 storage governance. It is transitional guidance rather than a new title or injection approval and does not itself authorize any offshore storage operation.
source: National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator (NOPTA)
status_note: Current transitional guidance associated with the RMA Regulations 2025 commencing on 31 March 2026.

document_title: Expiry of Offshore Greenhouse Gas Titles Fact Sheet
notes: This NOPTA fact sheet explains how Commonwealth offshore greenhouse-gas titles reach expiry and the legal and administrative consequences when a title ceases to be in force. It is relevant to lifecycle governance of offshore geological CO2 storage because expiry can interact with outstanding compliance, data, reporting and other statutory responsibilities and must be distinguished from voluntary surrender or regulatory cancellation. The document does not create or extend storage rights and does not authorize injection; it provides guidance on the ending of an existing offshore greenhouse-gas title under the Commonwealth statutory framework.
source: National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator (NOPTA)
status_note: Current NOPTA guidance listed with the greenhouse-gas title lifecycle materials in 2026.

document_title: Cancellation of Offshore Greenhouse Gas Titles Fact Sheet
notes: This NOPTA fact sheet explains the Commonwealth process and grounds for cancellation of offshore greenhouse-gas titles where statutory or title conditions are not satisfied. It forms part of the enforcement and lifecycle safeguards for marine geological CO2 storage by clarifying that title rights may be terminated through regulatory action rather than only by expiry or voluntary surrender. The fact sheet is compliance guidance, not a cancellation decision for a named project and not an authorization for storage activity; it therefore records the regulatory safeguard without implying that any particular offshore CCS title has been cancelled.
source: National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator (NOPTA)
status_note: Current NOPTA greenhouse-gas title compliance guidance listed in 2026.

document_title: Ley 40/2010, de 29 de diciembre, de almacenamiento geológico de dióxido de carbono
notes: This law establishes Spain's binding legal framework for environmentally safe geological CO2 storage and expressly applies to underground structures in Spain, including the territorial sea, exclusive economic zone and continental shelf. It requires research permits for exploration and storage concessions before a storage site can be used, and it regulates site characterization, operation, monitoring, closure, corrective measures and long-term responsibility. It also prohibits storage in the water column and requires marine-subsoil storage to comply with national, European Union and international marine-environment rules. The law creates the permitting architecture for offshore geological storage but does not itself authorize injection at a named project.
source: Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE) / Jefatura del Estado
status_note: In force since 31 December 2010.

document_title: Förordning (2014:21) om geologisk lagring av koldioxid
notes: This regulation provides Sweden's detailed rules for geological CO2 storage and applies within Sweden, on the continental shelf and in the exclusive economic zone. It limits large-scale storage to specified offshore areas, prohibits storage in the water column, and sets requirements for site characterization, permit conditions, financial security, monitoring, corrective measures, closure and post-closure responsibility. The instrument therefore allows geological storage only within a tightly controlled regulatory framework and does not constitute approval of a specific offshore storage project.
source: Sveriges riksdag / Government of Sweden
status_note: Current regulation, including later amendments.

document_title: Förordning (2026:691) om ändring i förordningen (2014:21) om geologisk lagring av koldioxid
notes: This 2026 amendment updates Sweden's binding geological CO2 storage regulation. Among other changes, it updates the legal basis and provisions concerning financial security so that security remains available for obligations associated with a storage permit and can be drawn upon when regulatory conditions require it, including situations connected with permit revocation. The amendment strengthens the financial and compliance safeguards surrounding geological storage; it does not issue a storage permit or authorize injection at a named offshore site.
source: Government of Sweden / Svensk författningssamling
status_note: Entered into force on 1 July 2026.

document_title: S.I. No. 575/2011 — European Communities (Geological Storage of Carbon Dioxide) Regulations 2011
notes: These regulations transpose the European Union geological CO2 storage framework into Irish law while adopting a restrictive national position. They apply to the State, including relevant maritime jurisdiction, and provide that geological storage of CO2 is not permitted in the areas covered by the regulations; storage in the water column is also prohibited. The instrument therefore functions primarily as a binding prohibition and environmental safeguard rather than as an authorization system for an Irish offshore storage project.
source: Irish Statute Book / Government of Ireland
status_note: Binding national regulations in force.

document_title: S.I. No. 279/2014 — European Communities (Geological Storage of Carbon Dioxide) (Amendment) Regulations 2014
notes: These amendment regulations modify Ireland's 2011 geological CO2 storage regulations as part of continued implementation of the European Union CCS framework. They operate within the same restrictive national regime and do not create a general right to develop geological storage in Irish maritime areas. The amendment is a technical legal update to the regulatory framework and is not an exploration permit, storage permit or deployment decision for a particular offshore project.
source: Irish Statute Book / Government of Ireland
status_note: Binding amendment to the 2011 regulations.

document_title: Ustawa z dnia 16 czerwca 2023 r. o zmianie ustawy — Prawo geologiczne i górnicze oraz niektórych innych ustaw
notes: This amending act modernizes Poland's Geological and Mining Law and related statutes, including provisions relevant to geological CO2 storage, concessions, competent authorities and administrative procedures. For marine ONCE purposes it forms part of the legal architecture under which storage areas and projects can be regulated in Polish maritime jurisdiction, including the Baltic Sea. The act establishes and updates regulatory powers and obligations but does not itself designate a specific offshore storage complex or issue an injection permit.
source: Government Legislation Centre / ELI Poland
status_note: Main provisions entered into force in 2023, with specified provisions taking effect later.

document_title: Rozporządzenie Ministra Środowiska z dnia 3 września 2014 r. w sprawie obszarów, na których dopuszcza się lokalizowanie kompleksu podziemnego składowania dwutlenku węgla
notes: This regulation establishes the spatial instrument used to identify areas in which underground CO2 storage complexes may be located in Poland. It is the parent regulation later amended to reflect additional eligible storage areas, including a Baltic exclusive economic zone area in the 2026 amendment. The regulation narrows where storage may be considered and supports site-screening and permitting, but designation under this instrument is not equivalent to a project storage permit or authorization to inject CO2.
source: Government Legislation Centre / ELI Poland
status_note: Binding parent regulation, as amended.

document_title: Rozporządzenie Ministra Klimatu i Środowiska z dnia 8 czerwca 2026 r. zmieniające rozporządzenie w sprawie obszarów, na których dopuszcza się lokalizowanie kompleksu podziemnego składowania dwutlenku węgla
notes: This 2026 amendment updates Poland's legally designated areas for potential underground CO2 storage complexes and adds or revises an area in the Baltic Sea exclusive economic zone. The amendment identifies geological zones in which storage development may be considered and therefore materially expands the offshore regulatory opportunity set. It is a spatial eligibility rule, not a concession or injection permit for a named storage operator, and any project remains subject to the separate Polish licensing and environmental requirements.
source: Government Legislation Centre / ELI Poland
status_note: Entered into force on 13 June 2026.

document_title: Lietuvos Respublikos anglies dioksido geologinio saugojimo įstatymas
notes: This law establishes Lithuania's national framework for geological CO2 storage and implements the core permitting, environmental-safety and operator-responsibility requirements of the European Union CCS regime. Its scope extends to Lithuanian jurisdiction including maritime areas such as the exclusive economic zone and continental shelf, and it provides for exploration and storage authorization, site assessment, monitoring, closure and liability arrangements. The law creates a conditional regulatory pathway but does not itself authorize a named offshore storage site.
source: Seimas of the Republic of Lithuania
status_note: Current consolidated law.

document_title: Grozījumi likumā "Par zemes dzīlēm"
notes: This 2025 amendment creates a substantially more complete Latvian legal framework for geological CO2 storage. It establishes exploration and storage licensing, financial security, monitoring and reporting, leakage response, closure and post-closure obligations, transfer of responsibility and third-party access rules. The framework can support geological storage development under Latvian jurisdiction, including offshore contexts where applicable, but the amendment does not itself select a storage site or authorize a particular injection project.
source: Saeima of the Republic of Latvia / Likumi.lv
status_note: Entered into force on 1 July 2025.

document_title: Ordonanță de urgență nr. 64 din 29 iunie 2011 privind stocarea geologică a dioxidului de carbon
notes: This emergency ordinance establishes Romania's binding framework for geological CO2 storage, including exploration, storage authorization, site characterization, monitoring, corrective measures, closure, financial security and transfer of responsibility. The framework is applicable to Romanian jurisdiction and, as subsequently clarified by legislation, extends to the Black Sea exclusive economic zone and continental shelf. It is the core regulatory instrument for geological storage but is not itself a permit for a named offshore storage project.
source: Government of Romania / Portal Legislativ
status_note: Binding CCS framework, as subsequently amended.

document_title: Legea nr. 114 din 24 aprilie 2013 pentru aprobarea Ordonanței de urgență a Guvernului nr. 64/2011 privind stocarea geologică a dioxidului de carbon
notes: This law approves and amends Romania's 2011 geological CO2 storage ordinance. It is especially relevant to marine storage because it clarifies the territorial scope of the framework to include Romania's Black Sea exclusive economic zone and continental shelf. The law therefore provides the statutory basis for regulating offshore geological storage under Romanian jurisdiction while retaining the separate requirements for site authorization, environmental safeguards and monitoring. It does not grant an offshore project permit by itself.
source: Parliament of Romania / Portal Legislativ
status_note: Binding approval and amendment law.

document_title: Ordonanță de urgență nr. 81 din 28 iunie 2024 privind înființarea Autorității Naționale de Reglementare în Domeniul Minier, Petrolier și al Stocării Geologice a Dioxidului de Carbon
notes: This 2024 emergency ordinance establishes and organizes the national regulator responsible for mining, petroleum and geological CO2 storage and updates related legislation. For offshore CCS, the institutional change matters because the authority administers regulatory functions that can apply to geological storage and associated activities in Romanian maritime jurisdiction, including the Black Sea continental shelf. The ordinance strengthens governance capacity and allocation of regulatory responsibility but does not authorize a storage complex or injection operation.
source: Government of Romania / Portal Legislativ
status_note: Binding institutional and regulatory reorganization in force.

document_title: Ordinul nr. 396 din 16 octombrie 2024 privind aprobarea procedurii pentru atestarea competenței tehnice în domeniul stocării geologice a dioxidului de carbon
notes: This order establishes a technical-competence certification procedure for persons and entities preparing documentation or performing work in the field of geological CO2 storage. It supports quality control in the Romanian CCS licensing system by requiring demonstrated technical capability for regulated tasks. The order is relevant to offshore storage because the same certified expertise can be required for work connected with storage under Romanian maritime jurisdiction. It is a technical qualification rule and does not authorize a specific storage site.
source: Romanian geological storage regulator / Portal Legislativ
status_note: Binding technical-competence procedure in force.

document_title: Ordinul nr. 172 din 12 mai 2026 privind tarifele aferente actelor emise în domeniul stocării geologice a dioxidului de carbon
notes: This 2026 order establishes or updates fees associated with regulatory acts, technical documentation, data use and competence-related services in Romania's geological CO2 storage regime. It operationalizes the administrative side of permitting and technical oversight, including activities that may support future Black Sea storage projects. The order does not define a new storage area and does not grant a concession or injection authorization; its function is to make the regulatory process administratively executable.
source: Romanian geological storage regulator / Portal Legislativ
status_note: Binding fee schedule issued in 2026.

document_title: Decreto Legislativo 14 settembre 2011, n. 162 — Attuazione della direttiva 2009/31/CE relativa allo stoccaggio geologico di biossido di carbonio
notes: This legislative decree transposes Directive 2009/31/EC and establishes Italy's national framework for environmentally safe geological CO2 storage. It governs site suitability, exploration and storage authorization, monitoring, corrective action, closure, financial security and transfer of responsibility, and it provides the legal basis for storage projects that may involve subsurface formations under Italian jurisdiction. The decree is a regulatory framework rather than an approval of a specific offshore project, and any marine deployment remains subject to applicable environmental and maritime controls.
source: Government of Italy / Normattiva
status_note: Binding national CCS framework, as amended.

document_title: Zakon o istraživanju i eksploataciji ugljikovodika
notes: This law regulates hydrocarbon exploration and exploitation together with permanent disposal of CO2 in geological structures. Its marine scope expressly includes the subsurface of internal marine waters, the territorial sea and the Croatian continental shelf in the Adriatic. It establishes the statutory basis for permits, rights, supervision and conditions governing geological storage and related subsurface activities. The law enables regulated offshore storage but does not itself grant a storage permit to a named operator.
source: Croatian Parliament / Narodne novine
status_note: Binding law in force, subject to later amendments.

document_title: Pravilnik o trajnom zbrinjavanju plinova u geološkim strukturama
notes: This regulation provided an earlier Croatian technical framework for permanent geological disposal of gases, including requirements relevant to geological CO2 storage. It addressed the technical and environmental conditions under which storage could be assessed and managed. The regulation is retained as a historical policy record because it formed part of the national CCS regulatory chain, but it was later replaced by the more specific 2018 CO2 storage regulation and should not be treated as the current operative standard.
source: Government of Croatia / Narodne novine
status_note: Repealed and replaced by the 2018 CO2-specific storage regulation.

document_title: Pravilnik o trajnom zbrinjavanju ugljikova dioksida u geološkim strukturama
notes: This regulation provides Croatia's detailed technical rules for permanent geological CO2 storage. It covers characterization and assessment of the storage complex, operational conditions, injected-stream requirements, monitoring, leakage and corrective measures, closure and post-closure obligations and supporting documentation. Because the parent law expressly covers Croatian marine waters and the Adriatic continental shelf, these technical rules are directly relevant to offshore geological storage. The regulation sets conditions for safe deployment but is not a permit for a specific storage site.
source: Government of Croatia / Narodne novine
status_note: Binding CO2-specific technical regulation in force.

document_title: Pravilnik o izmjenama i dopunama Pravilnika o trajnom zbrinjavanju ugljikova dioksida u geološkim strukturama
notes: This 2022 amendment updates Croatia's technical regulation for permanent geological CO2 storage. It modifies the operative requirements that apply to storage characterization, documentation, monitoring and regulatory compliance under the Croatian CCS framework. The amendment is relevant to offshore storage because the underlying legal regime extends to Croatian marine waters and the Adriatic continental shelf. It is a technical regulatory update and does not grant a storage permit to a named project.
source: Government of Croatia / Narodne novine
status_note: Binding amendment incorporated into the current technical framework.

document_title: Public consultation on draft law for carbon capture, use, transport and storage
notes: This Ministry of Environment and Energy consultation opened the draft national CCS law to public comment before enactment. The draft addressed capture, use, transport and geological storage, competent-authority functions, permits and environmental safeguards and was part of the policy process that led to the 2025 binding CCS law. The consultation itself did not authorize any storage project and its participation period has ended; it is retained as a distinct formal policy-development document rather than being treated as an active permit.
source: Hellenic Ministry of Environment and Energy
status_note: Public consultation concluded in November 2025 and was followed by enacted legislation.

document_title: Νόμος 5261/2025 — Ρυθμίσεις για τη δέσμευση, χρήση, μεταφορά και αποθήκευση διοξειδίου του άνθρακα
notes: This law establishes an integrated and updated Greek framework for CO2 capture, use, transport, liquefaction and environmentally safe geological storage. It defines the competent CCS authority and provides rules for exploration, storage permits, access, monitoring, corrective measures, closure, financial security and other operator obligations. The framework is the legal basis under which Greece can regulate offshore geological storage, including the Prinos project, but the law itself is not a permit for any individual storage complex. It has subsequently been amended in 2026.
source: Hellenic Parliament / Ministry of Environment and Energy
status_note: Published as Law 5261/2025 in Government Gazette 231/A/12.12.2025 and currently in force as amended.

document_title: Νόμος 5299/2026 — Amendments to Law 5261/2025 concerning marine-area use for CO2 exploration and storage
notes: This 2026 energy law makes substantive amendments to Greece's 2025 CCS framework. A key marine provision adds a mechanism allowing entities conducting CO2 exploration and storage activities, subject to environmental approval and statutory conditions, to obtain direct-use rights over the seashore, beach, water element, seabed and subsoil of the seabed for works required by those activities. The amendment materially improves the legal pathway for offshore CCS infrastructure while retaining environmental and licensing conditions. It does not itself grant a storage permit or seabed-use right to a named operator.
source: Hellenic Parliament
status_note: Published as Law 5299/2026 in Government Gazette 67/A/5.5.2026.

document_title: Storage permit issued for Prinos CO2
notes: This decision grants EnEarth Greece a 25-year storage permit for the Prinos CO2 storage site and storage complex within the offshore Prinos concession area near Kavala. HEREMA states that the geological formation is suitable for CO2 storage provided the procedures and permit conditions are fully observed. Injection may begin only after the regulator verifies fulfillment of the permit obligations, including final or updated safety, risk-management, monitoring, corrective-measures, closure and post-closure plans. This is therefore a genuine offshore project authorization, but it does not mean injection had already started on the permit-issuance date.
source: Hellenic Hydrocarbons and Energy Resources Management Company (HEREMA)
status_note: Storage permit issued on 26 February 2026; operations remain conditional on regulatory verification of permit obligations.

document_title: Decreto-Lei n.º 60/2012, de 14 de março
notes: This decree-law establishes Portugal's national legal regime for geological CO2 storage and applies across national jurisdiction including the territorial sea, contiguous zone, exclusive economic zone and continental shelf. It requires storage authorization and integrates site assessment, environmental impact assessment, financial guarantees, monitoring, corrective measures, closure and transfer-of-responsibility requirements. The instrument enables storage only under a formal regulatory process and does not authorize a specific offshore injection project.
source: Diário da República / Government of Portugal
status_note: Binding national CCS regime in force.

document_title: Decreto Legislativo Regional n.º 14/2024/A, de 24 de dezembro — Parque Marinho dos Açores
notes: This regional legislative decree establishes the Azores Marine Park and protection regimes for marine protected areas within the archipelago's maritime space. In specified protection classes, geological carbon storage is included among prohibited or excluded activities, creating a clear spatial constraint on marine geological CO2 storage. The instrument is therefore relevant as a marine environmental safeguard and prohibition, not as a CCS development policy. It does not prohibit every conceivable storage activity across all Portuguese maritime jurisdiction, only the areas and protection classes governed by the regional marine-park regime.
source: Legislative Assembly of the Autonomous Region of the Azores / Diário da República
status_note: Binding regional marine-protection regime, as subsequently amended.

document_title: Decreto Legislativo Regional n.º 20/2025/A, de 29 de julho — Regime regional de avaliação de impacte ambiental e licenciamento
notes: This Azores regional decree establishes an environmental impact assessment and licensing regime that expressly captures geological CO2 storage projects and related infrastructure within the categories subject to environmental review. It creates an additional regional safeguard for any qualifying storage, capture or transport proposal in the Azores by requiring environmental assessment before authorization. The decree does not establish a storage site, carbon credit mechanism or project permit; its role is procedural environmental control.
source: Legislative Assembly of the Autonomous Region of the Azores / Diário da República
status_note: Binding regional environmental assessment and licensing regime.

document_title: Decreto Legislativo Regional n.º 6/2026/A, de 3 de março — Alteração ao Parque Marinho dos Açores
notes: This 2026 regional legislative decree amends and republishes the Azores Marine Park regime. The updated framework continues to treat geological carbon storage as a prohibited activity in specified oceanic marine protected area classes, maintaining a direct spatial restriction on marine geological storage. The record is separate from the 2024 parent decree because it is a new formal legal version adopted in 2026. It is a conservation and regulatory safeguard rather than a storage authorization.
source: Legislative Assembly of the Autonomous Region of the Azores / Diário da República
status_note: Binding 2026 amendment and republication of the regional marine-protection regime.

document_title: Podnebni zakon (PoZ)
notes: The Slovenian Climate Act contains an explicit prohibition on injecting and geologically storing CO2 within the Republic of Slovenia, including its territorial waters. This creates a binding national barrier to domestic marine geological CO2 storage rather than a permitting pathway. The rule is directly relevant to ONCE because it regulates the marine geological storage pathway as prohibited activity; it does not prevent Slovenian entities from participating in lawful cross-border CCS arrangements outside the prohibited national area where other law permits them.
source: National Assembly of Slovenia / PISRS
status_note: Climate Act in force from August 2025.

document_title: Geological Storage of Carbon Dioxide Regulations, 2011 (L.N. 346 of 2011)
notes: These regulations establish Malta's legal framework for environmentally safe geological CO2 storage and expressly apply in Malta and on the continental shelf under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. They prohibit storage complexes extending beyond the regulated area and prohibit storage in the water column, while providing rules for storage permits, site characterization, monitoring, corrective measures, closure, financial security and transfer of responsibility. The regulations create a conditional offshore storage framework but do not grant a permit for a named storage site.
source: Government of Malta / Legislation Malta
status_note: Current subsidiary legislation 549.68, originally Legal Notice 346 of 2011 and subsequently amended.

document_title: Geological Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Amendment) Regulations, 2015 (L.N. 291 of 2015)
notes: This 2015 legal notice amends Malta's Geological Storage of Carbon Dioxide Regulations. It updates definitions and cross-references and adjusts environmental-liability and related provisions while leaving the underlying continental-shelf storage framework in place. The amendment forms part of the binding technical and legal safeguards for geological storage under Maltese jurisdiction. It does not authorize an offshore storage project or create a storage site by itself.
source: Government of Malta / Legislation Malta
status_note: Binding amendment incorporated into subsidiary legislation 549.68.

document_title: Laki hiilidioksidin talteenottamisesta ja varastoinnista 416/2012
notes: This Act implements core elements of the European Union CCS framework but adopts a prohibitive domestic storage policy. Geological CO2 storage is prohibited in Finnish territory and in Finland's exclusive economic zone, while captured CO2 may be transferred for permanent geological storage at a legally permitted site in another eligible European jurisdiction. The Act also governs capture, CO2-stream quality, transport networks, access and related oversight. For marine ONCE it is therefore primarily a prohibition on domestic and Finnish-EEZ storage combined with rules enabling regulated cross-border transport to permitted storage sites; it does not authorize a Finnish storage project.
source: Finlex / Ministry of Justice of Finland
status_note: Binding CCS Act in force, with later amendments.

document_title: Laki hiilidioksidin talteenottamisesta ja varastoinnista annetun lain 16 §:n muuttamisesta 127/2013
notes: This amendment modifies section 16 of Finland's 2012 Act on the capture and storage of carbon dioxide. It is part of the continuing legal maintenance of the national CCS framework, which prohibits geological storage in Finnish territory and the Finnish exclusive economic zone while regulating capture and transport to lawful storage elsewhere. The amendment does not create an exception allowing a domestic offshore storage project and does not issue any project authorization.
source: Finlex / Ministry of Justice of Finland
status_note: Amendment enacted and incorporated into the current CCS Act.

document_title: Laki hiilidioksidin talteenottamisesta ja varastoinnista annetun lain muuttamisesta 1426/2019
notes: This amendment updates multiple provisions of Finland's CCS Act, including rules connected with access to CO2 transport networks, regulatory decision-making and related administrative responsibilities. It modernizes how the national capture-and-transport framework is administered while leaving the core prohibition on geological storage in Finnish territory and the Finnish exclusive economic zone intact. The law supports regulated movement of captured CO2 toward lawful storage sites outside the prohibited Finnish storage area and does not authorize domestic marine storage.
source: Finlex / Ministry of Justice of Finland
status_note: Amendment enacted and incorporated into the current CCS Act.

document_title: Laki hiilidioksidin talteenottamisesta ja varastoinnista annetun lain 11 §:n muuttamisesta 807/2023
notes: This 2023 Act formally amends section 11 of Finland's carbon dioxide capture and storage law. It is a discrete legal update within the binding national CCS regime and therefore belongs in the policy chain separately from the 2012 parent Act. The amendment does not reverse Finland's prohibition on geological storage in Finnish territory and the exclusive economic zone and does not authorize any marine storage site; its function is maintenance of the regulatory framework.
source: Finlex / Ministry of Justice of Finland
status_note: Amendment enacted and incorporated into the current CCS Act.

document_title: Laki hiilidioksidin talteenottamisesta ja varastoinnista annetun lain 12 ja 16 §:n muuttamisesta 798/2025
notes: This 2025 Act formally amends sections 12 and 16 of Finland's carbon dioxide capture and storage law and represents the latest identified statutory maintenance of the CCS framework before the 2026 database cut-off. It updates the legal regime without creating a domestic geological storage right. Finland's core rule continues to prohibit geological storage in national territory and the exclusive economic zone while allowing regulated capture and transport toward lawful storage outside that prohibited area. The amendment is not a project authorization.
source: Finlex / Ministry of Justice of Finland
status_note: 2025 amendment incorporated into the current CCS Act.

document_title: Закон за съхранение на въглероден диоксид в земните недра
notes: This law establishes Bulgaria's binding framework for geological CO2 storage and applies to Bulgarian territory, the continental shelf and the Black Sea exclusive economic zone. It regulates exploration and storage permits, site suitability, monitoring, corrective measures, closure and operator obligations while prohibiting storage in the water column and other excluded settings. The law therefore provides a conditional legal pathway for offshore geological storage under Bulgarian jurisdiction but does not authorize injection at a named Black Sea project.
source: National Assembly of Bulgaria / State Gazette
status_note: Binding national geological CO2 storage law in force.

document_title: Ο Περί της Αποθήκευσης Διοξειδίου του Άνθρακα σε Γεωλογικούς Σχηματισμούς Νόμος του 2012 (71(I)/2012)
notes: This law establishes Cyprus's binding framework for geological CO2 storage and implements Directive 2009/31/EC. It applies to the Republic's jurisdiction including the exclusive economic zone and continental shelf and contains requirements for exploration and storage permits, permit modification and review, environmental assessment, financial security, monitoring, corrective action, closure and responsibility. The law enables storage only under formal authorization and does not itself approve a named offshore storage complex.
source: House of Representatives of Cyprus / CyLaw
status_note: Current consolidated law, including the 2015 amendment.

document_title: Ο περί της Αποθήκευσης Διοξειδίου του Άνθρακα σε Γεωλογικούς Σχηματισμούς (Τροποποιητικός) Νόμος του 2015 (174(I)/2015)
notes: This formal amendment updates Cyprus's 2012 geological CO2 storage law and is incorporated into the consolidated national framework. It maintains the binding permit-and-safeguard regime that applies to geological storage under Cypriot jurisdiction, including the exclusive economic zone and continental shelf. The amendment is a legal update rather than a storage-site decision and does not authorize a named offshore project or injection operation.
source: House of Representatives of Cyprus / CyLaw
status_note: Amendment enacted in 2015 and incorporated into the consolidated 2012 law.

document_title: Loi du 11 décembre 2022 visant la protection du milieu marin et l’organisation de l’aménagement des espaces marins belges
notes: This federal law protects the marine environment and governs activities in Belgian marine spaces. Its dumping regime prohibits disposal in Belgian marine areas and allows a royal exemption for captured CO2 streams only where the geological storage takes place outside Belgian marine spaces, making the law directly restrictive for domestic marine geological storage. The instrument therefore functions as a marine environmental prohibition and safeguard rather than an authorization for storage beneath the Belgian part of the North Sea.
source: Belgian Official Journal / Federal Government of Belgium
status_note: Binding federal marine-environment law in force.

document_title: Earth's Crust Act
notes: The current Earth's Crust Act contains a direct prohibition on geological CO2 storage in the territory of Estonia and under the Estonian continental shelf. A narrow exception applies where the total stored amount is below 100,000 tonnes and the activity is undertaken for research, development or testing of new products and processes. The Act therefore establishes a prohibitive national and offshore storage policy with only a small-scale research exception; it does not provide a commercial offshore storage authorization pathway.
source: Riigikogu / Riigi Teataja
status_note: Current Earth's Crust Act; the CO2 storage prohibition remains in force.

document_title: Water Act
notes: The Estonian Water Act contains an explicit prohibition on storing carbon dioxide in marine areas. For this purpose, marine storage includes placing CO2 into the water column, placing it on the seabed, or storing it in geological formations beneath the seabed. The Act also provides penalties for violating the marine CO2 storage prohibition. This is a direct marine-law restriction and should not be interpreted as an offshore CCS permitting framework.
source: Riigikogu / Riigi Teataja
status_note: Current Water Act; marine CO2 storage prohibition remains in force.

document_title: Atmospheric Air Protection Act
notes: The Atmospheric Air Protection Act regulates capture, transportation and geological-storage-related CO2 streams even though Estonia prohibits domestic commercial geological storage under other national laws. It defines geological storage, regulates transport-pipeline access and safety, sets CO2-stream composition requirements, requires reporting of captured and transported quantities and links verified permanent storage to emissions-trading treatment. It also limits transport for storage to eligible European Union territories, economic zones and continental shelves. The Act supports regulated capture and cross-border transport but does not authorize geological storage under the Estonian continental shelf.
source: Riigikogu / Riigi Teataja
status_note: Current atmospheric-air legislation with CCS capture, transport and reporting provisions.

document_title: Ordonnance n° 2010-1232 du 21 octobre 2010 — dispositions relatives au stockage géologique de dioxyde de carbone
notes: This ordinance introduced the legislative basis for geological CO2 storage into French environmental and mining law. The relevant provisions extend to French territory, the continental shelf and the French exclusive economic zone and establish the legal architecture for exploration, geological storage, network access and environmental protection. Storage in the water column is excluded, while sub-seabed geological storage may proceed only under the applicable authorization framework. The ordinance creates the statutory basis for marine CCS regulation but does not authorize a named offshore project.
source: Government of France / Légifrance
status_note: Legislative CCS provisions remain part of the French legal framework.

document_title: Décret n° 2011-1411 du 31 octobre 2011 relatif au stockage géologique de dioxyde de carbone afin de lutter contre le réchauffement climatique
notes: This decree implements detailed French procedures for geological CO2 storage. It addresses exploration and storage authorization, technical documentation, injection testing, monitoring, corrective measures, closure and post-closure obligations, financial security and administrative supervision, including applications involving the continental shelf. The decree operationalizes the binding statutory framework for potential marine geological storage but does not itself grant a permit to a named offshore project.
source: Government of France / Légifrance
status_note: Binding implementing decree in force, subject to later amendments and related regulations.

document_title: Mijnbouwwet
notes: The Dutch Mining Act is the principal statutory framework for subsurface activities and its current consolidated text contains the permit regime for permanent geological CO2 storage. The Act applies to activities on the Dutch continental shelf and requires ministerial authorization for storage, with CO2-specific provisions governing storage-complex boundaries, operating conditions, monitoring, corrective action, closure, financial security and transfer of responsibility. The 2002 year reflects the original enactment of the Mining Act; the detailed CO2 storage provisions were added through later amendments, especially the 2011 CCS implementation law. The Act is a regulatory framework and does not itself authorize a named offshore storage project.
source: Government of the Netherlands / Wetten.overheid.nl
status_note: Current consolidated Mining Act containing geological CO2 storage provisions.

document_title: Wet van 6 juni 2011 tot wijziging van de Mijnbouwwet in verband met implementatie van richtlijn 2009/31/EG en OSPAR Decision 2007/2
notes: This 2011 Act amended the Dutch Mining Act to implement Directive 2009/31/EC on geological CO2 storage and OSPAR Decision 2007/2 on storage of CO2 streams in geological formations. It inserted the core storage-permit, operator-responsibility, monitoring, closure, financial-security and environmental-safeguard rules that now operate through the consolidated Mining Act, including for offshore storage under Dutch jurisdiction. The amending Act has completed its legislative implementation function, so it should not be read as a separate project authorization; its substantive rules continue through the current Mining Act.
source: Government of the Netherlands / Staatsblad
status_note: The amending Act is officially identified as materially exhausted after implementation; its provisions remain incorporated in the current Mining Act.

document_title: Mijnbouwbesluit
notes: The Dutch Mining Decree provides detailed implementing rules under the Mining Act and contains a dedicated set of provisions for permanent CO2 storage and transport. The current rules address matters including storage plans, CO2-stream acceptance, leakage and significant irregularities, monitoring of injection facilities and the storage complex, periodic monitoring-plan updates and financial contributions associated with post-closure responsibility. These requirements apply within the Dutch geological storage licensing system, including offshore projects, but the decree does not authorize a specific storage site.
source: Government of the Netherlands / Wetten.overheid.nl
status_note: Current consolidated Mining Decree with CO2-specific implementing provisions.

document_title: Besluit van 29 augustus 2011 houdende wijziging van het Mijnbouwbesluit en twee andere besluiten in verband met bepalingen voor het permanent opslaan van CO2
notes: This 2011 decree amendment implemented detailed requirements for permanent geological CO2 storage in the Dutch Mining Decree and related regulations following the statutory CCS amendments. It translated the European Union CCS Directive into operational rules on storage safety, permit conditions, monitoring, leakage response, closure and other technical safeguards. The amendment is an implementing legal instrument rather than a project approval and its requirements now operate through the consolidated Mining Decree.
source: Government of the Netherlands / Staatsblad
status_note: Implemented in 2011; substantive provisions remain reflected in the current Mining Decree.

document_title: Regeling van 13 september 2011 houdende wijziging van de Mijnbouwregeling in verband met bepalingen voor het permanent opslaan van CO2
notes: This ministerial regulation amendment provides further implementation of the Dutch geological CO2 storage framework after the 2011 Mining Act and Mining Decree amendments. It supplies additional technical and administrative requirements needed to apply the CCS Directive and OSPAR Decision 2007/2 through the Mining Regulation, supporting standardized permit documentation, monitoring and regulatory oversight. It is a binding implementing rule and not a storage permit for a named offshore project.
source: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Agriculture and Innovation / Staatscourant
status_note: Implemented in 2011 as part of the Dutch CCS regulatory package.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Regulatory Levies) Act 2003
notes: The Act establishes statutory regulatory levies for the Commonwealth offshore petroleum and greenhouse-gas regime, including safety investigation, safety-case, well, annual title-administration and environment-plan levies. Its current framework expressly covers Commonwealth waters, designated coastal waters and cross-boundary greenhouse-gas titles. For marine geological CO2 storage, the Act provides the legal basis for recovering regulatory and title-administration costs from relevant offshore titleholders; it does not establish a carbon-credit mechanism, quantify carbon removal, or itself grant an assessment permit, holding lease or injection licence.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Principal Commonwealth levy legislation remains in force and supports administration of offshore greenhouse-gas titles.
