document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006
notes: This is the principal Commonwealth statute governing offshore petroleum and greenhouse-gas storage in Australian offshore areas. Chapter 3 creates a dedicated title system for greenhouse-gas assessment permits, holding leases and injection licences, provides for declaration of identified greenhouse-gas storage formations, prohibits unauthorised offshore injection and storage, imposes licence conditions, and provides for directions, surrender, cancellation and site-closing obligations. The current Act also accommodates cross-boundary greenhouse-gas titles. It establishes the legal pathway under which offshore geological CO2 storage can be authorised, but the Act itself is not a project-specific injection licence and does not demonstrate that any particular storage project has commenced injection or achieved verified removals.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Principal Commonwealth offshore greenhouse-gas storage statute; current compilation remains in force.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Environment) Regulations 2009
notes: These regulations formed the Commonwealth offshore environmental-management regime that applied under the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006 before the 2023 replacement instrument. The framework required regulated offshore activities to operate under accepted environment plans and incorporated consultation, environmental-performance objectives and risk-management requirements; greenhouse-gas-storage-specific amendments were incorporated into the instrument in 2020. The instrument is historically relevant to marine geological CO2 storage because it governed the environmental approval layer for offshore greenhouse-gas activities during part of the pre-2024 regime. It has been repealed and therefore does not provide the current environmental approval pathway.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Historical offshore environment regulations; replaced by the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Environment) Regulations 2023.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Safety) Regulations 2009
notes: These regulations provided the former Commonwealth safety-case and facility-safety regime for offshore petroleum and greenhouse-gas activities under the 2006 Act. They governed operator nomination, safety cases, offshore facilities, occupational safety obligations, notifications and reporting and therefore formed part of the regulatory conditions applicable to offshore greenhouse-gas infrastructure. The instrument was a safety and facility-control rule rather than an authorization to inject CO2, a carbon-accounting method or evidence of storage deployment. It ceased to operate when the 2024 Safety Regulations took over the framework in June 2025.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Former offshore safety regulations; repealed on 12 June 2025 and replaced by the 2024 Safety Regulations.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Resource Management and Administration) Regulations 2011
notes: The regulations established the former detailed resource-management, data and administrative framework under the Commonwealth offshore Act. Their stated objects included ensuring timely and consistent information on exploration for greenhouse-gas storage formations, discovery and appraisal of potential storage formations, greenhouse-gas injection operations and the results of operations, as well as collection, retention and dissemination of greenhouse-gas data. The instrument supported title administration and operational reporting rather than creating a standalone right to inject CO2. It was repealed on 31 March 2026 when the new 2025 Resource Management and Administration Regulations became operative.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Repealed on 31 March 2026 after long-running application; superseded by the 2025 resource-management regulations.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Greenhouse Gas Injection and Storage) Regulations 2011
notes: This former specialist instrument prescribed technical information and risk requirements for offshore greenhouse-gas injection and storage. It addressed determination of significant risk of significant adverse impact, declaration and characterization of identified storage formations, project and site-plan information, plume-migration modelling, storage-formation integrity, risk-control and remediation strategies, monitoring of stored greenhouse gases and losses from injection and wells, site closure and consultation. The regulations therefore provided an important MRV, risk and technical-planning layer for marine geological CO2 storage, but they did not themselves approve an individual injection project. They are no longer in force and have been replaced by the 2023 injection-and-storage regulations.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Historical specialist injection-and-storage regulations; no longer in force after 23 February 2024.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act 2019
notes: The amending Act made a substantial package of changes to the Commonwealth offshore statute, with Schedule 1 specifically devoted to greenhouse-gas storage. The amendments modernised and clarified elements of the offshore greenhouse-gas title, operational and compliance framework and were accompanied by broader changes to information protection, ministerial directions, compliance powers and well-integrity oversight. Its policy significance is regulatory: it strengthens and adjusts the legal architecture under which offshore CO2 storage can be assessed and controlled. It does not itself issue an assessment permit or injection licence and does not authorize a named storage project.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Assented to on 28 October 2019; relevant amendments were incorporated into the continuing Commonwealth offshore framework.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Cross-boundary Greenhouse Gas Titles and Other Measures) Act 2020
notes: The Act amended the Commonwealth offshore regime to create and administer cross-boundary greenhouse-gas titles where a storage formation or title area spans relevant jurisdictional boundaries. Schedule 1 is expressly dedicated to cross-boundary greenhouse-gas storage and provides the statutory architecture for cross-boundary assessment permits, holding leases and injection licences, together with associated administration and transitional provisions. The measure enables coherent permitting of offshore storage formations that cannot be managed within a single title boundary, but it does not itself approve a storage site, authorize injection into a named formation or demonstrate that cross-boundary storage has occurred.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Assented to in 2020; operative cross-boundary greenhouse-gas title provisions form part of the current Commonwealth regime.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Regulatory Levies) Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Act 2020
notes: This amending Act aligned the offshore regulatory-levy legislation with the new cross-boundary greenhouse-gas title framework. Schedule 1 specifically addresses cross-boundary greenhouse-gas titles and ensures that the regulatory cost-recovery architecture can apply when greenhouse-gas storage titles span relevant offshore boundaries. The instrument is administrative and financial regulation of the permitting system rather than carbon finance: it does not create tradable carbon units, subsidize storage, or itself confer a right to inject or permanently store CO2.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Assented to on 15 May 2020; its cross-boundary levy amendments support the continuing offshore title regime.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Legislation Amendment (Greenhouse Gas Storage) Regulations 2020
notes: This amending instrument updated several Commonwealth offshore regulations to implement revised greenhouse-gas storage provisions, including amendments to the environment and resource-management frameworks and associated regulatory levies. Its practical role was to integrate greenhouse-gas storage more fully into environmental, operational, information and administrative regulation under the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act. As an amending instrument, it completed its legislative function after its amendments were incorporated into principal regulations; it was not a project permit and does not provide current standalone operational rules.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Amending instrument made in April 2020; its amendments were incorporated into principal regulations and the instrument itself is no longer in force.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Legislation Amendment (Cross-boundary Greenhouse Gas Storage) Regulations 2020
notes: The regulations implemented consequential and administrative changes required by the 2020 cross-boundary greenhouse-gas title legislation. They amended the Commonwealth offshore regulatory framework so that resource-management, administration and related requirements could operate for cross-boundary greenhouse-gas permits, leases and injection licences. The measure supports a unified legal treatment of offshore storage formations that extend across relevant title or jurisdictional boundaries. It was an amending instrument rather than a storage authorization and has completed its standalone legislative function.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Amending regulations made in September 2020; their operative changes were incorporated into principal instruments.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Regulatory Levies) Amendment (Cross-boundary Greenhouse Gas Storage) Regulations 2020
notes: The instrument amended Commonwealth regulatory-levy rules to accommodate cross-boundary greenhouse-gas storage titles created by the 2020 legislative reforms. It ensured that the regulatory cost-recovery system could operate for cross-boundary assessment, holding and injection title administration. The measure concerns fees and regulatory administration rather than the environmental performance or carbon accounting of storage and did not grant any project-specific storage right. The amending instrument is no longer in force as a standalone regulation.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Amending instrument operated from 18 September 2020 to 2 February 2021; its changes were incorporated into the levy framework.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Regulatory Levies) Regulations 2022
notes: The regulations prescribe the amounts and operation of Commonwealth offshore regulatory levies, including annual title-administration charges for work-bid and cross-boundary greenhouse-gas assessment permits, greenhouse-gas holding leases and greenhouse-gas injection licences. They also form part of the safety, well and environment-plan cost-recovery system administered under the offshore legislation. Their purpose is regulatory financing and administration of the offshore title system; they are not a carbon-finance instrument, do not issue carbon credits and do not authorize a specific CO2 storage project.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Principal levy regulations registered in 2022 and currently in force, with a 2026 compilation.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Environment) Regulations 2023
notes: The regulations establish the current Commonwealth environmental-management process for offshore petroleum and greenhouse-gas activities. They require offshore project proposals and environment plans, provide for publication and public comment, and set the regulatory framework for assessing and managing environmental impacts before and during regulated offshore activities. For marine geological CO2 storage they operate as an environmental approval and safeguard layer alongside the title and injection/storage rules. Acceptance of an environment plan is not equivalent to grant of a greenhouse-gas injection licence, and the regulations do not by themselves authorize a specific storage project.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Registered and effective from 10 July 2023; current principal offshore environment regulations.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Greenhouse Gas Injection and Storage) Regulations 2023
notes: The regulations are the current specialist Commonwealth rules for offshore greenhouse-gas injection and storage. They prescribe how significant risk of significant adverse impact is determined and support statutory decisions concerning storage formations and greenhouse-gas titles. Together with the principal Act and resource-management rules, they provide technical and risk safeguards for marine geological CO2 storage. They establish regulatory criteria rather than an automatic deployment entitlement: a proponent still requires the relevant title, approvals and project-specific compliance before injection can occur.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Made in November 2023 and currently in force; latest compilation incorporates 2026 consequential amendments.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Safety) Regulations 2024
notes: The regulations establish the current offshore safety framework under the Commonwealth Act and expressly address new greenhouse-gas facilities through design-notification and safety-case requirements. They regulate operators, facilities, safety management, notices and reports and therefore form a mandatory technical safeguard for infrastructure used in offshore greenhouse-gas storage operations. The instrument controls facility safety and operational risk; it does not establish a carbon-removal methodology, quantify stored CO2, or substitute for the separate greenhouse-gas title and injection-licence process.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Current Commonwealth offshore safety regulations; operative framework includes specific provisions for new GHG facilities.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2010
notes: The Act establishes Victoria's statutory framework for offshore petroleum and greenhouse-gas storage in Victorian coastal waters. For greenhouse gases it creates a title system that includes assessment permits, holding leases and injection licences, together with related powers for storage-formation identification, title administration, transfer and compliance. The regime is directly relevant to marine geological CO2 storage because the State offshore framework applies within Victorian State waters. The Act establishes legal pathways and regulatory controls but does not itself approve a particular CO2 injection project, quantify a removal outcome or create a carbon-crediting mechanism.
source: Government of Victoria — Victorian Legislation
status_note: Principal Victorian offshore petroleum and greenhouse-gas storage legislation remains in force.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Regulations 2011
notes: These regulations formed the earlier subsidiary regulatory layer under Victoria's Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2010. They supported administration of offshore titles and operations, including the greenhouse-gas storage regime in Victorian coastal waters. They are retained as a historical implementation record because they governed the framework before being revoked on 12 December 2021 by the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Regulations 2021. The regulations no longer authorize or regulate new activities and should not be treated as the current operational rules.
source: Government of Victoria — Victorian Legislation
status_note: Revoked on 12 December 2021 and replaced by the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Regulations 2021.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Regulations 2021
notes: These regulations provide the current subsidiary rules supporting Victoria's Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2010. They operate within the State offshore title and regulatory framework for petroleum and greenhouse-gas activities in Victorian coastal waters and support administration, reporting and compliance for greenhouse-gas titles and operations. The authorised version history shows the regulations remain in force, with a current version effective from 7 May 2026. They regulate the framework but do not themselves issue an injection licence or authorize a specific CO2 storage project.
source: Government of Victoria — Victorian Legislation
status_note: In force; current authorised version effective from 7 May 2026.

document_title: Financial capability policy for petroleum and greenhouse gas applications
notes: The policy explains how the Victorian Minister for Energy and Resources or delegate assesses whether applicants have sufficient financial capability to undertake petroleum and greenhouse-gas exploration, injection, storage, rehabilitation and closure obligations. It expressly applies under the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2010 to work-bid and cash-bid greenhouse-gas assessment permits and to greenhouse-gas injection-licence applications, including applications by assessment-permit, holding-lease and petroleum-production-licence holders. The assessment considers the applicant's capacity to fund the full lifecycle of proposed work, including environmental protection, rehabilitation and closure. The policy is an application-assessment standard rather than a project approval and does not itself confer a storage title or injection licence.
source: Government of Victoria — Resources Victoria
status_note: Current Victorian application-assessment policy for petroleum and greenhouse-gas titles.

document_title: Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2009
notes: The Act establishes Queensland's statutory regime for greenhouse-gas geological storage and creates greenhouse-gas authorities, including exploration and storage tenure, associated pipeline access and safety and enforcement arrangements. Section 6 expressly applies the Act to Queensland coastal waters as if those waters were part of the State, while excluding the adjacent area governed by the Petroleum (Submerged Lands) Act 1982. The marine relevance is therefore explicit but geographically limited to State coastal waters. The Act establishes authorization and regulatory pathways for geological storage; it does not by itself approve a specific offshore injection project or quantify stored CO2.
source: Queensland Government — Queensland Legislation
status_note: In force; expressly applies to Queensland coastal waters, subject to the statutory exclusion of the adjacent area.

document_title: Greenhouse Gas Storage Regulation 2021
notes: The regulation implements the Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2009 by prescribing information and administrative requirements for greenhouse-gas permits, leases, work programs and development plans. It requires matters such as geological models, assessments of potential storage sites, proposed activities and resource-conflict information, and it also prescribes security and information-management requirements. Because the parent Act expressly extends to Queensland coastal waters, these subsidiary requirements can govern marine geological CO2 storage within that State-water jurisdiction. The regulation is a regulatory framework and does not itself award a GHG lease or authorize injection at a specific site.
source: Queensland Government — Queensland Legislation
status_note: In force; current reprint includes amendments commencing 19 June 2025.

document_title: Mineral and Energy Resources and Other Legislation Amendment Regulation 2025
notes: This amending regulation updates several Queensland resource regulations and includes a dedicated amendment to the Greenhouse Gas Storage Regulation 2021. Among other changes, it replaces the prescribed financial-security amounts for greenhouse-gas permits, greenhouse-gas leases and greenhouse-gas data-acquisition authorities. Because the underlying Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2009 expressly applies to Queensland coastal waters, the amendment also affects the financial-security architecture for GHG authorities that may operate within that marine State-water jurisdiction. It does not grant a storage lease, select a storage formation or authorize a specific injection operation.
source: Queensland Government — Queensland Legislation
status_note: Commenced on 19 June 2025.

document_title: Petroleum Legislation Amendment Act 2024
notes: The Act reforms Western Australia's petroleum legislation to establish a statutory framework for greenhouse-gas transport and permanent underground storage. Its amendments extend across the State's petroleum legislation, including the Petroleum (Submerged Lands) Act 1982, and introduce greenhouse-gas acreage release and licensing pathways, rights in identified storage formations, transport through pipelines, site closure and long-term liability arrangements. The marine component is direct because the amended Submerged Lands Act governs the offshore State jurisdiction. Most substantive greenhouse-gas provisions commenced on 28 May 2026 under a formal commencement proclamation. The Act creates the legal framework but does not itself approve a particular injection site or project.
source: Government of Western Australia — Parliamentary Counsel's Office
status_note: Assented to on 14 May 2024; the new greenhouse-gas storage and transport framework took effect on 28 May 2026.

document_title: Petroleum Legislation Amendment Act 2024 Commencement Proclamation 2026
notes: The proclamation activates the remaining substantive provisions of the Petroleum Legislation Amendment Act 2024, subject to the specific provisions excluded in the proclamation. It was published on 27 May 2026 and causes the relevant greenhouse-gas transport and storage reforms, including reforms to the State's submerged-lands offshore framework, to commence on the following day. Its practical role is commencement and legal activation rather than the creation of a separate project approval. It therefore marks the point at which the new Western Australian offshore greenhouse-gas storage framework became operational but does not itself grant an exploration permit, retention lease or injection licence.
source: Government of Western Australia — Parliamentary Counsel's Office
status_note: Published 27 May 2026; relevant substantive amendments commenced on 28 May 2026.

document_title: Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Submerged Lands) (Greenhouse Gas Injection and Storage) Regulations 2026
notes: These regulations are the dedicated offshore subsidiary rules for greenhouse-gas injection and permanent storage under Western Australia's Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Submerged Lands) Act 1982. Their stated objects include ensuring that greenhouse-gas injection and permanent storage operations are properly carried out and regulated. They provide the technical and administrative layer for operations under the new offshore title framework and became current on 28 May 2026. The regulations govern how authorized activities are conducted and assessed; they do not themselves award a particular injection licence or establish that any specific storage project has commenced injection.
source: Government of Western Australia — Parliamentary Counsel's Office
status_note: Published 27 May 2026; substantive provisions current from 28 May 2026.

document_title: Criteria for assessment: Petroleum, geothermal energy and greenhouse gas exploration permits
notes: The guideline sets assessment criteria for applications for petroleum, geothermal-energy and greenhouse-gas exploration permits under Western Australia's petroleum statutes, including the Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Submerged Lands) Act 1982. It therefore provides an application-assessment standard for offshore greenhouse-gas exploration acreage as well as the onshore framework. The document supports transparent evaluation of permit applicants and work proposals after commencement of the 2024 legislative reforms. It is guidance for deciding whether an exploration permit should be granted; it is not itself an exploration permit, a declaration of a storage formation or authorization to inject CO2.
source: Government of Western Australia — Department of Mines, Petroleum and Exploration
status_note: Final guidance updated on 10 June 2026 following commencement of the reformed greenhouse-gas framework.

document_title: Application for declaration of identified Greenhouse Gas Storage
notes: This guideline explains the application process for ministerial declaration of an identified greenhouse-gas storage formation under Western Australia's petroleum legislation. It expressly applies to both the Petroleum, Geothermal Energy and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 1967 and the Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Submerged Lands) Act 1982. A ministerial declaration of an identified storage formation is a prerequisite before an applicant can seek a greenhouse-gas retention lease or injection licence. The document therefore operationalizes a key screening step for offshore geological CO2 storage, but the guidance itself does not declare a formation, grant a retention lease or authorize injection.
source: Government of Western Australia — Department of Mines, Petroleum and Exploration
status_note: Final guidance updated on 9 June 2026.

document_title: Response to public submissions – Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Regulations
notes: This formal response document records Western Australia's consideration of stakeholder submissions on the draft greenhouse-gas injection and storage regulations that accompanied implementation of the Petroleum Legislation Amendment Act 2024. The consultation covered both the landward petroleum statute and the Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Submerged Lands) framework, so the response directly addresses the offshore regulatory package for permanent underground storage of greenhouse-gas substances. Submissions were grouped by theme and the regulations were revised where appropriate before finalization. The document is evidence of completed regulatory consultation and policy development; it is not a binding storage rule or a project authorization.
source: Government of Western Australia — Department of Mines, Petroleum and Exploration
status_note: Consultation response published in May 2026; the associated final regulations subsequently commenced on 28 May 2026.

document_title: Draft Annual Pipeline Performance Report for pipeline licensees – guideline and templates
notes: This consultation package proposed a standardized annual pipeline performance report and associated templates for Western Australian pipeline licensees. The package included reporting under the Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Submerged Lands) pipeline framework, making it relevant to offshore transport infrastructure that can support greenhouse-gas storage projects. Its policy function was to define a repeatable annual reporting and performance-information structure and to seek stakeholder feedback before finalization. The consultation closed in January 2026. Because the material was issued as a draft consultation package, it should not be treated as a final reporting standard or as authorization for a CO2 pipeline or storage project.
source: Government of Western Australia — Department of Mines, Petroleum and Exploration
status_note: Draft consultation closed on 30 January 2026; the record represents the consultation stage rather than an adopted final guideline.

document_title: Mines and Petroleum Regulations Amendment Regulations 2026
notes: These amending regulations implement consequential changes required for Western Australia's reformed petroleum and greenhouse-gas storage framework. The instrument directly amends multiple petroleum regulations, including the Submerged Lands environment, pipeline and resource-management regimes, by inserting greenhouse-gas activities and updating statutory references following the Petroleum Legislation Amendment Act 2024. Its marine relevance is explicit because dedicated parts amend regulations made under the State's submerged-lands offshore legislation. The instrument integrates greenhouse-gas storage into the existing offshore regulatory architecture but does not itself grant a greenhouse-gas title or authorize injection at a specific storage formation.
source: Government of Western Australia — Parliamentary Counsel's Office
status_note: Published 27 May 2026; relevant amendments commenced with the new greenhouse-gas framework on 28 May 2026.

document_title: Environment Regulations Amendment (Petroleum Legislation) Regulations 2026
notes: This instrument updates Western Australia's environmental regulatory references to align them with the new petroleum and greenhouse-gas storage legislation. It expressly incorporates references to the Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Submerged Lands) (Environment) Regulations 2012 and the corresponding Submerged Lands resource-management rules, thereby integrating offshore greenhouse-gas activities into the broader environmental regulatory framework. The amendments commenced in conjunction with key provisions of the Petroleum Legislation Amendment Act 2024. The instrument strengthens regulatory alignment and environmental oversight but does not itself approve a storage formation, injection licence or individual offshore project.
source: Government of Western Australia — Parliamentary Counsel's Office
status_note: Published 27 May 2026; substantive amendments commenced with the greenhouse-gas legislative reforms on 28 May 2026.

document_title: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Minister for Environment of the Flemish Region and the Federal Minister for the North Sea of Belgium and the Minister of Energy and Climate of the Walloon Region and the Minister of Energy of Norway on Cross-border Transportation of CO2 with the Purpose of Permanent Geological Storage
notes: The memorandum establishes a bilateral administrative framework for cross-border transport of captured CO2 from Belgium to Norway for permanent geological storage, supporting implementation of the London Protocol Article 6 requirements and related permitting, reporting and supervisory coordination. It is designed to remove legal and administrative barriers to cross-border CCS chains and clarify cooperation between competent authorities. The MoU is expressly non-binding and does not create rights or obligations under international law. It enables regulatory cooperation but does not itself grant a transport permit, storage permit or injection authorization for any specific offshore project.
source: Governments of Belgium and Norway
status_note: Signed on 15 April 2024 and operating as a non-binding cross-border CCS administrative arrangement.

document_title: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities of Denmark and Ministry of Energy of Norway on Cross-border Transportation of CO2 with the Purpose of Permanent Geological Storage
notes: The memorandum creates a bilateral cooperation arrangement for cross-border transport of captured CO2 between Denmark and Norway for permanent geological storage. It supports implementation of the London Protocol Article 6 framework and coordinates the authorities responsible for permitting, supervision, reporting and exchange of information across a transboundary CCS chain. The arrangement is policy-enabling rather than a commercial or project-specific approval. It is non-binding and does not itself authorize shipment, pipeline transport, storage-site operation or injection at any particular offshore reservoir.
source: Governments of Denmark and Norway
status_note: Signed on 15 April 2024 as a non-binding bilateral arrangement for cross-border CO2 transport and storage.

document_title: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Ministry of Climate and the Environment in Sweden and Ministry of Energy of Norway on Cross-border Transportation of CO2 with the Purpose of Permanent Geological Storage
notes: The memorandum establishes non-binding cooperation between Sweden and Norway for cross-border transport of CO2 intended for permanent geological storage. It is part of the bilateral arrangements used to facilitate compliance with international rules governing export of CO2 streams for sub-seabed storage and to coordinate competent authorities, permitting and information exchange. Its policy effect is to enable a transboundary CCS value chain while retaining the need for all project-level approvals under domestic and international law. It does not itself authorize transport, approve a storage site or permit injection.
source: Governments of Sweden and Norway
status_note: Concluded in April 2024 as a non-binding bilateral arrangement supporting cross-border CO2 transport and permanent storage.

document_title: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities of Denmark and Ministry of Climate and Enterprise of Sweden on Cross-border Transportation of CO2 with the Purpose of Permanent Geological Storage
notes: The memorandum establishes a non-binding Denmark–Sweden framework for cross-border transport of captured CO2 for permanent geological storage. It supports the international legal arrangements needed for transboundary CCS, promotes administrative cooperation and helps coordinate permitting, reporting and competent-authority responsibilities. The instrument facilitates future transport-and-storage chains but leaves individual projects subject to national licensing, environmental assessment and other applicable requirements. It therefore should not be interpreted as a transport authorization, storage permit or approval for a particular injection operation.
source: Governments of Denmark and Sweden
status_note: Signed on 15 April 2024 as a non-binding bilateral cross-border CCS arrangement.

document_title: Høring - forslag til endringer i lagringsforskriften
notes: The Ministry of Energy consultation proposes amendments to Norway's regulation on the use of subsea reservoirs on the continental shelf for CO2 storage and on CO2 transport on the continental shelf. The proposal is intended to simplify parts of the regulatory framework and make technical adaptations based on experience with the developing CCS sector. Because the underlying storage regulation governs subsea reservoirs and offshore CO2 transport, the consultation is directly relevant to marine geological CO2 storage. The consultation closed on 5 June 2026 and remains under consideration; the proposed amendments are not yet binding rules and do not constitute authorization for any specific storage project.
source: Norway Ministry of Energy
status_note: Consultation launched on 9 March 2026; deadline 5 June 2026; government page lists the matter as under consideration.

document_title: Forskrift om endring i forskrift 27. juni 1997 nr. 653 til lov om petroleumsvirksomhet, forskrift 5. desember 2014 nr. 1517 om utnyttelse av undersjøiske reservoarer på kontinentalsokkelen til lagring av CO2 og om transport av CO2 på kontinentalsokkelen og forskrift 12. juni 2020 nr. 1192 til havenergilova
notes: This amending regulation modifies several Norwegian offshore energy instruments, including the 2014 regulation governing use of subsea reservoirs on the continental shelf for CO2 storage and transport of CO2 on the continental shelf. It forms part of the legal coordination of offshore activities with wider marine-environment and international obligations and updates the regulatory treatment of activities that may have significant effects beyond national jurisdiction. The amendment is legally binding and entered into force for Norway on 17 January 2026. It changes the regulatory framework applicable to offshore storage and transport but does not itself award acreage, approve a storage plan or authorize injection at a particular reservoir.
source: Norway — Lovdata / Ministry of Energy
status_note: Adopted on 27 May 2025; relevant provisions entered into force for Norway on 17 January 2026.

document_title: Qatar National Environment and Climate Change Strategy 2030
notes: Qatar's national environment and climate strategy provides the high-level policy framework for environmental and climate action through 2030. Official implementation material under its greenhouse-gas priority identifies further carbon capture and storage deployment and investment in nature-based solutions, including blue-carbon projects, as components of the mitigation portfolio. The blue-carbon element makes the strategy relevant to coastal and marine carbon-sink enhancement, while the CCS element is broader and is not treated here as evidence of a particular marine storage project. The strategy is enabling and programmatic: it does not establish a blue-carbon crediting methodology, quantify a verified ocean carbon-removal outcome or itself issue a deployment permit.
source: Qatar Ministry of Environment and Climate Change
status_note: Launched in October 2021 and remains the national environment and climate strategy to 2030.

document_title: Meddelelse om ikrafttredelse av forskrift 27. mai 2025 nr. 870 om endring i forskrift 27. juni 1997 nr. 653 til lov om petroleumsvirksomhet, forskrift 5. desember 2014 nr. 1517 om utnyttelse av undersjøiske reservoarer på kontinentalsokkelen til lagring av CO2 og om transport av CO2 på kontinentalsokkelen og forskrift 12. juni 2020 nr. 1192 til havenergilova
notes: This formal commencement notice fixes 17 January 2026 as the effective date for Regulation FOR-2025-05-27-870. The underlying amendment changes, among other instruments, Norway's 2014 regulation on use of subsea reservoirs on the continental shelf for permanent CO2 storage and on transport of CO2 on the continental shelf. The notice therefore has a distinct legal function in the offshore carbon-storage regulatory chain: it activates the previously adopted amendment on a specified date. It does not itself alter the substantive storage requirements beyond bringing the amendment into force, allocate offshore acreage, approve a storage development plan or authorize injection at a specific site.
source: Norway — Lovdata / Ministry of Energy
status_note: Formal commencement notice published on 2 December 2025; the underlying amendment entered into force on 17 January 2026.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Titles Administration and Other Measures) Act 2021
notes: This amending Act materially strengthens administration of offshore petroleum and greenhouse-gas titles under the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006. Its schedules create a statutory approval regime for changes in control of registered titleholders, expand trailing-liability arrangements, revise application and decision-making processes, strengthen information-gathering powers and modernise administrative handling of offshore titles. These controls apply to greenhouse-gas assessment permits, holding leases and injection licences as part of the Commonwealth offshore carbon-storage framework. The Act is therefore a governance and safeguard instrument rather than a project approval: it does not identify a storage formation, allocate acreage or authorize injection, and its relevance lies in ownership control, regulatory accountability and continuing obligations around offshore titleholders.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Assented to on 2 September 2021; the substantive title-administration measures commenced in stages and remain incorporated in the current OPGGS Act framework.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Legislation Amendment (Titles Administration) Regulations 2021
notes: These regulations implemented parts of the 2021 titles-administration reforms by amending the Commonwealth offshore resource-management, environment and safety regulations. The instrument prescribed an application fee for approval of a change in control of a registered titleholder and made consequential provisions supporting the expanded trailing-liability regime. Because the affected title architecture includes greenhouse-gas assessment permits, holding leases and injection licences, the instrument formed part of the regulatory safeguards for offshore geological CO2 storage. The instrument is historical rather than current: the Federal Register records it as no longer in force, with its final operative period ending on 7 September 2022. It did not itself issue a greenhouse-gas title or authorize injection at any storage formation.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Registered on 9 December 2021; no longer in force after 7 September 2022. Its effects were part of the transition to the revised titles-administration framework.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Regulatory Levies) Amendment Act 2021
notes: This Act amends the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Regulatory Levies) Act 2003 as part of the Commonwealth offshore titles-administration reform package. The levy framework finances regulatory administration of offshore titles, including greenhouse-gas titles, and operates alongside the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006 and the National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator system. Its policy effect is administrative and cost-recovery oriented rather than technological: it supports the functioning of the offshore permitting and title-management regime but does not set a carbon-credit methodology, establish a verified removal quantity, identify a storage formation or grant permission to inject CO2. It is retained because it is a separate binding Act directly governing the administration of the same offshore greenhouse-gas title system.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Assented to on 3 September 2021 and listed by the Federal Register of Legislation as in force.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Legislation Amendment (Safety and Other Measures) Act 2024
notes: This Act strengthens the Commonwealth offshore safety and remedial-direction framework and makes additional amendments to the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006. The amendments expressly operate across greenhouse-gas assessment permits, greenhouse-gas holding leases and greenhouse-gas injection licences, including remedial directions concerning title areas and post-activity obligations. The Act also refines the statutory description of the spatial extent of an eligible greenhouse-gas storage formation by reference to expected migration pathways, which is directly relevant to delineation and regulation of subseabed CO2 storage. Its role is regulatory and precautionary: it strengthens safety, remediation and title-area governance but does not itself approve a particular storage formation or grant an injection licence.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Assented to on 11 June 2024; the Federal Register lists the Act as in force, with different schedules commencing according to the statutory commencement table.

document_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Regulatory Levies) Amendment (Annual Titles Administration Levy) Regulations 2024
notes: These regulations update the annual titles-administration levy and related application and service fees used to fund the National Offshore Petroleum Titles Administrator. The explanatory statement states that the instrument implements NOPTA's cost-recovery settings for 2025. The underlying levy system expressly applies to offshore greenhouse-gas titles, including work-bid and cross-boundary greenhouse-gas assessment permits, greenhouse-gas holding leases and greenhouse-gas injection licences. The measure therefore forms part of the administrative infrastructure of the Commonwealth offshore CO2-storage licensing system. It is a cost-recovery rule only: it does not establish environmental performance criteria, determine the suitability of a storage formation, issue a title or authorize CO2 injection.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Registered on 8 November 2024 and commenced on 1 January 2025; its levy changes are incorporated in the current Regulatory Levies Regulations 2022.

document_title: DENR Administrative Order No. 2026-05 — Guidelines Governing the Establishment, Registration, and Monitoring of Voluntary Forest Carbon Credit Projects
notes: The order creates binding procedures for establishing, registering and monitoring voluntary forest carbon credit projects and expressly recognizes blue-carbon and wetland restoration projects covering mangroves, seagrasses and marshes. It requires project documentation and database registration, use of recognized methodologies, independent validation and verification, MRV, protected-area or tenure approvals where applicable, and community and free, prior and informed consent safeguards. International voluntary-market participation is allowed only subject to DENR determinations, while NDC eligibility, corresponding adjustments and transfers of internationally transferred mitigation outcomes remain subject to separate policy issuances. The order therefore enables regulated blue-carbon credit projects but does not itself certify or issue credits to a specific project.
source: Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), Philippines
status_note: Promulgated on 24 February 2026 and applicable to new, pipeline and existing voluntary forest carbon credit projects within covered areas.

document_title: Thirteenth Malaysia Plan, 2026–2030
notes: The Thirteenth Malaysia Plan makes blue carbon part of the 2026–2030 national development framework. It calls for exploring the mapping of locations with high carbon-dioxide absorption, developing a blue-carbon credit assessment mechanism, integrating blue-economy information through blue accounting, and exploring blue-carbon initiatives in mangrove and wetland areas to support climate mitigation and coastal protection. The plan also places this work alongside implementation of a national carbon-market policy. These provisions establish an official planning and evidence-building pathway, but they do not by themselves create an operational blue-carbon credit methodology, issue credits, authorize a specific project, or quantify a stand-alone marine carbon-removal target.
source: Ministry of Economy, Malaysia
status_note: Presented in 2025; the national plan is being implemented for the 2026–2030 period.

document_title: The United Arab Emirates’ Third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0)
notes: The UAE NDC 3.0 treats removals as an explicit part of the national 2035 pathway, targeting aggregate negative-emissions capacity of about 9.3 MtCO2e and identifying extensive mangrove afforestation among the nature-based contributions. It reiterates the target to plant an additional 160 million mangroves by 2030 and describes management and restoration of blue-carbon ecosystems, blue-carbon accounting, coastal carbon-stock data and MRV, and long-term monitoring. The NDC also discusses the feasibility of blue-carbon offset projects and a national carbon-registry platform under Article 6, but the offset work remains at feasibility and policy-development stage rather than constituting a project-specific credit authorization. The 9.3 MtCO2e figure is an aggregate negative-emissions capacity that also includes non-marine removal approaches, so it should not be treated as a quantified blue-carbon removal target.
source: Government of the United Arab Emirates / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted to the UNFCCC on 6 November 2024.

document_title: J-Blue Credit Certification Application Guidelines — Climate Change Mitigation Utilizing Blue Carbon — Ver. 2.6
notes: Version 2.6 is the current Japanese application guide for seeking J-Blue Credit certification and issuance in fiscal year 2026. It provides the procedural and technical framework through which blue-carbon projects are documented, quantified, monitored and submitted for certification under the J-Blue Credit scheme, and the programme page confirms that applications for 2026 issuance are being accepted through the J-Blue Credit operating system. J-Blue Credit evaluates carbon dioxide removed from the atmosphere and stored for the long term in coastal and marine blue-carbon ecosystems using objective methodologies and independent committee review. The guide supports voluntary blue-carbon crediting rather than a statutory compliance market, and publication of the guide does not itself certify a project or guarantee credit issuance.
source: Japan Blue Economy Association (JBE)
status_note: Japanese Ver. 2.6 was issued in March 2026 and is being used for fiscal-year 2026 certification applications.

document_title: Host Party Participation Requirements for Article 6.4 Mechanism — Costa Rica
notes: Costa Rica’s host-Party submission identifies blue-carbon removal activities involving protection and restoration of mangroves, seagrasses and tidal marshes as activity types that may be considered for national approval under the Paris Agreement Article 6.4 mechanism. It commits the national authorities to a regulatory and operational framework covering technical guidance, safeguards, environmental integrity, registration, MRV and controls against double counting and double issuance. Approval of an Article 6.4 activity does not automatically authorize international transfer: each internationally transferred mitigation outcome must be assessed case by case and formally authorized by the Ministry of Environment and Energy. The submission therefore establishes eligibility and governance direction, not blanket project approval or automatic credit issuance.
source: FONAFIFO / Ministry of Environment and Energy (MINAE), Costa Rica / UNFCCC
status_note: Submitted to the UNFCCC and published on 5 December 2025 as Costa Rica’s host-Party participation framework for Article 6.4.

document_title: Seychelles NDC 3.0
notes: Seychelles NDC 3.0 records a concrete blue-carbon evidence and accounting step: mapping blue-carbon seagrass and incorporating the associated carbon stock into the national greenhouse-gas inventory. The NDC also states that the blue economy is considered in national strategies and transparency reporting, while additional data are still needed before the sector can be fully integrated into target modelling. The ONCE relevance is therefore primarily inventory, monitoring and knowledge building rather than deployment. The document does not set a quantified seagrass-removal target, authorize a restoration project, or establish a blue-carbon crediting mechanism.
source: Government of Seychelles / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted to the UNFCCC on 30 September 2025.

document_title: Fiji’s Third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0)
notes: Fiji’s NDC 3.0 includes restoration of blue-carbon ecosystems among its national ocean and marine-resource commitments, alongside sustainable management of the entire exclusive economic zone by 2035 and a 30 percent marine-protected-area objective. The blue-carbon measure is framed principally as a nature-based resilience and ecosystem action with climate-mitigation co-benefits rather than as a stand-alone quantified carbon-removal target. The NDC therefore supports restoration deployment at policy level, but the commitment does not specify a separate blue-carbon carbon-dioxide-equivalent quantity, project-level authorization, or dedicated crediting methodology.
source: Government of Fiji / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted to the UNFCCC on 6 November 2025; implementation period extends to 2035.

document_title: Panama NDC 3.0
notes: Panama’s third NDC commits the country to restore and reforest 100,000 hectares of ecosystems by 2035, explicitly including 2,500 hectares of mangroves, in support of increased national carbon-sink capacity and its longer-term objective of remaining carbon negative. The mangrove area is a concrete restoration component within a broader ecosystem target rather than a stand-alone blue-carbon credit programme. The NDC does not, for this commitment, provide a separate project-level authorization or dedicated blue-carbon crediting methodology, so the record treats the mangrove target as deployment and policy planning rather than an established marine crediting mechanism.
source: Government of Panama / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted to the UNFCCC on 27 November 2025.

document_title: Colombia NDC 3.0 — Transformaciones para la Vida
notes: Colombia’s NDC 3.0 establishes a blue-carbon knowledge, accounting and implementation pathway that goes beyond general coastal adaptation. It assigns national research institutions to calculate the greenhouse-gas mitigation potential of mangroves, seagrasses and other priority ecosystems, account for reduced or absorbed carbon, and build a monitoring system for non-forest land covers so that emissions, absorptions, reductions and removals can enter national information systems. The NDC also links standardized data and methodologies to the future participation of nature-based projects in voluntary and regulated carbon markets and includes restoration actions for mangroves and seagrasses. These provisions build measurement and market readiness, but they do not by themselves issue credits or quantify one aggregate blue-carbon removal target.
source: Government of Colombia / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted to the UNFCCC on 19 December 2025.

document_title: Host Party Participation Requirements for Article 6.4 Mechanism — Bangladesh
notes: Bangladesh’s Article 6.4 host-Party submission expressly lists mangrove reforestation and blue-carbon projects in marine and coastal ecosystems among the removal activities it would prioritize for consideration under the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism. Eligible activities must reduce or remove greenhouse-gas emissions, support sustainable development and contribute to implementation of the national NDC. The submission also records an Article 6 Designated National Authority governance structure and a national readiness roadmap, while noting that positive and negative project lists were still being prepared at the time of submission. It is therefore a formal eligibility and market-governance signal, not an approval of every blue-carbon project or an automatic authorization of internationally transferred credits.
source: Department of Environment, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bangladesh / UNFCCC
status_note: Published by the UNFCCC on 6 January 2025 as Bangladesh’s host-Party participation submission for the Article 6.4 mechanism.

document_title: Costa Rica NDC 2025–2035
notes: Costa Rica’s NDC 2025–2035 contains a dedicated Blue Carbon axis that links wetland conservation and mangrove restoration directly to greenhouse-gas capture and avoided emissions. It establishes milestones for characterizing wetlands with carbon-capture potential, building coverage and condition baselines for marine wetlands, and placing 2,000 hectares of mangrove into restoration, with recovery of 500 hectares per year. The NDC estimates approximately 52.33 Gg CO2e of sequestration associated with the 2,000-hectare restoration and rehabilitation effort over the stated period, while also requiring stronger monitoring and carbon-accounting information. These are formal national targets and quantified estimates, but they do not by themselves issue carbon credits or constitute project permits.
source: Ministry of Environment and Energy (MINAE), Costa Rica / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 2025–2035 submitted to the UNFCCC on 14 November 2025.

document_title: Troisième Contribution Déterminée au niveau National (CDN 3.0) de la République du Congo
notes: The Republic of the Congo’s NDC 3.0 recognizes mangroves and coastal wetlands as ecosystems that provide carbon-sequestration services and includes conditional 2026–2035 measures for sustainable management and for restoration and expansion of mangrove areas. These actions primarily serve coastal resilience and biodiversity while also reinforcing the country’s broader role as a net carbon sink. The NDC reports larger national net-removal figures for the overall sink pathway, but those figures combine multiple land and ecosystem measures and should not be attributed solely to mangroves. The mangrove component is therefore recorded as a formal restoration commitment without a stand-alone marine removal quantity or carbon-credit authorization.
source: Government of the Republic of the Congo / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted to the UNFCCC on 12 February 2026; relevant measures extend through 2035.

document_title: Host Party Participation Requirements for Article 6.4 Mechanism — Dominican Republic
notes: The Dominican Republic’s Article 6.4 host-Party participation submission establishes the national framework for screening and approving activities under the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism and identifies mangrove restoration among the priority activity types relevant to national participation. The framework links eligible activities to national climate commitments and sustainable-development benefits and places project approval within the authority of the national Designated National Authority. Subsequent UNFCCC reporting on the country’s Article 6 readiness confirms mangrove restoration as one of the priority project categories alongside other mitigation activities. The submission creates a formal route for considering such projects under Article 6.4, but it does not constitute approval of a specific mangrove project, quantify a blue-carbon removal volume, or automatically authorize transfer of credits.
source: National Council for Climate Change and CDM, Dominican Republic / UNFCCC
status_note: Published by the UNFCCC on 14 July 2024 as the Dominican Republic’s host-Party participation requirements for Article 6.4.

document_title: Seychelles. 2024 National Inventory Document (NID)
notes: The national inventory document formally incorporates seagrass into Seychelles’ greenhouse-gas inventory and reports that this addition materially increases the estimated AFOLU sink relative to the previous biennial-update-report inventory. The document states that seagrass carbon-dioxide removal potential strongly influences the AFOLU results and provides the methodological and reporting basis for recognizing this coastal blue-carbon sink in the national inventory time series. This is an implemented national accounting and transparency step rather than a restoration or carbon-credit project: the document reports removals associated with the inventory and does not authorize new seagrass deployment, issue credits, or establish a project-specific additionality baseline.
source: Government of Seychelles / UNFCCC
status_note: Submitted to the UNFCCC on 15 July 2025 as Seychelles’ 2024 National Inventory Document covering the national greenhouse-gas inventory.

document_title: Nigeria NDC 3.0 — Mangrove Conservation and Ocean/Coastal Ecosystem Removals
notes: Nigeria's NDC 3.0 explicitly includes marine and coastal ecosystems in its mitigation portfolio. In the LULUCF package, the document calls for conservation of 13,000 hectares of mangroves alongside wider forest protection and restoration, and a separate measure calls for enhancing removals through preservation and restoration of oceans and coastal ecosystems, including mangroves, coastal wetlands and marine protected areas. The NDC reports a combined mitigation potential for the broader land-sector action that also contains the mangrove target, so that figure should not be interpreted as a stand-alone quantified marine or mangrove removal estimate. The commitment establishes national mitigation direction and restoration/protection actions, but it does not itself create a blue-carbon crediting methodology, issue credits, establish a project-specific baseline, or authorize a particular marine carbon-removal project.
source: Federal Government of Nigeria / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in 2025; marine and mangrove measures are implementation commitments, while project-level methods, finance and approvals require subsequent instruments.

document_title: 关于印发《温室气体自愿减排项目方法学 造林碳汇（CCER-14-001-V01）》等4项方法学的通知
notes: This Ministry of Ecology and Environment notice formally issued four methodologies for China's national voluntary greenhouse-gas emission-reduction programme, including the mangrove afforestation methodology CCER-14-002-V01. The notice places the methodology into the national CCER framework and standardizes the basis on which eligible projects can be designed, validated, quantified and verified. For Global ONCE purposes, its importance is institutional rather than project-specific: it gives formal effect to a marine blue-carbon accounting and crediting methodology within the national voluntary market. The notice does not itself approve a mangrove project, establish ownership over a project site, issue CCER units, or quantify achieved removals; those outcomes depend on subsequent project registration, monitoring, verification and issuance procedures.
source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China
status_note: Issued in October 2023 and operative within the national CCER methodology framework; no final 2026 replacement of the mangrove V01 methodology was confirmed as of 7 August 2026.

document_title: 温室气体自愿减排项目方法学 红树林营造（CCER—14—002—V01）
notes: CCER-14-002-V01 is the national methodology for greenhouse-gas voluntary emission-reduction projects based on mangrove establishment. It sets eligibility conditions for project areas such as suitable unvegetated tidal flats and retired aquaculture ponds, requires clear land or sea-use rights and project emission-reduction rights, and specifies project-boundary, baseline, additionality, carbon-pool, monitoring, calculation, validation and verification rules. The methodology treats increased mangrove ecosystem carbon stocks as anthropogenic removals and covers biomass and soil-organic-carbon accounting while addressing relevant methane and nitrous-oxide effects. It is a crediting and accounting standard rather than a restoration permit: use of the methodology does not by itself authorize occupation of a tidal area, prove ecological compliance, register a project, or guarantee issuance or sale of CCER units.
source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China
status_note: National CCER mangrove methodology issued in 2023 and still the operative final version as of 7 August 2026, while a revised text remained in draft form.

document_title: 关于公开征求《温室气体自愿减排项目方法学 造林碳汇（修订征求意见稿）》和《温室气体自愿减排项目方法学 红树林营造（修订征求意见稿）》意见的函
notes: This Ministry of Ecology and Environment consultation launched public review of proposed revisions to the national CCER afforestation and mangrove methodologies. For the mangrove pathway, the consultation is evidence of an active rule-updating process covering project design, implementation, validation, emission-reduction accounting and verification within China's voluntary carbon market. The consultation period closed on 7 July 2026. It does not itself amend the operative 2023 methodology, approve projects, issue credits or create a new deployment authorization; unless and until a final revised methodology is formally issued, the consultation package should be treated as a proposed regulatory and methodological update rather than a final rule.
source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China
status_note: Public consultation opened in June 2026 and closed on 7 July 2026; final adoption of the proposed revised mangrove methodology was not confirmed as of 7 August 2026.

document_title: 温室气体自愿减排项目方法学 红树林营造（修订征求意见稿）
notes: This 2026 consultation draft proposes a revised national CCER methodology for mangrove establishment. It retains a project-based carbon-removal framework for suitable unvegetated tidal flats and retired aquaculture ponds, requires clear rights over the relevant sea or land area and the resulting emission reductions, sets a minimum continuous planted area, protects the intertidal character of eligible sites, and requires legal and policy compliance. The draft provides long-term crediting-period rules, spatial boundary and monitoring requirements, biomass and soil-organic-carbon accounting, baseline and project-emission calculations, and treatment of methane and nitrous oxide. Because the document is explicitly a consultation draft, it has no final methodological effect by itself and should not be interpreted as superseding CCER-14-002-V01, granting a restoration permit, registering a project or guaranteeing issuance of credits.
source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China
status_note: Revision draft released for public consultation in June 2026; the consultation had closed, but a final revised methodology was not confirmed as of 7 August 2026.

document_title: 广东省碳普惠交易管理办法
notes: The Guangdong Carbon-Inclusion Trading Management Measures establish the provincial institutional framework for carbon-inclusion reductions and trading. The measures expressly recognize marine carbon sinks, describing relevant resources and activities to include mangroves, seagrass beds, salt marshes, macroalgae and shellfish, and they provide a basis for cross-regional carbon-inclusion cooperation. Their ONCE relevance is therefore the legal and market-governance framework under which marine methodologies and projects can subsequently be developed and recognized. The measures do not themselves quantify marine removals, prescribe a single marine accounting formula, approve any specific blue-carbon project or prove that credits have been issued from every listed ecosystem or aquaculture pathway.
source: Department of Ecology and Environment of Guangdong Province
status_note: Provincial carbon-inclusion trading rules issued in 2022 with a five-year validity period; active as of 7 August 2026 unless replaced or repealed by a later formal instrument.

document_title: 广东省红树林碳普惠方法学（编号2023001-V01）
notes: This Guangdong methodology provides a provincial carbon-inclusion accounting framework for greenhouse-gas reductions generated by mangrove ecological restoration and sink enhancement, with Shenzhen excluded from its geographic scope. It specifies the project-accounting process, eligibility and boundary rules, baseline and project scenarios, monitoring data and verification requirements that can be used to quantify eligible mangrove carbon benefits. The methodology connects mangrove restoration to Guangdong's carbon-inclusion system and therefore provides a subnational route from ecological restoration to quantified and potentially tradable reductions. It is a methodology rather than an individual administrative approval: it does not itself confer site-use rights, authorize ecological works, validate a project, issue reductions or guarantee a transaction.
source: Department of Ecology and Environment of Guangdong Province
status_note: Provincial mangrove carbon-inclusion methodology issued in 2023 and used within Guangdong's carbon-inclusion framework; Shenzhen is outside this methodology's stated geographic scope.

document_title: 深圳市规划和自然资源局关于印发《红树林保护碳汇项目方法学（V1.0）》的通知
notes: Shenzhen's Mangrove Conservation Carbon Sink Project Methodology (V1.0) standardizes the development and implementation of projects that maintain and enhance carbon-storage functions through mangrove conservation. The methodology supports ecological-product value realization by defining project boundaries, data requirements, carbon-sink accounting and monitoring expectations for conservation-oriented mangrove projects. It is especially relevant because it complements restoration-focused methodologies by addressing the carbon value of continued conservation and management. The document is a technical methodology, not a site-specific conservation approval or carbon-credit issuance decision, and it does not by itself establish that a project has generated verified or tradable units.
source: Planning and Natural Resources Bureau of Shenzhen Municipality
status_note: Version 1.0 formally released in February 2026 and active as a Shenzhen technical methodology; project-level validation, approval and any market use remain separate steps.

document_title: 广州市红树林碳普惠方法学（2025年试行版）
notes: Guangzhou's 2025 trial mangrove carbon-inclusion methodology was registered after public solicitation and expert evaluation under the city's voluntary greenhouse-gas reduction framework. It creates a city-level technical basis for defining eligible mangrove projects, calculating reductions or removals, monitoring project performance and supporting verification for carbon-inclusion use. The methodology provides the accounting infrastructure subsequently used by project applications in Nansha and therefore represents an operational local standard rather than a general policy aspiration. Its trial status is important: the document does not itself approve a restoration site, certify a particular quantity of removals, issue GZCER units or guarantee that an application will pass review.
source: Guangzhou Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau
status_note: Trial methodology registered and published in late 2025; active for applicable Guangzhou carbon-inclusion project development unless superseded by a later formal version.

document_title: 南沙湿地红树林营造GZCER项目（一期）减排量申请公示
notes: This Guangzhou public notice concerns the Phase I Nansha Wetland mangrove afforestation GZCER project submitted by Guangzhou Nansha Wetland Tourism Development Co. The application uses Guangzhou's 2025 trial mangrove carbon-inclusion methodology and requests recognition of 554 tCO2e of emission reductions/removals. The notice is valuable as project-level evidence that the municipal methodology has moved from rulemaking into an actual credit application workflow. The figure is an amount requested in an application, not proof of final verification or issuance, and the public notice does not replace any separate ecological restoration, land/sea-use or environmental approvals that may be required for the underlying works. A later Guangzhou Ecology and Environment Bureau announcement confirmed that the 554 tCO2e requested for this afforestation component was subsequently issued; the present record is retained because it documents the distinct application and public-comment stage.
source: Guangzhou Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau
status_note: Application public-notice phase ran from 28 May to 3 June 2026 and is complete; a later Guangzhou official announcement confirmed issuance of the requested 554 tCO2e, which is recorded separately in this update.

document_title: 南沙湿地红树林修复GZCER项目（一期）减排量申请公示
notes: This is a separate Phase I Nansha Wetland GZCER application covering mangrove restoration rather than the afforestation application recorded separately. The applicant submitted the project under Guangzhou's 2025 trial mangrove carbon-inclusion methodology and requested recognition of 697 tCO2e of emission reductions/removals. Because it is an independent project application with its own requested quantity and public notice, it is retained as a separate record rather than treated as a duplicate of the afforestation project. The 697 tCO2e figure remains an application-stage quantity: the notice does not by itself demonstrate final verification, registration, credit issuance, sale, or separate authorization for the ecological works. A later Guangzhou Ecology and Environment Bureau announcement confirmed that the 697 tCO2e requested for this restoration component was subsequently issued; the present record is retained because it documents the distinct application and public-comment stage.
source: Guangzhou Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau
status_note: Application public-notice phase ran from 28 May to 3 June 2026 and is complete; a later Guangzhou official announcement confirmed issuance of the requested 697 tCO2e, which is recorded separately in this update.

document_title: 山东省生态环境厅 山东省海洋局关于发布《山东省海草床碳汇碳普惠方法学》的通知
notes: Shandong's ecology and environment and ocean authorities jointly issued a provincial seagrass-bed carbon-sink carbon-inclusion methodology in 2025. The methodology is designed for voluntary carbon-inclusion seagrass projects in Shandong and provides rules for project design and application, baseline and project scenarios, carbon-sink or emission-reduction calculation, monitoring, reporting and verification. It converts seagrass restoration or management outcomes into a standardized quantification framework that can support provincial carbon-inclusion recognition. The methodology is not an individual project decision and does not by itself establish ownership of a seagrass site, authorize restoration works, certify a specific quantity of removals or prove that credits have been issued or traded.
source: Department of Ecology and Environment of Shandong Province / Shandong Provincial Ocean Bureau
status_note: Provincial methodology issued under document Lu Huan Zi [2025] No. 52 and effective from 29 May 2025; active unless superseded by a later formal version.

document_title: “十五五”“海上福建”建设规划
notes: Fujian's 15th Five-Year Maritime Fujian Construction Plan contains a dedicated marine-carbon-sink policy package. It calls for provincial marine carbon-sink standards, monitoring, accounting and trading methods, development of methodologies for macroalgae-based marine carbon-sink trading, and a more complete marine and fishery carbon-sink accounting and transaction chain. The plan also links marine carbon sinks with judicial mechanisms, finance, pledge registration, funds and insurance, and promotes cross-strait cooperation and potential mutual recognition of standards. These are formal planning tasks and market-development directions, not proof that every proposed methodology, financial product or trading arrangement is already operational; the plan itself does not issue credits or authorize a specific sink-enhancement project.
source: People's Government of Fujian Province
status_note: Provincial 15th Five-Year maritime plan issued in 2026 and active for the 2026–2030 planning period; multiple marine-carbon market and methodology elements remain implementation tasks.

document_title: 福建省“十五五”生态省建设暨生态环境保护规划
notes: Fujian's 15th Five-Year ecological-province and environmental-protection plan includes a marine blue-carbon value-realization workstream. It directs continued development of mechanisms linking marine carbon-sink trading with ecological judicial, procuratorial and administrative enforcement, work on accounting standards for losses of marine ecosystem services, guidance for judicial ecological compensation and replicable cases that use marine carbon sinks in restoration or compensation arrangements. This places blue carbon within a broader environmental-governance and ecological-value framework rather than treating it solely as a voluntary offset product. The plan establishes policy tasks and institutional direction, but it is not itself a project methodology, a credit issuance decision, a court judgment or a quantified marine carbon-removal programme.
source: People's Government of Fujian Province
status_note: Provincial 15th Five-Year environmental plan issued in 2026 and active; the marine blue-carbon legal, accounting and compensation mechanisms described in it require subsequent implementing standards and cases.

document_title: 福建省国民经济和社会发展第十五个五年规划纲要
notes: Fujian's provincial 15th Five-Year development outline explicitly includes marine carbon-sink institutional development. It calls for marine surveys, observation and monitoring, improvement of marine ecosystem-product value realization, and construction of a fuller marine and fishery carbon-sink accounting and trading chain. The outline therefore provides high-level authorization and planning support for the province's later, more detailed blue-carbon standards, methodologies and trading initiatives. It remains a strategic planning instrument: it does not supply a project-level accounting formula, issue a carbon credit, quantify achieved marine removals or authorize a named restoration or aquaculture project.
source: People's Government of Fujian Province
status_note: Provincial development outline for 2026–2030, active as the overarching 15th Five-Year framework; detailed marine carbon accounting and trading rules are to be implemented through follow-on instruments.

document_title: 辽宁省“十五五”海洋经济发展规划
notes: Liaoning's final 15th Five-Year marine-economy plan combines marine-carbon governance with research on offshore geological carbon storage. It calls for marine carbon-sink resource surveys and monitoring, stronger standards research, and exploration of accounting and trading mechanisms, while its marine technology programme also deploys research on carbon capture, liquefied transport, offshore storage, marine injection and integrated equipment. The plan therefore covers both evidence and standards for marine sinks and research-stage marine geological CO2 storage. It does not itself establish a provincial carbon-credit methodology, quantify verified removals, select a storage reservoir, grant an injection permit or authorize commercial-scale offshore CO2 storage.
source: People's Government of Liaoning Province
status_note: Final provincial marine-economy plan issued in 2026 and active for the 2026–2030 period; marine carbon accounting/trading and offshore CO2 storage elements are exploratory or research-stage tasks.

document_title: 辽宁省“十五五”海洋经济发展规划（征求意见稿）
notes: This consultation draft preceded Liaoning's final 15th Five-Year marine-economy plan and exposed the proposed marine-carbon package to public comment. The draft called for surveys and monitoring of marine carbon-sink resources, standards research, exploration of carbon-sink accounting and trading, and research on carbon capture, liquefied transport, offshore storage and marine injection technologies. It is retained separately because it is a distinct formal consultation version and documents the policy-development process. The consultation closed on 12 June 2026 and the draft was subsequently superseded by the final provincial plan, so it has no independent current implementation effect and does not authorize carbon credits or offshore CO2 injection.
source: Liaoning Provincial Development and Reform Commission
